faqs.a: Yes, Sean is the son of well-known apologist Josh McDowell. The two have co-authored several books together, including the updated editions of Evidence That Demands a Verdict.

faqs.q: What is Sean McDowell known for?
faqs.a: McDowell is known for youth-oriented apologetics, his scholarly work on the fate of the apostles, and his charitable public dialogues with atheists, progressive Christians, and LGBTQ advocates. His approach emphasizes both truth and relational grace toward those who disagree.

He teaches Christian apologetics at Talbot School of Theology at Biola University in La Mirada, California. Before joining Biola's faculty he taught high school Bible for many years, and he continues to speak at conferences, churches, and universities worldwide.

name: Bethel McGrew
bio: Bethel McGrew is a freelance writer, educator, and mathematician whose essays on Christianity and culture appear in First Things, The Spectator, WORLD, and other national publications. She maintains the popular Further Up Substack newsletter.

name: Scot McKnight
bio: Scot McKnight is an acclaimed New Testament scholar and historian of early Christianity who has written over eighty books on the historical Jesus, Christian theology, and biblical interpretation. A leading voice in evangelical scholarship, his work has shaped conversations on scripture, the kingdom of God, and ecclesiology.

name: Jason McMartin
bio: Jason McMartin is a professor of theology at Rosemead School of Psychology at Biola University, where he works at the intersection of systematic theology and the behavioral sciences. His writing explores Christian anthropology, sanctification, and the theological dimensions of human flourishing.
affiliation: Biola University / Rosemead School of Psychology

books.title: Being Saved: Dimensions of Human Salvation

name: Nicola A. Menzie
bio: Nicola A. Menzie is a religion journalist and editor known for her insightful coverage of faith, culture, and social issues affecting Black Christians and communities of color. Her work bridges the gap between faith communities and broader cultural conversations, exploring how Christianity intersects with contemporary social movements and cultural trends.
affiliation: Religion News Service, The Christian Century

name: Zlati Meyer
bio: Zlati Meyer is a journalist and newsletter writer at The Wall Street Journal covering business, finance, and economics. She has previously worked at USA Today, the Detroit Free Press, and the Philadelphia Inquirer.

name: J. Gary Millar
bio: J. Gary Millar is the Principal of Queensland Theological College in Brisbane, Australia, and a theologian specializing in Old Testament and biblical theology. A former pastor in Ireland and Northern Ireland, he has particular expertise in Deuteronomy and the theology of prayer.

books.title: Calling on the Name of the Lord

name: Joshua Mitchell
bio: Joshua Mitchell is a professor of political theory at Georgetown University and the author of American Awakening: Identity Politics and Other Afflictions of Our Time. He writes at the intersection of Christian theology and political philosophy, bringing a Tocquevillian lens to contemporary cultural and spiritual debates.

name: Michael Mock
bio: Pastor of Grace Presbyterian Church (PCA) in Fresno, California, and ACBC-certified biblical counselor. Former teacher of Spanish, Greek, and theology; earned D.Min in Biblical Counseling from Reformed Presbyterian Theological Seminary.
education: M.Div from Phoenix Seminary; D.Min in Biblical Counseling from Reformed Presbyterian Theological Seminary

books.title: Hey, Dad, Why Do We...?: Kids Ask the Greatest Questions

name: R. Albert Mohler
bio: R. Albert Mohler Jr. is the president of The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary and one of the most influential evangelical leaders in America. A prolific writer and speaker, he is known for applying biblical theology to contemporary cultural and political issues facing Christians today.

books.title: The Gathering Storm: Secularism, Culture, and the Church
We Cannot Be Silent: Speaking Truth to a Culture Redefining Sex, Marriage, and the Very Meaning of Right and Wrong
The Prayer That Turns the World Upside Down: The Lord's Prayer as a Manifesto for Revolution
Atheism Remix: A Christian Confrontation of Contemporary Atheism
The Disappearance of God: Dangerous Beliefs in the New Spiritual Darkness

known_for: Leading the conservative resurgence at Southern Seminary and providing daily Christian worldview analysis of news and culture through The Briefing.
current_role: President, The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary (since 1993); host of The Briefing podcast

faqs.a: Albert Mohler is Southern Baptist. He has served as the ninth president of The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary in Louisville, Kentucky, the flagship seminary of the Southern Baptist Convention, since 1993, and he remains one of the SBC's most influential voices.

Mohler identifies with Reformed soteriology within Baptist convictions and has been a key figure in the resurgence of Calvinism in the Southern Baptist Convention. Under his leadership, Southern Seminary returned to its founding confession, the Abstract of Principles, which reflects a Reformed Baptist theology.

faqs.q: What is The Briefing by Albert Mohler?
faqs.a: The Briefing is Mohler's daily podcast and program offering analysis of news and events from a Christian worldview. It is one of the most widely followed evangelical commentary programs on culture, politics, and theology.

faqs.q: What is Albert Mohler's view on women pastors?
faqs.a: Mohler is a complementarian who holds that the office and title of pastor are reserved for qualified men. At the 2026 SBC annual meeting he proposed a 'Truth and Unity Amendment' to the SBC constitution intended to clarify the Baptist Faith and Message 2000's position that women should not carry the title of pastor.

faqs.q: What is Albert Mohler known for?
faqs.a: Mohler is known for leading Southern Seminary's return to confessional orthodoxy after becoming its president at age 33, for his prolific cultural commentary, and for his role as a leading intellectual voice of conservative evangelicalism in America.

name: Clarissa Moll
bio: Clarissa Moll is an award-winning writer and podcaster specializing in grief and bereavement ministry. Her writing appears in Christianity Today and The Gospel Coalition, and she is the author of Beyond the Darkness, a guide for living and thriving after loss.

name: Jared Moore
bio: Jared Moore (PhD, Southern Baptist Theological Seminary) is pastor of Cumberland Homesteads Baptist Church in Crossville, Tennessee, and has served in Southern Baptist pastoral ministry since 2000, including a term as second vice president of the Southern Baptist Convention. He is the author of The Lust of the Flesh: Thinking Biblically About "Sexual Orientation," Attraction, and Temptation and coauthor of The Pop Culture Parent, and his writing appears in outlets such as Reformation21 and the Aquila Report.

name: Russell Moore
bio:
Russell D. Moore is an ordained Baptist minister who served as Editor-in-Chief of Christianity Today from 2022-2025, stepping into one of evangelicalism's most prominent editorial platforms. Previously serving as President of the Ethics & Religious Liberty Commission of the Southern Baptist Convention, Moore has established himself as a thoughtful voice on the intersection of faith, politics, and culture, calling evangelicals toward moral courage and gospel-centered witness in the public square.

His book Losing Our Religion: An Altar Call for Evangelical America articulates his concern for evangelical integrity and political faithfulness. Through his writing for Christianity Today, his podcast The Russell Moore Show, and his public speaking, Moore works to strengthen the public witness of the church while challenging Christians to prioritize Jesus Christ and the gospel above political tribalism and cultural warfare.
education: University of Southern Mississippi (BA); New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary (MDiv, PhD)

name: Greg Morse
bio: Greg Morse is a staff writer at Desiring God and a graduate of Bethlehem College and Seminary. A prolific author of essays on biblical theology and Christian living, his writing covers topics including biblical manhood, the new birth, and spiritual formation.

name: Meredith Lee Myers
bio: Web editor for Ligonier Ministries and Tabletalk magazine. Christian publishing professional involved in theological education and ministry resource development.

name: Reem Nadeem
bio: Reem Nadeem is a digital producer and journalist at Pew Research Center and contributing writer to RealClearReligion on religious topics. A former news editor at George Mason University's student paper and journalism intern at CNN and Quartz Media, she discovered her passion for journalism while discovering faith.
education: Graduate, Columbia University/Craig Newmark School of Journalism
known_for: Producing digital publications for Pew Research Center, including reports from its religion research team.
current_role: Associate Digital Producer, Pew Research Center

faqs.a: Reem Nadeem is an associate digital producer at Pew Research Center in Washington, DC. She prepares and produces the center's online reports, including major studies from its religion team such as the Religious Landscape Study and projections on the future of religion in America.

faqs.q: Is Reem Nadeem a religion writer?
faqs.a: She is a digital producer rather than a researcher or opinion writer; her byline appears on Pew Research Center report pages she helps produce. Pew Research Center is a nonpartisan 'fact tank' and does not take policy or theological positions.

faqs.q: What is Pew Research Center's religion research?
faqs.a: Pew Research Center's religion team conducts widely cited surveys on American and global religious life, including the Religious Landscape Study. Its findings on evangelical identity, church attendance, and religious switching are frequently discussed in Christian media.

name: Trillia Newbell
bio:
Trillia Newbell is an author, speaker, and advocate for racial reconciliation in the church whose work challenges evangelicals toward multi-ethnic community and justice. After serving seven years as Director of Community Outreach at the Ethics & Religious Liberty Commission (ERLC) of the Southern Baptist Convention, Newbell transitioned to her current role as Acquisitions Director at Moody Publishers, where she evaluates and acquires manuscripts reflecting evangelical values and priorities.

Her books—including United: Captured by God's Vision for Diversity, A Great Cloud of Witnesses, Sacred Endurance, If God Is For Us, and the children's books Creative God and Colorful Us—address racial justice, identity in Christ, and faithful Christian living. Through her writing for Christianity Today, The Gospel Coalition, and Desiring God, Newbell continues to be an important voice calling evangelicals toward reconciliation, biblical community across racial lines, and justice rooted in the gospel.

name: Cole Newton
bio: Cole Newton is pastor of Western Meadows Baptist Church in Durant, Oklahoma. A self-described Christian, husband, father, writer, and amateur classicist, his passion is proclaiming the good news of Jesus Christ through the study and declaration of Scripture. His sermons and essays on biblical books and Christian living are shared through his church and republished at outlets such as The Aquila Report.

name: Carey Nieuwhof
bio: Carey Nieuwhof is a bestselling leadership author, former attorney, and founding pastor of Connexus Church. His Carey Nieuwhof Leadership Podcast ranks in the top 0.1% of podcasts worldwide and he is a sought-after speaker on Christian leadership and sustainable ministry pace.
education: BA in Law; BA in Theology, University of Toronto

name: O. Alan Noble
bio: O. Alan Noble is an Associate Professor of English at Oklahoma Baptist University and co-founder and editor-in-chief of Christ and Pop Culture. He is the author of several books examining contemporary culture, technology, and what it means to be human in a distracted age.
affiliation: Oklahoma Baptist University, Christ and Pop Culture

name: James Norris
bio: James Norris is a writer and pastor contributing to Reformation21, the online journal of the Alliance of Confessing Evangelicals. He writes on biblical exegesis, Reformed theology, and the church's witness in a post-Christian culture.

name: J.I. Packer
bio:
James Innell Packer (22 July 1926 – 17 July 2020) was an English-born Canadian evangelical theologian and one of the most influential voices in twentieth-century Christianity. Trained in the low-church Anglican and Calvinist traditions, Packer spent the first half of his life in England and the second in Canada, joining the faculty of Regent College in Vancouver in 1979 where he remained through his academic career.

Packer is best known for his spiritual classic Knowing God (1973), which has sold over one million copies in North America alone and remains foundational reading for evangelicals seeking to understand God's character and our relationship with Him. His prolific theological output, ecumenical engagement, and role as a key architect of evangelical identity made him a towering figure recognized by Time magazine in 2005 as one of the 25 most influential evangelicals, though macular degeneration concluded his public ministry in 2016.

name: Kevin Palau
bio:
Kevin Palau is president and leader of the Luis Palau Association, following in the footsteps of his father, international evangelist Luis Palau. Joining the association in 1985 and directing day-to-day operations since the late 1990s, Kevin has evolved the ministry toward a collaborative, relational model of urban evangelism centered on City Gospel Movements rather than large-scale crusades.

Under Kevin's leadership, the Palau Association has shifted toward building relationships with civic leaders and mobilizing thousands of church volunteers to meet community needs, demonstrating the transforming power of gospel-centered service. His vision for collaborative, sustainable evangelism across 150 countries through mentoring, equipping, and networking of evangelists reflects a contemporary evangelical approach to urban mission and church-city engagement that extends beyond his father's model.

name: Jillian Parks
bio: Junior fellow at First Things magazine and journalism student at Hillsdale College. Writes on Christian faith, culture, and technology for leading conservative and religious publications.

name: Paul J. Pastor
bio: Paul J. Pastor is an author, pastor, and spiritual director known for his thoughtful writing on faith, Scripture, and the contemplative Christian life. His work emphasizes the integration of biblical truth with lived experience, offering readers deeper insights into discipleship and spiritual formation. He has contributed to various Christian publications and speaks regularly at conferences and churches.
affiliation: Imago Dei Community; Christianity Today contributor

books.title: The Listening Life: Embracing Contemplative Traditions in an Active World
Heal Us, Emmanuel: Receiving God's Love in the Midst of Suffering
The Renewal of All Things: A Conversation about the New Heaven and the New Earth

name: André Paultre
bio: Haitian reporter based in Port-au-Prince with over a decade of experience covering international news. Freelance journalist for The New York Times, Reuters, and other major outlets.

name: Dan Perkins
bio: Political cartoonist best known by pen name Tom Tomorrow, creating political satire through the syndicated cartoon This Modern World for over 25 years.

books.title: The Great Big Book of Tomorrow

name: John Piper
bio:
John Piper (born January 11, 1946) is the founder and lead teacher of Desiring God, chancellor of Bethlehem College and Seminary, and former senior pastor of Bethlehem Baptist Church (1980-2013), where he served for nearly 33 years. The son of a traveling evangelist, Piper studied English at Wheaton College, earned his BD from Fuller Theological Seminary, and completed a doctorate from the University of Munich, establishing himself as one of the most influential Reformed pastor-theologians of our generation.

Piper's theological vision, grounded in the concept of "Christian hedonism" (the pursuit of joy in God as the highest good), permeates his more than fifty books including the eponymous Desiring God, Don't Waste Your Life, and Providence. Through Desiring God Ministries (founded 1994), his prolific writing, preaching, and digital ministry, Piper has shaped evangelical theology and practice around the supremacy of God in all things for the joy of all peoples through Jesus Christ.
education: Wheaton College (BA); Fuller Seminary (MDiv); University of Munich (DTheol)
denomination: Baptist (Bethlehem Baptist Church is affiliated with Converge, formerly the Baptist General Conference)
known_for: The book Desiring God and the theology of 'Christian hedonism' — that God is most glorified in us when we are most satisfied in him — developed over 33 years pastoring Bethlehem Baptist Church.
current_role: Founder and lead teacher of Desiring God; chancellor of Bethlehem College and Seminary

faqs.a: Yes. Piper is one of the best-known Reformed (Calvinist) Baptist theologians of his generation and a central figure in the 'New Calvinism' resurgence. He affirms the doctrines of grace, including unconditional election and God's sovereignty in salvation.

Piper is a Baptist. He pastored Bethlehem Baptist Church in Minneapolis from 1980 to 2013; the church belongs to Converge (formerly the Baptist General Conference). His ministry through Desiring God is interdenominational.

Christian hedonism is Piper's signature teaching that the pursuit of joy in God is not optional but essential to the Christian life. Its best-known summary is 'God is most glorified in us when we are most satisfied in him,' developed in his 1986 book Desiring God.

faqs.q: What does John Piper do now?
faqs.a: Since leaving the pastorate in 2013, Piper has served full time as founder and lead teacher of desiringGod.org and as chancellor of Bethlehem College and Seminary in Minneapolis. He continues to write, preach at conferences, and answer questions on the Ask Pastor John podcast.

faqs.q: What books has John Piper written?
faqs.a: Piper has authored more than 50 books, including Desiring God, Don't Waste Your Life, Let the Nations Be Glad!, and the 700-page Providence. Nearly all of his sermons, articles, and books are available free at desiringGod.org.

name: Cornelius Plantinga
bio:
Cornelius "Neal" Plantinga Jr. (born February 14, 1946) is a renowned Reformed theologian and member of the Christian Reformed Church who shaped evangelical and Reformed thought through his academic leadership and prolific writing. After earning degrees from Calvin College (BA 1967), Calvin Theological Seminary (BD 1971), and Princeton Theological Seminary (PhD 1982), he served as professor at Calvin University before becoming Dean of the Chapel and then president of Calvin Theological Seminary (2001-2011).

Plantinga is also president emeritus of Calvin Theological Seminary and an emeritus senior research fellow at the Calvin Institute of Christian Worship. His major works include Not the Way It's Supposed to Be (Christianity Today "Book of the Year" 1996) and Engaging God's World (Christianity Today "Book of the Year" 2003), while his more than 230 articles have appeared in Christianity Today, The Christian Century, First Things, and other leading periodicals, establishing him as a thoughtful voice in Reformed evangelical theology.
education: Calvin College (BA); Yale University (MDiv); Yale University (PhD)

books.title: Not the Way It's Supposed to Be
Reading for the Love of God

name: Rob Plummer
bio: Rob Plummer is a New Testament scholar and professor known for his accessible teaching on biblical interpretation and Greek language studies. He is committed to helping Christians engage deeply with Scripture through sound exegetical methods and theological insight.
education: Ph.D. in New Testament, Southern Baptist Theological Seminary

books.title: Paul's Understanding of the Church's Mission

name: Joseph Porter
bio: Pastor of teaching and creative vision at Van City Church in Vancouver, Washington. Former member of punk band Showbread who writes theologically about reclaiming faithfulness within Christian orthodoxy.

books.title: Death to Deconstruction: Reclaiming Faithfulness as an Act of Rebellion
How to Die: Chaos, Mortality, and the Scandal of Christian Discipleship

name: David Powlison
bio:
David Arthur Powlison (December 14, 1949 – June 7, 2019) was a transformative figure in biblical counseling who served as executive director of the Christian Counseling and Educational Foundation (CCEF) from 2014-2019 and taught at Westminster Theological Seminary. A theologian and Christian counselor, Powlison shifted biblical counseling from a polemical stance toward a more compassionate, nuanced approach that integrated theological depth with psychological insight.

As CCEF's senior editor of the Journal of Biblical Counseling and author of numerous groundbreaking works on biblical counseling and the faith-psychology intersection, Powlison helped evangelicals understand how Scripture addresses the deepest human struggles with compassion and wisdom. His legacy continues through CCEF's ministry and his published works, which established him as one of the most influential voices in evangelical counseling. He died on June 7, 2019, following a battle with stage IV pancreatic cancer.
education: University of Pennsylvania (PhD); Westminster Theological Seminary (MDiv)

books.title: Good and Angry: Redeeming Anger, Irritation, Complaining, and Bitterness
Speaking Truth in Love: Counsel in Community

name: Justin N. Poythress
bio: Justin N. Poythress is a Christian author and scholar known for his work in biblical theology and apologetics. He contributes to Christian content curation and theological discussion, helping readers engage deeply with Scripture and faith questions.
known_for: Pastoring and writing on identity, rest, and Christian living for outlets such as The Gospel Coalition.
current_role: Lead Pastor, All Saints Presbyterian Church (Boise/Meridian, Idaho)

faqs.a: Justin N. Poythress is the pastor of All Saints Presbyterian Church, a PCA congregation in the Boise, Idaho area. He earned his MDiv and DMin from Westminster Theological Seminary in Philadelphia and served as an assistant pastor in Indianapolis and Fort Myers before moving to Idaho in 2022.
He is a minister in the Presbyterian Church in America (PCA), a conservative Reformed denomination. His church, All Saints Presbyterian, serves the Boise and Meridian area of Idaho.

faqs.q: What does Justin Poythress write about?
faqs.a: Poythress writes on identity, rest, wonder, and everyday discipleship, with articles at The Gospel Coalition and his own site. He is the author of Who Am I and What Am I Doing with My Life?, which grew out of his doctoral work on identity.

name: Karen Swallow Prior
bio: Karen Swallow Prior is an award-winning author and scholar specializing in literature, ethics, and Christian thought. She writes extensively on faith, culture, and the integration of reading with spiritual formation, and is a fellow at the Trinity Forum.

name: Lynn Pryor
bio: Lynn Pryor is a Christian writer and speaker who contributes to faith-based content and ministry discussions. With a passion for helping believers navigate their spiritual journeys, Pryor offers thoughtful perspectives on Christian living and discipleship.

name: Sherry Qin
bio: Sherry Qin is a Chinese Christian author and speaker who shares insights on faith, cultural identity, and spiritual growth with audiences across Asia and beyond. Her work bridges contemporary Christian thought with practical wisdom for believers navigating modern challenges.

name: Emmett Rensin
bio: Emmett Rensin is a writer and editor known for his thoughtful commentary on culture, politics, and ideas. His work has explored themes relevant to Christian readers seeking to understand contemporary society through a reflective lens.

name: Motoko Rich
bio: Motoko Rich is a New York Times reporter and journalist who has covered education, publishing, and cultural trends for major American publications. While not primarily known as a Christian author, her investigative journalism has explored topics relevant to faith communities, including the role of libraries, literacy, and cultural institutions in American life.
known_for: Leading New York Times coverage of Italy and the Vatican after eight years as Tokyo bureau chief.
current_role: Rome Bureau Chief, The New York Times (since 2025), covering Italy, the Vatican, and Greece

faqs.a: Motoko Rich is a veteran New York Times journalist who became the paper's Rome bureau chief in 2025, leading coverage of Italy, the Vatican, and Greece. She previously served as Tokyo bureau chief from 2016 to 2024 and has covered education, publishing, and the economy.

faqs.q: Is Motoko Rich a Christian author?
faqs.a: No. Rich is a mainstream news journalist, and her public work does not indicate a religious affiliation. Her reporting appears in Christian news digests primarily because her Rome post includes coverage of the Vatican and global religious affairs.

As Rome bureau chief she covers Italian politics and society, the papacy and the Catholic Church, and Greece. Earlier in her career she covered Japan and the Korean peninsula, American education, and the book publishing industry.

name: Joseph Rigney
bio: Joseph Rigney is a writer and pastor committed to helping Christians think deeply about faith, culture, and Scripture. His work explores themes of Christian living, biblical wisdom, and spiritual formation for contemporary believers.

books.title: The Things of Earth: Treasuring God by Enjoying His Gifts
Getting the Gospel Right: The Tie That Binds Evangelicals Together
Pierced for Our Transgressions: Rediscovering the Glory of Penal Substitution

name: Vaneetha Rendall Risner
bio: Vaneetha Rendall Risner is an author and speaker who writes about faith, suffering, and God's grace from her own experience navigating chronic illness and disability. Her transparent and vulnerable approach to Christian living has resonated with readers seeking honest conversations about pain and God's faithfulness. She contributes to various Christian publications and speaks at conferences about finding hope and purpose in difficult circumstances.

books.title: Walking Through Fire: A Memoir of Loss and Redemption
The Scars That Have Shaped Me: How God Meets Us in Suffering
This Was Never the Plan: Walking with God through the Heartache of Divorce

name: Emiliano Rodríguez Mega and César Rodríguez
bio: Emiliano Rodríguez Mega and César Rodríguez are collaborative reporters covering politics and science in Latin America. Emiliano, a Mexico City-based journalist, reports for The New York Times in Spanish, while César collaborates on election coverage and political reporting, including pieces published in The New York Times en Español and Infobae.
affiliation: The New York Times, Infobea, Scientific American, Science magazine

name: Emiliano Rodríguez Mega and Simon Romero
bio: Emiliano Rodríguez Mega and Simon Romero are journalists who have covered major news stories across Latin America and the Caribbean. Their reporting often intersects with themes of faith, culture, and social issues relevant to Christian communities in the region.

name: Tim Rosenberger
bio: Tim Rosenberger is a writer at Mere Orthodoxy who explores the relationship between authentic faith and the cultural forces that can distort it. His essays examine how sentiment, aesthetics, and cultural Christianity can substitute for genuine conviction, calling evangelicals back to a more robust theological and spiritual foundation.

name: Leland Ryken
bio: Professor emeritus of English at Wheaton College who served as the literary stylist for the English Standard Version of the Bible. Author of 60+ books on literature, biblical studies, and Christian scholarship.

books.title: The Word of God in English: Criteria for Excellence in Bible Translation
How to Read the Bible as Literature
A Complete Handbook of Literary Forms in the Bible
The ESV and the English Bible Legacy

name: Mike Sabo
bio: Mike Sabo is a writer and editor at American Reformer, where he covers conservative Christian politics, cultural analysis, and the challenges facing the church in American public life. He writes from a Reformed perspective on nationalism, the common good, and Christian civic engagement.

name: Summer Said
bio: Summer Said is a Senior Middle East Correspondent at The Wall Street Journal covering energy, Saudi Arabia, and regional diplomacy. She previously worked at Reuters.

name: Ken Sande
bio:
Ken Sande is a lawyer, engineer, mediator, and founder of Peacemaker Ministries (now Relational Wisdom 360), who has devoted his career to equipping Christians with biblical tools for conflict resolution and reconciliation. His groundbreaking book The Peacemaker: A Biblical Guide to Resolving Personal Conflict (first published 1991) sold over 500,000 copies in twenty languages and set the standard for evangelical approaches to biblical mediation and dispute resolution.

Sande's four-part peacemaking process—Glorify God, Get the log out of your eye, Gently restore, Go and be reconciled—has shaped evangelical practice in churches, families, and Christian organizations worldwide. Through Peacemaker Ministries, the Institute for Christian Conciliation, and now Relational Wisdom 360, Sande continues to provide training, mediation, and conciliation services while advocating for a distinctly Christian approach to conflict that prioritizes gospel reconciliation over litigation.
education: Montana State University (BS); University of Montana School of Law (JD)

books.title: The Peacemaker: A Biblical Guide to Resolving Personal Conflict

name: Kirsten Sanders
bio: Kirsten Sanders is a writer at Mere Orthodoxy who engages questions of art, culture, and Christian faithfulness. Her essays examine how Christians should navigate contested cultural spaces — including film, visual art, and public discourse — with discernment and conviction.

name: German Saucedo
bio: German Saucedo is a Mexican writer, lawyer, and cultural commentator based in New York. Associate Editor and Podcast Producer at First Things, he writes essays on theology, culture, and philosophy with a focus on faith and contemporary issues.

name: Steven Searcy
bio: Steven Searcy is a fiber-optic telecommunications engineer and poet whose work explores Christian faith and the natural world. His debut poetry collection Below the Brightness was published in 2024.

name: Marshall Segal
role: Writer & Managing Editor at Desiring God
bio:
Marshall Segal serves as President and CEO of Desiring God, guiding the ministry's vision of spreading passion for the supremacy of God in all things for the joy of all peoples. After graduating from Wake Forest University and earning his Master of Divinity from Bethlehem College and Seminary in Minneapolis, Segal became known for his writing and speaking particularly to younger evangelicals, addressing issues of singleness, dating, and faithful living.

His books, including Not Yet Married: The Pursuit of Joy in Singleness & Dating and contributions to anthologies like Designed for Joy and Happily Ever After, demonstrate his gift for making theological truth accessible and attractive to a young evangelical audience. As an elder at Cities Church, Segal combines pastoral concern with intellectual depth, representing a new generation of evangelical leaders committed to both doctrinal rigor and compassionate engagement with contemporary culture.

name: Noah Senthil
bio: Noah Senthil is an adjunct professor of English at Biola University and editorial intern at The Gospel Coalition, focusing on Protestant moral theology and Christian virtue. With degrees from Wheaton College and Talbot School of Theology, he previously served as youth pastor and writes on theology, ethics, and culture.
affiliation: Biola University, The Gospel Coalition, Credo Magazine
role: Adjunct professor, theologian, and editorial contributor
education: BA, Wheaton College; MA, Talbot School of Theology

name: Cameron Shaffer
bio: Senior pastor of Langhorne Presbyterian Church and PhD candidate at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Author of Keeping Kids Christian on discipleship and faith retention.
education: Redeemer Seminary (Master of Divinity); University of Glasgow (Master of Theology); Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (PhD candidate)

books.title: Keeping Kids Christian: Recovering a Biblical Vision for Lifelong Discipleship

name: Mark E. Shaw
bio:
Dr. Mark E. Shaw is founder of The Addiction Connection, a certified biblical counselor since 2002, and pastor of counseling at the Nocatee Campus of First Baptist Church of Jacksonville, Florida. With a Doctor of Ministry in Biblical Counseling (2008), Shaw has pioneered approaches to addiction counseling grounded in Scripture while incorporating contemporary understanding of neurochemistry and psychological dynamics.

His extensive publication record—over 28 resources—includes The Heart of Addiction: A Biblical Perspective, which equips both addicts and counselors with biblical frameworks for understanding and addressing addiction holistically. Through The Addiction Connection, his training of Commissioned Addictions Biblical Counselors (CABC), and his emphasis on compassion alongside biblical truth, Shaw represents biblical counseling's maturation toward greater pastoral sensitivity and practical effectiveness in real-world addiction recovery.

books.title: The Heart of Addiction: A Biblical Perspective

name: Kate Shellnutt
bio: Religion reporter and editor with more than 15 years of experience covering faith news. Former Houston Chronicle religion correspondent whose work spans Washington Post, New York Times, and Vox.
education: Bachelor of Arts in Journalism and Religion from Washington and Lee University

name: Nate Shurden
bio: Nate Shurden is a writer for Ligonier Ministries who contributes expositions of Scripture and meditations on the life of Christ for evangelical readers. His work draws on careful biblical study to illuminate the meaning and significance of the gospel narratives.

name: Matt Smethurst
bio: Matt Smethurst is an editor and writer for The Gospel Coalition, where he helps curate and create Christian content for a global audience. Known for his clear, accessible writing on Scripture, theology, and Christian living, Smethurst has become a trusted voice for evangelical readers seeking to deepen their faith and understanding of God's Word.

books.title: Practically Speaking: A Toolkit for Practically Applying God's Word
Before You Open Your Bible: Nine Ways to Approach Scripture

name: Ryan Smith
bio: Ryan Smith is a writer for American Reformer contributing to evangelical conversations about education, culture, and Christian citizenship. His work engages the classical Christian education movement and broader questions of how Christians should form the next generation.

name: Christy Nockels Smith
bio:
Christy Lynette Nockels (born November 17, 1973) is an accomplished worship artist, singer-songwriter, and worship leader raised in Oklahoma by a pastor father. After meeting her husband Nathan Nockels at a Christian artists' seminar in 1993, she became a worship leader at Metro Bible Study in Houston alongside Louie Giglio's Passion Conference, where they released five albums as the duo Watermark under Rocketown Records.

Following Watermark's retirement in 2006, Christy launched a solo career with sixstepsrecords, releasing albums including Life Light Up and Into the Glorious, while also hosting The Glorious in the Mundane podcast since 2016 and authoring The Life You Long For. As co-owner of Keeper's Branch Records with her husband Nathan, she continues to influence contemporary Christian worship and spirituality through music and digital media.

name: Paul Sonne
bio: Paul Sonne is a journalist and writer who has contributed to major Christian and secular publications, bringing thoughtful analysis to contemporary faith issues. His work often explores the intersection of Christianity, culture, and current events with nuance and depth.
affiliation: The Wall Street Journal, Religion News Service

name: Matthew Spear
bio: Matthew Spear is a writer for Relevant Magazine whose work explores the spiritual disciplines, Christian formation, and the life of faith in everyday culture. He writes with pastoral attentiveness to the challenges of faithful living in a distracted age.

name: Andrew Spencer
bio: PhD-holding theologian and associate editor for books at The Gospel Coalition. Elder at CrossPointe Church with expertise in biblical theology and creation care.

books.title: Hope for God's Creation: Stewardship in an Age of Futility

name: R.C. Sproul
bio:
Robert Charles Sproul (1939-2017) was an American Reformed theologian, Christian apologist, and Presbyterian pastor who profoundly shaped evangelical theology and practice. Founder and first chairman of Ligonier Ministries, Sproul established a platform for expository teaching and theological education that reached millions through his daily Renewing Your Mind radio broadcast and extensive published work.

Described as "the greatest and most influential proponent of the recovery of Reformed theology in the last century," Sproul authored more than one hundred books including The Holiness of God, which exemplifies his gift for making profound theological concepts accessible to popular audiences. His death on December 14, 2017, at age 78, marked the end of a legacy that continues to influence evangelical understandings of God's sovereignty, holiness, and redemptive work.
education: Westminster College (BA); Free University of Amsterdam (postgraduate)

books.title: Essential Truths of the Christian Faith

known_for: The Holiness of God, the Renewing Your Mind broadcast, and leading the twentieth-century recovery of Reformed theology for lay audiences through Ligonier Ministries.
current_role: Deceased (died December 14, 2017). Was founder and chairman of Ligonier Ministries and co-pastor of Saint Andrew's Chapel, Sanford, Florida

faqs.a: R.C. Sproul died on December 14, 2017, at age 78, from complications of emphysema. Ligonier Ministries, which he founded in 1971 as the Ligonier Valley Study Center in western Pennsylvania, continues his teaching ministry today.

Sproul was a Presbyterian. Originally ordained in the mainline United Presbyterian Church, he transferred his credentials to the conservative Presbyterian Church in America (PCA) and served as co-pastor of Saint Andrew's Chapel in Sanford, Florida, from 1997 until his death.

Yes. Sproul was arguably the most influential popularizer of Reformed (Calvinist) theology in the last century, teaching doctrines like God's sovereignty, predestination, and justification by faith alone to mass audiences. His book Chosen by God remains a standard introduction to Reformed soteriology.

faqs.q: What is R.C. Sproul best known for?
faqs.a: Sproul is best known for The Holiness of God (1985), his daily radio program Renewing Your Mind, and founding Ligonier Ministries. He authored more than one hundred books and served as general editor of the Reformation Study Bible.

name: Daniel Stegeman
bio: Daniel Stegeman (DMin, Gordon-Conwell) has pastored churches in Ohio, New York, and Pennsylvania and serves as director of pastoral care with Fruitful Vine Ministry. He is the author of 'Help! I Want to Be a Loving Husband' (Shepherd Press), blogs at pastoral-theology.com, and contributes to The Gospel Coalition.

books.title: Help! I Want to Be a Loving Husband

name: Alex Stevens
bio: Marine Corps veteran and mental health therapist who writes fantasy fiction blending Christian themes with worldbuilding. Published author of Sympathy for the Devil and Stairway to Heaven.
education: University of Nevada, Las Vegas (BA Interdisciplinary Studies); Walden University (Master of Social Work)

name: Daniel Stevens
bio: Daniel Stevens is associate professor of New Testament interpretation at Boyce College, the undergraduate school of The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary, where he has taught Greek and New Testament since 2022. He is the author of Songs of the Son: Reading the Psalms with the Epistle to the Hebrews and The Theme of Promise in the Epistle to the Hebrews, and he is a regular guest teacher on the Daily Dose of Greek.

books.title: Songs of the Son: Reading the Psalms with the Hebrews
The Theme of Promise in the Epistle to the Hebrews

name: Jordan Stone
bio: Senior pastor at Redeemer Presbyterian Church in McKinney, Texas, and assistant professor of pastoral theology at Reformed Theological Seminary Dallas. Scholar and author specializing in the spirituality of Robert Murray M'Cheyne.
affiliation: Redeemer Presbyterian Church; Reformed Theological Seminary
role: Senior Pastor; Assistant Professor of Pastoral Theology
education: PhD, The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary; Th.M., The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary; M.A.R., Reformed Theological Seminary; BA, Texas Tech University

books.title: A Holy Minister: The Life and Spiritual Legacy of Robert Murray M'Cheyne
Love to Christ: The Piety of Robert Murray M'Cheyne
A Communion of Love: The Christ-Centered Spirituality of Robert Murray M'Cheyne

name: John Stott
bio:
John Robert Walmsley Stott (1921-2011) was a towering figure in world evangelicalism and one of the twentieth century's most significant Christian leaders. The longtime rector of All Souls Church, Langham Place in London (1950-1975), Stott became a global evangelical statesman, pioneering the Lausanne Movement and founding Langham Partnership International to train pastors and writers in the developing world.

Named by Time magazine in 2005 as one of the 100 most influential people in the world, Stott authored more than 50 books and became known for his winsome, biblically grounded approach to faith that bridged evangelical and mainline sensibilities. His commitment to Scripture, social engagement, and careful theological reasoning made him a model of evangelical intellectual seriousness. He died on July 27, 2011, at age 90, leaving a legacy that continues to shape evangelical witness and scholarship globally.

name: Walter Strickland
bio:
Walter R. Strickland II is Professor of Systematic and Contextual Theology at Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary and an important voice in African American evangelical theology. Elected first vice president of the Southern Baptist Convention in 2017, Strickland brings scholarly rigor and prophetic concern to conversations about race, theology, and justice within evangelicalism.

His groundbreaking two-volume work Swing Low: A History of Black Christianity in the United States provides a theological-intellectual history highlighting how theology has formed and motivated Black Christianity across centuries. Framing his analysis around five theological anchors—"a big God," Jesus as essential, conversion, sanctification, and walking in the Spirit—Strickland recovers the deep theological traditions of Black churches while addressing systemic injustices. His scholarship and leadership challenge evangelicals to acknowledge and learn from Black theological traditions.

name: Jay Stringer
bio:
Jay Stringer is a licensed mental health counselor, trauma-informed therapist, and author of the award-winning book Unwanted: How Sexual Brokenness Reveals Our Way to Healing. For over 15 years, he has helped thousands decode the narratives behind anxiety, self-sabotage, and disconnection, drawing on original research from 3,800+ participants to explore how trauma and unmet longings shape unwanted sexual behavior and choices.

Holding an MA in Counseling Psychology and MDiv from The Seattle School of Theology & Psychology, Stringer integrates trauma-informed care, adult development theory, and narrative work into his approach. With over 100,000 copies sold, Unwanted has become a trusted resource for evangelicals and beyond seeking freedom from sexual brokenness, while his forthcoming book Desire: The Longings Inside Us and the New Science of How We Love, Heal, and Grow (Random House, 2026) continues his exploration of human longing and healing.
education: The Seattle School of Theology & Psychology (MDiv, MA Counseling Psychology)

books.title: Unwanted: How Sexual Brokenness Reveals Our Way to Healing

name: Margaret Sullivan
bio: Margaret Sullivan is a media columnist and journalist known for her sharp cultural commentary and analysis of faith-related topics in contemporary media. Her work examines how Christian values intersect with journalism, public discourse, and institutional accountability.

name: A. J. Swoboda
bio: Dr. A. J. Swoboda is an associate professor of Bible and theology at Bushnell University and co-host of the Slow Theology podcast. He specializes in Christian formation, spiritual disciplines, and contemporary theological issues, with a particular focus on practices like sabbath and doubt in the modern church.

name: William Tate
bio: William Tate is a writer at Mere Orthodoxy contributing essays on literature, culture, and the Christian intellectual tradition. He writes with an eye toward recovering the richness of Christian humanist thought for evangelical readers navigating questions of art, education, and the good life.

name: John Taylor
bio: John Taylor is a writer contributing to Relevant Magazine on topics of faith, culture, and Christian living. He writes for a younger evangelical audience navigating questions of spirituality, church, and life in a post-Christian culture.

name: Abigail Thompson
bio: Christian writer and author who writes about biblical themes, women's ministry, and faith. Known for award-winning fiction blending biblical truth with engaging storytelling.

name: Curt Thompson
bio:
Dr. Curt Thompson is a psychiatrist in private practice in Falls Church, Virginia, who bridges the intersection of neuroscience, theology, and spiritual formation in innovative ways. Raised in an evangelical Quaker community in Ohio, Thompson has built his career on exploring how interpersonal neurobiology (IPNB) connects with Christian anthropology, helping individuals understand their deep need to be known and to know God at the neural level.

Through the Being Known Podcast (co-hosted with Pepper Sweeney), his writing, speaking, and his therapeutic work, Thompson has become an influential voice helping evangelicals integrate modern neuroscience with Christian spiritual practices. His approach emphasizes how meaningful relationships and spiritual formation actually rewire our brains toward wholeness, offering evangelicals a compelling framework for understanding human psychology and healing through the lens of the gospel.
education: Wright State University School of Medicine (MD)

name: Jemar Tisby
bio: Jemar Tisby is a New York Times bestselling historian, author, and speaker focusing on race, religion, and social movements. A professor at Simmons College of Kentucky, he is known for his scholarship on the American church's relationship with racism and justice.

name: Paul David Tripp
bio:
Paul David Tripp (born November 12, 1950) is an American pastor, author, biblical counselor, and international conference speaker who has dedicated his career to connecting the transforming power of Jesus Christ to everyday life. After receiving his Master of Divinity from the Reformed Episcopal Seminary and Doctor of Ministry in Biblical Counseling from Westminster Theological Seminary, Tripp served as faculty at the Christian Counseling and Educational Foundation (CCEF) for many years.

Founder and president of Paul Tripp Ministries, a nonprofit organization producing gospel-centered resources, Tripp has authored more than 30 books including "What Did You Expect?: Redeeming the Realities of Marriage," "New Morning Mercies: A Daily Gospel Devotional," and "Do You Believe?: 12 Historic Doctrines to Change Your Everyday Life." His work exemplifies biblical counseling's maturation, combining theological depth with psychological insight to help Christians understand how grace transforms the ordinary struggles of daily life.
denomination: Presbyterian (longtime association with Tenth Presbyterian Church, Philadelphia)
known_for: Gospel-centered books on marriage, parenting, and everyday sanctification, including New Morning Mercies and What Did You Expect?, drawn from decades in the biblical counseling movement.
current_role: Founder and president of Paul Tripp Ministries

faqs.q: What denomination is Paul David Tripp?
faqs.a: Paul David Tripp comes from a Reformed and Presbyterian background. He trained at Reformed Episcopal Seminary and Westminster Theological Seminary and served for years on the pastoral staff of Tenth Presbyterian Church in Philadelphia. Today he ministers interdenominationally through Paul Tripp Ministries.

faqs.q: What is Paul David Tripp known for?
faqs.a: Tripp is best known as a biblical counselor and author of more than 30 books, including the bestselling daily devotional New Morning Mercies and the marriage book What Did You Expect?. His signature theme is connecting the transforming grace of Jesus Christ to the ordinary struggles of everyday life.

faqs.q: What is biblical counseling, and what is Tripp's role in it?
faqs.a: Biblical counseling is a movement that treats Scripture as the primary lens for understanding and addressing personal and relational problems. Tripp served on the faculty of the Christian Counseling and Educational Foundation (CCEF) for many years and is one of the movement's most widely read popularizers.

faqs.q: Is Paul David Tripp still in ministry?
faqs.a: Yes. Tripp, born in 1950, continues to lead Paul Tripp Ministries, a nonprofit that produces gospel-centered books, devotionals, and conference teaching for individuals, families, and pastors.

name: Kyle Tucker
bio: Kyle Tucker (MDiv, The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary) is a pastor at City on a Hill Church in the Brighton neighborhood of Boston, where he oversees community groups, leadership development, and systems of care and discipleship. Currently pursuing a doctor of ministry at Wheaton College, he writes on apologetics and Scripture for The Gospel Coalition.

name: Ligonier Updates
bio: Ligonier Updates is the official news and content platform of Ligonier Ministries, dedicated to equipping Christians with Reformed theological resources and biblical teaching. Through articles, updates, and curated content, Ligonier Updates serves the global church by promoting the study of Scripture and classical Christian doctrine.

name: Ian J. Vaillancourt
bio: Ian J. Vaillancourt is a biblical scholar and writer for The Gospel Coalition who specializes in Old Testament wisdom literature. His work explores how the Psalms, Proverbs, and the wisdom books of Scripture speak to the full range of human experience and point readers toward Christ.

name: Gene Edward Veith
bio: Gene Edward Veith Jr. is professor of literature at Patrick Henry College and a contributing editor at World Magazine and Ligonier Ministries. One of evangelical Christianity's leading voices on culture and the arts, he is the author of numerous books including Postmodern Times, State of the Arts, and God at Work: Your Christian Vocation in All of Life. He writes from a confessional Lutheran perspective on everything from classical education to contemporary media.
affiliation: Patrick Henry College / World Magazine / Ligonier Ministries
education: PhD in English, University of Kansas

name: Rob Ventura
bio: Rob Ventura (MDiv, Reformed Baptist Seminary) is one of the pastors of Grace Community Baptist Church in North Providence, Rhode Island. A former Hip Hop promoter turned preacher, he brings unconventional background to evangelical ministry and has contributed to Reformation 21 magazine and biblical scholarship works.
education: Master of Divinity, Reformed Baptist Seminary

books.title: Equipped to Evangelize: A Biblical Foundation
Expository Outlines and Observations on Romans

name: Guy Prentiss Waters
bio: Guy Prentiss Waters is a Reformed theologian and pastor known for his accessible yet scholarly writings on biblical theology and Christian living. He has served in pastoral ministry and has been a prolific author and teacher, helping evangelical Christians understand the depth of Scripture through a Reformed lens.
affiliation: Ligonier Ministries, Reformed Presbyterian Church of North America

books.title: How Jesus Fulfills the Old Testament
Justification and the New Perspective on Paul

name: Trevin Wax
bio:
Trevin Wax is Vice President of Resources and Marketing at the North American Mission Board and a visiting professor at Cedarville University, bringing missional and cultural expertise to evangelical leadership. A former missionary to Romania with extensive teaching experience at Wheaton College and lectures at Oxford University, Wax brings international and academic perspective to contemporary evangelical conversation.

As a regular columnist at The Gospel Coalition and contributor to The Washington Post, World magazine, and Christianity Today, Wax addresses the intersection of faith, culture, and politics from a gospel-centered perspective. He is a founding editor of The Gospel Project, served as publisher of the Christian Standard Bible, and is a fellow for The Keller Center for Cultural Apologetics, making him an important voice helping evangelicals think carefully about cultural engagement and Christian witness in a pluralistic age.
education: Wheaton College (BA); Southern Baptist Theological Seminary (MDiv)

name: Ed Welch
bio:
Ed Welch is a faculty member and counselor at the Christian Counseling and Educational Foundation (CCEF) where he has served since 1981, bringing three decades of counseling experience to his teaching and writing. With a doctor of philosophy in counseling (neuropsychology) from the University of Utah and a master of divinity from Biblical Theological Seminary, Welch holds licensure as a psychologist and maintains deep roots in local church ministry.

As a council member of the Biblical Counseling Coalition, Welch has authored numerous influential books addressing addiction, depression, anxiety, shame, and anger from a biblical perspective, including When People Are Big and God Is Small, Addictions: A Banquet in the Grave, and Shame Interrupted. His approach represents biblical counseling's evolution toward greater pastoral sensitivity and psychological sophistication, helping evangelicals see how Scripture speaks to complex human struggles with both truth and compassion.
education: University of Utah (PhD, Counseling Psychology); Biblical Theological Seminary (MDiv)

books.title: Addictions: A Banquet in the Grave
When People Are Big and God Is Small

name: Alexandra Wexler
bio: Alexandra Wexler is an Africa correspondent for The Wall Street Journal, based in Johannesburg, covering companies, markets, and trends across sub-Saharan Africa, from mining and banking to retail. She holds a master's in journalism from Stanford University and previously covered commodities and futures markets for the Journal in New York.

name: Laura Wifler
bio: Laura Wifler is a bestselling author of children's and adult books exploring the intersection of faith and everyday life. Co-founder of Risen Motherhood and founder of The KidLit Lab, she is a beloved voice for Christian mothers and aspiring writers.

books.title: Any Time, Any Place, Any Prayer

name: Jen Wilkin
bio:
Jen Wilkin is a Bible teacher and author from Dallas, Texas, who has organized and led Bible studies for women in home, church, and parachurch contexts across the country and internationally. Her book Women of the Word: How to Study the Bible with Both Our Hearts and Minds (2014) has become widely used in evangelical churches as a foundational text for teaching women inductive Bible study methods and hermeneutical skills.

Now serving on staff with The Village Church Institute where she directs adult classes across their five campuses, Wilkin continues to influence evangelical women's ministry through her teaching, writing, and speaking. Her passion is to help believers become articulate, committed followers of Jesus with clear understanding of biblical truth grounded in careful Scripture study, making her a significant voice shaping how evangelicals approach the Bible.
education: Baylor University (MA, Biblical Studies); Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary

name: Dallas Willard
bio:
Dallas Albert Willard (September 4, 1935 – May 8, 2013) was a prolific Christian philosopher and spiritual formation pioneer who taught in USC Dornsife's School of Philosophy for 47 years (1965-2013). A scholar of phenomenology and medieval philosophy with deep expertise in Edmund Husserl, Willard became one of evangelicalism's most important voices on Christian discipleship and spiritual transformation through his writing and ministry with the Renovare movement.

Willard's signature works—The Divine Conspiracy (Christianity Today "Book of the Year" 1999) and Renovation of the Heart (Christianity Today Book Award 2003)—fundamentally reshaped evangelical thinking about spiritual formation and the ordinary life of discipleship. His death on May 8, 2013, after a brief battle with cancer, marked the end of a legacy that continues to influence how evangelicals understand the transformation of the soul and the kingdom of God in everyday life.
education: University of Oklahoma (BA); Southern Baptist Seminary (BD); University of Wisconsin (MA, PhD)

name: Daniel K. Williams
bio: Daniel K. Williams is a historian at Ashland University specializing in American religion and politics, the Christian Right, and the pro-life movement. His scholarly works examine the intersection of faith and American political history.

name: Nadya Williams
bio: Nadya Williams is a classicist and historian who left academia to write about ancient Christianity and classical literature from a Christian perspective. Books Editor at Mere Orthodoxy, she is the author of Cultural Christians in the Early Church and other works on the ancient world.

books.title: Cultural Christians in the Early Church
Mothers, Children, and the Body Politic

name: Kyle Worley
bio: Kyle Worley is the lead pastor of Mosaic Church in Richardson, Texas, and co-host of the Knowing Faith podcast with J. T. English and Jen Wilkin. An author and teacher with over twenty years in ministry, he writes on union with Christ and the theological formation of local churches.

name: Roland Barnes
bio: Rev. Roland S. Barnes is a PCA minister who served as the organizing and senior pastor of Trinity Presbyterian Church in Statesboro, Georgia, from 1981 until his retirement in 2023. Over more than four decades he led the congregation's growth and its overseas mission work, and he is now pastor emeritus and an honorably retired minister.

name: Paul Christopher
bio: Paul Christopher is a Christian author and thought leader who writes on faith, culture, and spiritual discipleship. His work encourages believers to engage thoughtfully with contemporary issues through a biblical worldview.

name: Hayden Nesbit
bio: Hayden Nesbit is an assistant pastor at Walnut Creek Presbyterian Church (PCA) and a writer whose work appears at Desiring God and Mere Orthodoxy. His writing explores Scripture, spiritual formation, and living faithfully in a digital age.

name: Samuel D. James
bio: Samuel D. James is a writer and editor known for thoughtful commentary on faith, culture, and technology from a Christian perspective. He has contributed to leading evangelical publications and is recognized for helping Christians think biblically about contemporary cultural issues.

name: O. Alan Noble
bio: O. Alan Noble is a writer and editor focused on Christian engagement with culture, technology, and faith. He has written extensively on how Christians can think critically about media, entertainment, and digital life while remaining grounded in biblical wisdom. Noble's work encourages believers to develop a thoughtful, redemptive perspective on contemporary culture.
education: MA in English Literature, University of Nebraska

books.title: Disruptive Witness: Speaking Truth in a Fragmented World
You Are Not Your Own: Belonging to God in an Inhuman World
Conscience: Three Generations of Abortion, Family, and Tradition

name: Aaron M. Renn
bio: Aaron M. Renn is a writer and analyst focused on Christianity's cultural and institutional place in American public life. He explores how Christian faith engages with broader cultural trends, offering thoughtful commentary on secularization, religious liberty, and the future of Christian witness in contemporary society.

books.title: The Masculinity Crisis: Why the Modern Male is Struggling, Why It Matters, and What to Do About It

name: Collin Hansen
bio: Collin Hansen is a respected evangelical author and editor known for his work on church history, theology, and contemporary Christian issues. As editorial director for The Gospel Coalition, he has helped shape conversations among Reformed and evangelical leaders worldwide. His writing combines scholarly insight with pastoral concern for the local church.

books.title: Young, Restless, Reformed: A Journalist's Journey with the New Calvinism
Blind Spots: Becoming a Courageous, Compassionate, and Commissioned Church
That's Not What I Meant: Finding Grace When Words Backfire
Redeeming Sex: Naked Conversations About Sexuality and Following Jesus
Our Secular Age: Ten Years of Reading and Applying Charles Taylor

name: Kathy Keller
bio: Kathy Keller is a writer, speaker, and co-founder of Redeemer City to City, an organization dedicated to planting and strengthening churches in global cities. She has written extensively on faith, marriage, and Christian living, drawing from her decades of experience in ministry alongside her husband, Timothy Keller. Her work encourages Christians to live out their faith authentically in contemporary culture.
affiliation: Redeemer City to City, The Gospel Coalition

books.title: The Meaning of Marriage: Facing the Complexities of Commitment with the Wisdom of God
Jesus the King: Understanding the Life and Death of the Son of God
God's Loving Plan: Experiencing the Gospel in Work, Relationships, and Even Loss

name: Damien Cave
bio: Damien Cave is an accomplished journalist and correspondent known for his investigative reporting and in-depth coverage of complex social and political issues. His work has appeared in major national publications where he has brought thoughtful analysis and human-centered storytelling to contemporary challenges.

name: Chris Martin
bio: Chris Martin is a worship leader, songwriter, and pastor known for his contributions to contemporary Christian music and spiritual leadership. He has dedicated his ministry to helping believers engage with God through authentic worship and biblical teaching.

name: Zia ur-Rehman and Asim Hafeez
bio: Zia ur-Rehman and Asim Hafeez are Pakistani journalists and documentarians known for their investigative work covering conflict, terrorism, and security issues in South Asia. While not primarily Christian content creators, their reporting has provided important context on religious extremism and persecution for international audiences seeking to understand global challenges.

name: J. A. Medders
bio: J. A. Medders is a writer and pastor dedicated to helping Christians understand and live out their faith with greater depth and authenticity. His work focuses on biblical discipleship, spiritual growth, and the practical application of Scripture to everyday life.
affiliation: Send Network (NAMB); Midwestern Baptist Theological Seminary (visiting professor)

books.title: Sola Scriptura: What the Bible Says About Itself
The Expository Preacher: How to Preach the Whole Bible

known_for: Writing Humble Calvinism and serving Southern Baptist church planting through Send Network's theological training.
current_role: Director of Theology and Content, Send Network (North American Mission Board, SBC)

faqs.a: Jeff (J.A.) Medders is the Director of Theology and Content for Send Network, the church-planting arm of the Southern Baptist Convention's North American Mission Board. He previously served as lead pastor of Redeemer Church in Tomball, Texas, and holds a PhD from The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary.

Yes, though he is best known for warning fellow Calvinists against pride. His book Humble Calvinism argues that genuinely grasping the doctrines of grace should produce humility and love rather than the combative spirit sometimes associated with the 'young, restless, and Reformed' movement.

faqs.q: What is J.A. Medders known for?
faqs.a: Medders is known for Humble Calvinism, his work on Charles Spurgeon connected to the Spurgeon Library at Midwestern Baptist Theological Seminary, and books on prayer, discipleship, and evangelism such as The Soul-Winning Church.

name: Wyatt Graham
bio: Wyatt Graham (PhD, The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary) is executive director of The Davenant Institute and editor in chief of The Gospel Coalition Canada, having previously served as TGC Canada's executive director. His scholarship focuses on biblical theology, patristics, and moral formation, and he is the author of 'The Promised Davidic King.'

name: Stephen Kalin
bio: Stephen Kalin is a researcher and analyst specializing in Middle Eastern politics and religious affairs. His work examines the intersection of faith, geopolitics, and international relations, with particular focus on how religious identity shapes political outcomes in the region.

name: Joseph Sherrard
bio: Joseph "Joey" Sherrard (PhD, University of St Andrews) is associate pastor of discipleship at Signal Mountain Presbyterian Church near Chattanooga, Tennessee, and a fellow with the Center for Pastor Theologians. He is the author of The Augustinian Pastor: Deep Wisdom for Modern Ministry and T. F. Torrance as Missional Theologian, and his writing appears in outlets including The Gospel Coalition and Mere Orthodoxy.

name: R.C. Sproul
bio: R.C. Sproul was a highly influential Reformed theologian, pastor, and prolific author who dedicated his life to making complex theological concepts accessible to everyday Christians. He founded Ligonier Ministries and was known for his passionate teaching on the holiness of God, biblical Reformed theology, and the sovereignty of God. Through his books, radio program, and teaching ministry, Sproul shaped the spiritual lives of countless believers worldwide.
education: M.Div., Westminster Theological Seminary; Ph.D., Free University of Amsterdam

books.title: Essential Truths of the Christian Faith

name: Joshua Heavin
bio: Joshua Heavin (PhD, University of Aberdeen) is a curate and deacon in the Anglican tradition in the Dallas area and an adjunct professor in the School of Christian Thought at Houston Christian University as well as at West Texas A&M University. He serves as book reviews editor for Pro Ecclesia, and his essays on Pauline theology, the church, and contemporary culture appear regularly in Mere Orthodoxy and other publications.

name: Joshua Budimlic
bio: Joshua Budimlic is a Christian teacher and writer who brings together his interests in theology, education, and literature to serve the next generation. His articles on the Christian life and sanctification have appeared at The Gospel Coalition Canada and The Aquila Report, and he writes at joshuabudimlic.com.

name: Taigen Joos
bio: Taigen Joos is a Christian writer and contemplative theologian exploring the intersection of Buddhist-Christian dialogue and contemplative spirituality. His work engages readers in deepening their faith through meditative practices and interfaith understanding rooted in Christian tradition.

name: Lauren Groves
bio: Lauren Groves is a Christian author and speaker known for her work in faith-based content creation and spiritual encouragement. She has built a platform focused on helping believers deepen their relationship with God through authentic and practical Christian living.

name: Allen D. Hertzke
bio: Allen D. Hertzke is a distinguished political scientist and scholar who has written extensively on the intersection of religion and politics in American public life. His research examines how faith communities engage with political institutions and shape policy on issues ranging from religious freedom to human rights advocacy.

books.title: Representing God in Washington: Religious Interest Groups and the American Political System
Freeing God's Children: The Unlikelihood of Religious Politics and the Unlikely Alliances for Religious Freedom
Faith in the Halls of Power: How Evangelicals Joined the American Elite

name: Chad Van Dixhoorn
bio: Chad Van Dixhoorn is a Reformed theologian and scholar known for his extensive work on the Westminster Standards and historical theology. He serves as a professor and has dedicated much of his career to making classical Reformed theology accessible to contemporary Christians.

books.title: Confessing the Faith: A Reader's Guide to the Westminster Confession of Faith
The Covenant Renewed: A Reader's Guide to the Shorter Catechism
The Living Christ: An Exposition of Hebrews

name: Anne Kerhoulas
bio: Anne Kerhoulas is a Christian author and speaker who writes about faith, family, and spiritual growth. Her work encourages believers to deepen their relationship with God through practical wisdom and scriptural insight.

name: Emily Belz
bio: Emily Belz is a journalist and editor known for her reporting on religious freedom, international affairs, and the intersection of faith and public life. She has contributed extensively to evangelical publications and brings a thoughtful, nuanced perspective to contemporary issues facing the Christian community.

name: Uwa Ede-Osifo
bio: Uwa Ede-Osifo is a Nigerian Christian writer and communicator passionate about faith, culture, and discipleship. Through his writing and speaking, he engages thoughtfully with contemporary issues from a biblical worldview, seeking to help believers navigate their faith in the modern world.

name: David M. Halbfinger
bio: David M. Halbfinger is a veteran journalist and media analyst who has served as executive editor and chief political correspondent for major American news organizations. With decades of experience covering politics, culture, and faith-related issues, he brings thoughtful analysis to contemporary issues of interest to Christian readers and faith communities.
known_for: Serving as New York Times politics editor after posts including Jerusalem bureau chief.
current_role: Politics Editor, The New York Times

faqs.a: David M. Halbfinger is the politics editor of The New York Times. He previously served as the paper's Jerusalem bureau chief, deputy national editor, and 2016 presidential campaign editor, and reported on politics, the South, and the movie business.

faqs.q: Is David Halbfinger a Christian author?
faqs.a: No. Halbfinger is a mainstream news editor, and his public work does not indicate an evangelical affiliation. His byline appears in Christian news digests mainly through his earlier coverage of Israel as Jerusalem bureau chief.

faqs.q: What does David Halbfinger do at The New York Times?
faqs.a: As politics editor he oversees the paper's political coverage. During his years in Jerusalem he led coverage of Israel and the Palestinian territories, a beat closely followed by many Christian readers.

name: Natalie Andrews
bio: Natalie Andrews is a White House reporter for The Wall Street Journal in Washington. She joined the Journal in 2014 and spent years covering Congress, House and Senate leadership, and national politics, reporting on two presidential impeachments and multiple election cycles before moving to the White House beat. She previously worked for KSL News in Salt Lake City.

name: Tyler Bauer
bio: Dr. Tyler Bauer is a professor of humanities and dean of students at Christ College and a PhD student at Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary. A classical educator, philosopher, and writer, he works to make Christian philosophy and theology accessible while defending historic orthodoxy, and contributes to The Gospel Coalition.

name: Robert VanDoodewaard
bio: Robert VanDoodewaard is a pastor and Christian author known for his work on biblical theology and historical Christian thought. He has written extensively on topics including idolatry, the sufficiency of Scripture, and the practical application of Reformed theology to contemporary Christian life.

books.title: The Headcovering: A Study of the Biblical Basis and Application of Headcovering
Idols of the Heart: Learning to Long for God Alone
What Does the Bible Really Teach about Homosexuality

name: Gray Ewing
bio: Gray Ewing (MDiv, Covenant Theological Seminary) is a church-planting pastor in the Phoenix, Arizona area and a regular contributor to Mere Orthodoxy. He writes on Christianity, culture, and the Christian life, collecting and sharing resources he finds most helpful for discipleship.

name: A PCA Ruling Elder
bio: A PCA Ruling Elder serves as a lay leader in the Presbyterian Church in America, devoted to faithful church governance and spiritual oversight. Ruling Elders work alongside pastoral staff to shepherd their congregations with biblical wisdom and pastoral care.

name: Haley Byrd Wilt
bio: Haley Byrd Wilt is a writer and editor known for her work in Christian publishing and content creation. She has contributed to various Christian publications and platforms, bringing thoughtful perspectives on faith, culture, and discipleship to evangelical audiences.

name: Stu Escalona
bio: Stu Escalona is a pastor and Christian communicator dedicated to helping believers grow in their faith and understanding of Scripture. Through teaching and writing, he seeks to make biblical truths accessible and applicable to everyday Christian living.

name: Malcolm Guite
bio: Malcolm Guite is a poet, priest, and scholar who serves as Chaplain of Girton College, Cambridge. He is known for his contemporary sonnets, theological reflections, and work in Christian apologetics and the integration of faith with literature and the arts. His writing draws on both classical Christian tradition and modern sensibilities to help readers encounter God's presence in beauty, nature, and everyday life.
affiliation: Girton College, Cambridge; The Christian Institute

name: Grant Dutro
bio: Grant Dutro is an editorial project coordinator and Young Storytellers Fellow at Christianity Today, based in Nashville, Tennessee. He is pursuing a Master of Theological Studies at Vanderbilt Divinity School, and his writing explores modern culture through a theological lens.

name: Andy Olsen
bio: Andy Olsen is senior features writer at Christianity Today, where he previously oversaw the print magazine team. A graduate of Asbury University, his reporting on immigration, foreign aid, and the church's humanitarian work has been recognized by the Religion News Association and the Evangelical Press Association.

name: Erika Solomon
bio: Erika Solomon is a Reuters correspondent and journalist known for her investigative reporting on Middle Eastern affairs, international politics, and religious dynamics in global contexts. Her work frequently examines complex geopolitical issues with nuance and depth.

name: Ashley Ahn
bio: Ashley Ahn is a writer and content creator who engages Christian audiences with thoughtful perspectives on faith, culture, and discipleship. Her work encourages believers to deepen their understanding of Scripture and live out their faith authentically in today's world.

name: Bobby Jamieson
bio: Bobby Jamieson is a pastor, author, and editor known for his work on biblical ecclesiology and the doctrine of the local church. He has contributed significantly to evangelical conversations about church membership, discipline, and Baptist theology through both pastoral ministry and theological writing.

books.title: A Peculiar People: The Church as Culture
Going Public: Why Christians Should Care About Justice and the Common Good

name: Daniel R. Hyde
bio: Daniel R. Hyde is a Reformed pastor and prolific Christian author known for his accessible theological writings. He has dedicated his ministry to helping believers understand biblical doctrine and church history through clear, engaging scholarship.
education: M.A. in Theological Studies, Westminster Seminary California

books.title: Jesus Loves the Church: Female Ministry and the Office of Deacon
The Ten Commandments: Living as God's Covenant People
With Heart and Mind: A Guide to Loving God
The Serpent's Seed: A Reformation Understanding of Genesis 3:15
What Can I Find in the Psalms? A Study of the Psalms

name: Ryan Currie
bio: Ryan Currie (PhD, South African Theological Seminary) is associate professor of Bible and theology and dean of students at Gulf Theological Seminary in the United Arab Emirates, where he has served since 2015 as a global partner with Training Leaders International. He is the author of Evangelical Theological Aesthetics, and his writing appears in The Gospel Coalition and Credo Magazine.

name: Hunter Beaumont
bio: Hunter Beaumont (ThM, Dallas Theological Seminary) is the lead pastor of Fellowship Denver Church, which he helped plant in central Denver, and serves on the board of the Acts 29 church-planting network. Before ministry he worked in public accounting as a CPA, and he remains active investing in church planters.

name: John Freeman
bio: John Freeman is the founder of Harvest USA, a ministry begun in 1983 through Philadelphia's Tenth Presbyterian Church that helps the church minister to those affected by sexual struggles and brokenness. A graduate of the University of Tennessee and Westminster Theological Seminary, he is the author of 'Hide or Seek: When Men Get Real with God about Sex.'

name: Drake Osborn
bio: Drake Osborn serves as Pastor of Teaching and Liturgy at Grace Church in Waco, Texas. He writes on theology, Scripture, and the Christian life for outlets including Mere Orthodoxy and The Spurgeon Library, and shares regular theological reflections through his church's teaching ministry.

name: Aamna Mohdin
bio: Aamna Mohdin is a community affairs correspondent who reports on social issues, community developments, and human interest stories. Her journalism focuses on giving voice to underrepresented communities and exploring the real-world impact of social change.

name: Emma Brockes
bio: Emma Brockes is a British-American journalist and author known for her thoughtful reporting and personal essays exploring faith, culture, and human experience. Her work has appeared in major publications where she combines keen observation with emotional insight, often touching on themes relevant to Christian readers seeking depth and authenticity.

books.title: An Unsafe Haven: A Woman's Story of Escape from War
She Left Me the Gun: A True Story of Youth, Madness, and Guns

name: Chun Han Wong
