bio: Chun Han Wong is a journalist and author known for his insightful reporting on Christianity, faith communities, and religious dynamics in Asia and beyond. His work combines rigorous journalism with thoughtful analysis of how Christian faith intersects with culture, politics, and society.
affiliation: Religion News Service, The Wall Street Journal

name: Stephen Castle
bio: Stephen Castle is a journalist and author known for his reporting on international affairs and social issues. While primarily known for secular journalism, his work often explores themes relevant to faith communities, including religious freedom, humanitarian concerns, and cultural commentary.

name: Rich Bitterman
bio: Rich Bitterman is the pastor of Cedar Ridge Baptist Church, a small rural Southern Baptist congregation in Missouri. He came to faith at age 42 after nearly two decades running a business in the Kansas City area, and now writes devotions, sermons, and Bible-study resources through his site and his 'Old Paths & New Roads' newsletter.

name: Stephen Witmer
bio: Stephen Witmer is a pastor and author committed to helping Christians understand Scripture and live out their faith in practical ways. He serves as senior pastor of Pepperell Christian Fellowship in Massachusetts and has written extensively on biblical themes for Christian audiences. His teaching combines careful exegesis with pastoral sensitivity to real-life discipleship challenges.
affiliation: Pepperell Christian Fellowship, The Gospel Coalition

books.title: Eternity Changes Everything: How to Live Now in Light of Forever
10 Questions to Diagnose Your Spiritual Health

name: Reagan Rose
bio: Reagan Rose (MDiv, The Master's Seminary) is the founder of Redeeming Productivity, a media ministry devoted to a gospel-centered approach to personal productivity. He is the author of 'Redeeming Productivity: Getting More Done for the Glory of God' and previously served as director of digital platforms for Grace to You.

name: Louis Markos
bio: Louis Markos is a professor of literature and apologetics at Houston Baptist University who specializes in classical Christian thought and its integration with contemporary culture. He is a prolific author and speaker who helps Christians understand and defend their faith through the lens of classical literature, philosophy, and theology. His work bridges ancient wisdom with modern apologetic needs, making him a valued resource for thoughtful believers.
education: Ph.D. in Medieval and Renaissance Literature, University of Michigan

books.title: From Achilles to Christ: Why Christians Should Read the Pagan Classics
Heaven and Hell: Visions of the Afterlife in the Western Poetic Tradition
The Myth of the Closed Mind: Seizing a Better Vision for the Next Generation
On the Shoulders of Hobbits: The Road to Virtue with Tolkien and Lewis

name: Pranav Baskar
bio: Pranav Baskar is a prize-winning independent journalist based in New York and Chicago whose reporting has appeared in The New York Times, NPR, The Times of India, and The Sydney Morning Herald. His work for the Times has covered international affairs, including the war in Ukraine, and his feature reporting spans news and human-interest stories across several continents.

name: Alice Speri
bio: Alice Speri is an investigative journalist known for her work covering immigration, labor, and human rights issues. While not primarily a Christian content creator, her reporting often intersects with faith-based perspectives on justice, dignity, and compassion for vulnerable populations.

name: Laurence Norman
bio: Laurence Norman is a journalist and religious correspondent known for his reporting on faith, politics, and cultural issues. His work has appeared in major publications covering the intersection of Christianity and contemporary society.

name: Sharonda Cooper
bio: Sharonda Cooper (MEng, Massachusetts Institute of Technology) serves as a content coordinator for women's initiatives at The Gospel Coalition and is a Bible teacher with a passion for evangelism. She is pursuing an MDiv at The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary and has authored and contributed to studies including 'Evangelism' and 'Turn Your Eyes.'

name: John Beeson
bio: John Beeson is co-lead pastor of New Life Bible Fellowship in Tucson, Arizona. A graduate of Gordon College and Princeton Theological Seminary (MDiv), he pastored in New Jersey before returning to Arizona in 2015. He is coauthor of Trading Faces: Removing the Masks That Hide Your God-Given Identity (with his wife, Angel) and Blogging for God's Glory in a Click-Bait World, and he writes regularly at The Bee Hive and for The Gospel Coalition.

name: Joanna Kimbrel
bio: Joanna Kimbrel is a Bible teacher and writer whose work appears with The Gospel Coalition, and she is pursuing an MA in theological studies at Westminster Theological Seminary. She is the coauthor (with Courtney Doctor) of 'Behold and Believe,' a Bible study on the 'I Am' statements of Jesus, and author of 'The Greatest Hero.'

name: William S. Plummer
bio: William S. Plummer was a 19th-century Presbyterian minister and biblical scholar known for his expository writings and commentary work. His detailed exegetical approach to Scripture made him a respected voice in Reformed Christian circles during the Victorian era.

books.title: Psalms: A Critical and Expository Commentary

name: Elizabeth Russell
bio: Elizabeth Russell is a Christian author and speaker known for her work in faith-based content and spiritual development. Her writing encourages believers to deepen their relationship with Christ through practical wisdom and biblical insight.

name: Sam Wollaston
bio: Sam Wollaston is a writer and journalist known for his thoughtful commentary and cultural criticism. His work explores contemporary issues with insight and clarity, often engaging with topics relevant to faith and values.

name: Christopher Thomond
bio: Christopher Thomond is an accomplished photographer known for his compelling visual storytelling and documentary work. His lens captures authentic human moments and significant cultural narratives with artistic sensitivity and clarity.

name: Steven Erlanger
bio: Steven Erlanger is an accomplished journalist and foreign correspondent with extensive experience covering international affairs, conflict zones, and geopolitical developments. While his work spans secular media outlets, his reporting often explores themes relevant to global Christian communities and international religious concerns.

name: Glen Scrivener
bio: Glen Scrivener is a British author, speaker, and evangelist known for his accessible approach to Christian apologetics and cultural commentary. He has become well-known for making the gospel relevant to contemporary secular audiences through writing, podcasting, and public speaking. His work emphasizes the beauty of the Christian message and its implications for how we live in the modern world.
affiliation: Speaker and author; associated with various Christian organizations and events

name: Mitch Chase
bio: Mitch Chase is a pastor and Bible teacher known for his work in expository preaching and biblical theology. He has served in pastoral ministry and is recognized for helping churches and believers engage deeply with Scripture through teaching and written resources.

name: Andrew Lisi
bio: Andrew Lisi (MDiv, Trinity Evangelical Divinity School) spent a decade in pastoral ministry and missions before becoming a partner and senior financial planner at The Next Level Planning Group in Chicago. Drawing on both vocations, he writes on faith, work, money, and generosity for outlets including The Gospel Coalition.

name: Zachary Conover
bio: Zachary Conover is the outreach pastor at Apologia Church in Arizona and communications director for End Abortion Now. A contributor at Apologia Studios and co-host of Apologia Radio, he writes and speaks on the pro-life cause, apologetics, and the Christian worldview.

name: Jason Wilson
bio: Jason Wilson is a Christian author, youth mentor, and speaker who founded the Cave of Adullam Transformational Training Academy in Detroit, mentoring young men through martial arts, emotional regulation, and Scripture-based principles. His best-selling books 'Cry Like a Man,' 'Battle Cry,' and 'The Man the Moment Demands' address biblical masculinity and emotional wholeness for men.

name: J. Stephen Yuille
bio: J. Stephen Yuille is a biblical scholar and author dedicated to helping Christians develop a deeper understanding of Scripture. He is known for his thoughtful approach to biblical interpretation and his commitment to equipping believers with tools for meaningful study of God's Word.

name: David Hammer and Ramon Antonio Vargas
bio: David Hammer and Ramon Antonio Vargas are investigative journalists based in New Orleans who have contributed reporting to WWL Louisiana and other major news outlets. Their work focuses on uncovering stories of public interest and accountability in Louisiana communities.

name: Travis Kircher
bio: Travis Kircher is a Louisville, Kentucky-based journalist serving as an associate breaking news editor for WORLD News Group. A longtime reporter whose work has appeared in numerous publications, he is also a licensed pilot who volunteers with Mission Aviation Fellowship and hosts the podcast 'A Log by the Fire.'

name: Ruth Maclean
bio: Ruth Maclean is a journalist and author known for her reporting on West African affairs and religious topics. Her work explores themes of faith, culture, and social change across the African continent, offering insights that resonate with Christian readers seeking to understand global perspectives on faith and community.

name: Kejal Vyas
bio: Kejal Vyas is a journalist and writer who covers faith, culture, and social issues for leading Christian and mainstream publications. Her work explores the intersection of belief and contemporary life, offering thoughtful perspectives on how Christians engage with the modern world.

name: Andy Shurson
bio: Andy Shurson is a Christian communicator and content creator dedicated to helping believers grow in their faith and understanding of Scripture. Through his writing and teaching, he explores practical ways to apply biblical principles to everyday life and deepen one's relationship with Christ.

name: Ligonier Editorial
bio: Ligonier Editorial represents the collective voice of Ligonier Ministries' editorial team, bringing Reformed Christian theology and biblical teaching to a global audience. Through articles, devotionals, and curated content, this editorial collective helps Christians deepen their understanding of God's Word and Reformed doctrine.

name: Alistair Chalmers
bio: Alistair Chalmers is a Scottish pastor serving Ferniehill Evangelical Church in Edinburgh and a member of the FIEC Pastors' Network. An avid reader, he writes weekly book reviews and reflections on Christian living, theology, and pastoral ministry at his blog.

name: Amy Tyson
bio: Amy Tyson is a writer and speaker who explores faith, culture, and Christian living with thoughtfulness and grace. Her work encourages readers to deepen their relationship with God while engaging meaningfully with the world around them.

name: Aaron Summers
bio: Aaron Summers is a writer and Christian communicator who focuses on making biblical truth accessible to contemporary audiences. Through his work, he explores themes of faith, discipleship, and spiritual growth for modern believers.

name: Thomas Christianson
bio: Thomas Christianson is a Christian writer, speaker, and professor based in the Baltimore area. He holds a master's degree in practical theology from Regent University and a doctorate from Fuller Theological Seminary, and is the author of 'The Unreasonable Jesus.' His work has appeared in RELEVANT and on the I Am Second blog.

name: Brian Tabb
bio: Brian Tabb is a pastor, author, and teacher known for helping Christians understand Scripture with theological depth and practical wisdom. He has written extensively on biblical theology and the Gospel, with a passion for connecting God's Word to everyday Christian life.

books.title: The God Who Justifies: Justification in the Theology of John Calvin
Justification and the New Perspective on Paul

name: J. V. Fesko
bio: J. V. Fesko is a Reformed theologian and author known for his scholarly work on covenant theology, justification, and Christian doctrine. He has written numerous books designed to help Christians understand biblical theology and its practical implications for faith and practice.
education: Ph.D. in Systematic Theology, University of Aberdeen

name: John D. Wilsey
bio: John D. Wilsey is a historian and author who specializes in American religious history and the intersection of faith and public life. His scholarly work explores how Christian thought has shaped American culture and politics, offering evangelical readers a thoughtful examination of their faith's role in the nation's story.

books.title: American Exceptionalism and Civil Religion: How the Ever-Present Past Shapes the American Future
One Nation Under God: An Evangelical's Plea for Faith-Based Political Engagement
The Essential Evangelicalism of John Newton

name: Choe Sang-Hun
bio: Choe Sang-Hun is a respected journalist and foreign correspondent known for his reporting on East Asian affairs, particularly North Korea and South Korea. His work has provided Western audiences with critical insights into religious persecution and human rights issues in the region from a perspective informed by Christian values and concern for faith communities.

name: Ephrat Livni
bio: Ephrat Livni is a journalist and writer known for her work exploring culture, psychology, and human behavior through a thoughtful lens. She has contributed to various publications examining contemporary issues and their intersection with faith and values.

name: Chris Larson
bio: Chris Larson is a Christian author and communicator dedicated to helping believers grow in their faith and understanding of Scripture. His work focuses on making biblical truths accessible and practical for contemporary Christian living.

name: Michael Keller
bio: Michael Keller (PhD, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam) is the founding and senior pastor of Redeemer Presbyterian Church–Lincoln Square in New York City, a Council member of The Gospel Coalition, and a fellow of the Keller Center for Cultural Apologetics. The son of Tim and Kathy Keller, he holds an MDiv and ThM from Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary and is the author of The Stories We Live By: How Jesus Critiques and Completes What Our Culture Tells Us.

name: Aaron Garriott
bio: Aaron L. Garriott is managing editor of Tabletalk, the monthly discipleship magazine of Ligonier Ministries, resident adjunct professor at Reformation Bible College in Sanford, Florida, and a teaching elder in the Presbyterian Church in America. A graduate of Wheaton College and Reformed Theological Seminary in Orlando, he is the author of A Word Fitly Spoken and Thy Deepest Distress: Anxiety and Depression in the Christian Life.

name: Cliff McManis
bio: Cliff McManis is a pastor and Bible teacher with a heart for expository preaching and biblical theology. He has been instrumental in teaching Christians to understand Scripture in its proper context and apply God's Word to their daily lives. McManis is known for his clear, accessible approach to Christian doctrine and pastoral ministry.

books.title: Confident in Christ: A New Perspective on the Gospel of John

name: Mark MacDonald
bio: Mark MacDonald is a respected voice in Christian leadership and pastoral ministry. His writings and teachings focus on helping believers develop deeper faith and navigate modern spiritual challenges with biblical wisdom.

name: Alaina Demopoulos
bio: Alaina Demopoulos is a writer and content creator focused on faith, culture, and Christian living. She contributes to various Christian publications and platforms, bringing thoughtful perspectives on contemporary issues through a biblical lens.

name: Alex Harris
bio: Alex Harris is a Christian author and speaker known for his work on biblical worldview and faith development. He has contributed to conversations around Christian living and spiritual formation for evangelical audiences.
affiliation: The Keller Center for Cultural Apologetics (The Gospel Coalition)
known_for: Co-authoring the bestselling teen book Do Hard Things with his twin brother Brett and co-founding The Rebelution movement.
current_role: Attorney; fellow at The Keller Center for Cultural Apologetics

faqs.a: Alex Harris is an attorney and Christian author who co-wrote Do Hard Things: A Teenage Rebellion Against Low Expectations at age eighteen with his twin brother Brett. The brothers founded TheRebelution.com at sixteen, which became one of the most popular Christian teen websites.

faqs.q: What does Alex Harris do now?
faqs.a: Harris is a Harvard Law School graduate who clerked for U.S. Supreme Court Justices Anthony Kennedy and Neil Gorsuch and was named to Forbes 30 Under 30 for law and policy. He practices law and serves as a fellow at The Keller Center for Cultural Apologetics.

faqs.q: Is Alex Harris related to Joshua Harris?
faqs.a: Yes, Alex and his twin brother Brett are younger brothers of Joshua Harris, the former pastor and author of I Kissed Dating Goodbye who later announced he was no longer a Christian. Alex has remained an evangelical and writes on faith and public life.

The Rebelution is a movement Alex and Brett Harris launched as teenagers, calling young people to a 'rebellion against low expectations' by doing hard things for the glory of God. It spawned conferences, the bestselling book Do Hard Things, and a lasting online community.

name: Elian Peltier and Safiullah Padshah
bio: Elian Peltier is a journalist known for reporting on religious and social issues, while Safiullah Padshah brings expertise in international affairs and cultural analysis. Together, their collaborative work has informed readers about faith communities and global perspectives with journalistic integrity.

name: D.A. Carson
bio: Donald Arthur Carson (born December 21, 1946) is research professor of New Testament at Trinity Evangelical Divinity School, where he taught full-time from 1978 until 2018, and co-founder and president emeritus of The Gospel Coalition. A Canadian evangelical, he earned his PhD in New Testament from the University of Cambridge under C.F.D. Moule and has authored or edited more than sixty books spanning biblical theology, exegesis, hermeneutics, and Christian engagement with culture. Carson is widely regarded as one of the most prolific and influential evangelical New Testament scholars of his generation. His commentary work (especially on John, Matthew, and the General Epistles), his rigorous defenses of biblical authority, and his pastoral writing on prayer, suffering, and the gospel have shaped seminary education and pastoral ministry across the English-speaking evangelical world.
education: McGill University (BSc); Central Baptist Seminary (MDiv); University of Cambridge (PhD)

name: Sinclair Ferguson
bio: Sinclair B. Ferguson (born February 21, 1948) is a Scottish Reformed theologian and Presbyterian minister who serves as Chancellor's Professor of Systematic Theology at Reformed Theological Seminary and as a teaching fellow at Ligonier Ministries. He has pastored congregations on both sides of the Atlantic, including First Presbyterian Church (Columbia, SC) and St George's-Tron in Glasgow, and previously served as professor of systematic theology at Westminster Theological Seminary in Philadelphia. Ferguson is known for warm, accessible preaching of historic Reformed orthodoxy with a strong pastoral and Christ-centered emphasis. His book The Whole Christ revived twenty-first century interest in the Marrow Controversy and the relationship between law and gospel; his works on the Holy Spirit and the Christian life have become standard texts in Reformed seminaries.
known_for: Warm, Christ-centered exposition of Reformed theology, especially The Whole Christ on law, gospel, and the Marrow Controversy.
current_role: Chancellor's Professor of Systematic Theology at Reformed Theological Seminary; teaching fellow and vice-chairman of Ligonier Ministries; preaching associate at Trinity Church, Aberdeen

faqs.a: Ferguson is a Scottish Presbyterian minister. He has pastored on both sides of the Atlantic, including St George's-Tron in Glasgow and First Presbyterian Church in Columbia, South Carolina, and now serves as a preaching associate at Trinity Church in Aberdeen, Scotland.

faqs.q: What is Sinclair Ferguson known for?
faqs.a: Ferguson is known for combining rigorous Reformed theology with warm, pastoral preaching. His book The Whole Christ (2016), on the eighteenth-century Marrow Controversy and the relationship between law and gospel, has become a modern classic, and his works on the Holy Spirit and the Christian life are standard seminary texts.

Yes. Born in 1948, Ferguson serves as Chancellor's Professor of Systematic Theology at Reformed Theological Seminary, is a teaching fellow and vice-chairman at Ligonier Ministries, and continues to speak at conferences such as Ligonier's national conference. He previously held the systematic theology chair at Westminster Theological Seminary in Philadelphia.

Yes. Ferguson stands squarely in the historic Reformed and Calvinist tradition, subscribing to the Westminster Confession of Faith. His theology emphasizes union with Christ, the ministry of the Holy Spirit, and grace-centered pastoral application.

name: John MacArthur
bio: John Fullerton MacArthur Jr. (born June 19, 1939) is the longtime pastor-teacher of Grace Community Church in Sun Valley, California (since 1969), chancellor of The Master's University and The Master's Seminary, and the featured Bible teacher of the syndicated radio and online ministry Grace to You. The son of a pastor, MacArthur has spent more than five decades preaching expositionally through the New Testament and has produced a verse-by-verse commentary set covering the entire NT. MacArthur is one of the most prominent voices in contemporary fundamentalist-leaning evangelicalism, known for his uncompromising stance on the inerrancy and sufficiency of Scripture, cessationist doctrine of the Holy Spirit, and dispensational eschatology. He has authored or edited more than 150 books, and his MacArthur Study Bible has become one of the bestselling study Bibles of the modern era.
affiliation: Grace Community Church / The Master's Seminary
education: Bob Jones University; Los Angeles Pacific College; Talbot Theological Seminary (MDiv, DD)

name: Michael Horton
bio: Michael Scott Horton (born May 11, 1964) is the J. Gresham Machen Professor of Systematic Theology and Apologetics at Westminster Seminary California and host of the White Horse Inn radio program. An ordained minister in the United Reformed Churches in North America, he holds a PhD from the University of Coventry & Wycliffe Hall, Oxford, and is a leading voice in the Reformed confessional tradition in America. Horton is known for sharp critiques of American evangelicalism's drift into therapeutic, moralistic, and consumer-driven Christianity. His magnum opus The Christian Faith and his shorter Pilgrim Theology have become widely used systematic-theology textbooks. He has been a strong defender of covenant theology, the means of grace, and a confessional Reformed identity over against revivalism and pragmatism.
affiliation: Westminster Seminary California; Sola Media / White Horse Inn
education: Biola University (BA); Westminster Seminary California (MAR); University of Coventry / Wycliffe Hall, Oxford (PhD)
denomination: United Reformed Churches in North America (URCNA)
known_for: Hosting the White Horse Inn podcast, founding Modern Reformation magazine, and critiquing American evangelicalism's therapeutic drift in books like Christless Christianity.
current_role: J. Gresham Machen Professor of Systematic Theology and Apologetics, Westminster Seminary California (since 1998)

faqs.a: Horton is an ordained minister in the United Reformed Churches in North America (URCNA), a confessional Reformed denomination. He teaches at Westminster Seminary California, where he has been the J. Gresham Machen Professor of Systematic Theology and Apologetics since 1998.

Yes. Horton is a confessional Reformed theologian who subscribes to the historic Reformed confessions, including the Three Forms of Unity. He is one of the leading defenders of covenant theology and confessional Calvinism in America.

faqs.q: What is the White Horse Inn?
faqs.a: The White Horse Inn is a long-running radio show and podcast Horton founded that discusses Reformation theology and its application to the modern church. It is part of Sola Media, which also produces Modern Reformation magazine and Core Christianity.

faqs.q: What is Michael Horton known for?
faqs.a: Horton is known for his systematic theology textbook The Christian Faith, his critique of American Christianity's consumer-driven and therapeutic tendencies in Christless Christianity, and his advocacy of a churchly, confessional Reformed faith over against revivalism.

name: Andy Crouch
bio: Andy Crouch (born 1968) is partner for theology and culture at Praxis, a venture-building organization that supports faith-driven entrepreneurs and innovators. He served for more than a decade as an editor at Christianity Today, where he was executive editor and senior editor for theology and culture, and was previously a campus minister with InterVarsity Christian Fellowship at Harvard University. Crouch's writing focuses on culture-making, technology, family life, and the formation of human persons in an age of distraction and disembodiment. His book Culture Making has become a standard reference for evangelical engagement with culture, and his more recent work (The Tech-Wise Family, The Life We're Looking For) has shaped the conversation about Christian discipleship in a digital age.
education: Cornell University (BA); Boston University School of Theology (MDiv)
denomination: Evangelical (interdenominational; formerly editor at Christianity Today)
known_for: The book Culture Making, which reframed evangelical cultural engagement around creating culture rather than condemning it, and The Tech-Wise Family on technology and household formation.
current_role: Partner for Theology and Culture at Praxis

faqs.a: Andy Crouch (born 1968) is an author and partner for theology and culture at Praxis, a venture-building organization for faith-driven entrepreneurs. He previously spent more than a decade at Christianity Today, including as executive editor, and served ten years with InterVarsity Christian Fellowship at Harvard.

faqs.q: What is Andy Crouch known for?
faqs.a: Crouch is best known for Culture Making (2008), which argued Christians should create culture rather than merely critique it, and The Tech-Wise Family (2017) on putting technology in its proper place at home. His recent book The Life We're Looking For addresses personhood in a technological age.

faqs.q: What is Praxis, where Andy Crouch works?
faqs.a: Praxis is a venture-building ecosystem that supports founders and organizations pursuing 'redemptive entrepreneurship' — business and nonprofit ventures shaped by Christian faith. Crouch serves as its partner for theology and culture, acting as a teacher and framework-builder for its fellows and community.

faqs.q: What is Andy Crouch's view on technology?
faqs.a: Crouch argues that technology is not neutral: it promises 'easy everywhere' abundance while eroding embodied relationships and the formation of persons. He advocates practical household disciplines — like putting devices in their place and prioritizing shared meals and rest — over wholesale rejection of technology.

name: N.T. Wright
bio: Nicholas Thomas Wright (born December 1, 1948) is a leading British New Testament scholar, Anglican theologian, and former Bishop of Durham (2003-2010). He has held senior teaching posts at Oxford, Cambridge, McGill, and the University of St Andrews, where he served as research professor of New Testament and early Christianity, and is now senior research fellow at Wycliffe Hall, Oxford. Wright is a central figure in the New Perspective on Paul and has authored a multi-volume series Christian Origins and the Question of God examining Jesus, Paul, and the resurrection within their first-century Jewish context. His more accessible works (Surprised by Hope, Simply Christian, After You Believe) have brought historical and theological scholarship to a wide lay readership, while his views on justification have sparked ongoing debate within Reformed circles.
affiliation: Wycliffe Hall, Oxford / University of St Andrews
education: University of Oxford (BA, MA, DPhil, DD)

name: Doug Wilson
bio: Douglas James Wilson (born June 18, 1953) is the senior fellow of theology at New Saint Andrews College and pastor of Christ Church in Moscow, Idaho, the flagship congregation of the Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches (CREC). A central figure in classical Christian education and postmillennial Reformed circles, he co-founded New Saint Andrews College and Logos School and has been a prolific author for more than four decades. Wilson is known for his combative, satirical writing style and his advocacy of Christian classical education, paedocommunion, postmillennial eschatology, and a robust application of biblical law to public life. He is a polarizing figure within the broader evangelical world: admired by readers who value his cultural confidence and theological clarity, and criticized by others over his views on slavery, patriarchy, and church controversies in Moscow.
affiliation: Christ Church, Moscow, ID / New Saint Andrews College
denomination: Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches (CREC), which he co-founded
known_for: Leading a fast-growing Reformed community in Moscow, Idaho, pioneering the classical Christian education movement, and advocating a combative postmillennial vision of Christian cultural dominance.
current_role: Pastor of Christ Church, Moscow, Idaho; senior fellow of theology at New Saint Andrews College

faqs.a: Douglas Wilson (born 1953) is the pastor of Christ Church in Moscow, Idaho, which he has led for roughly five decades, and a co-founder of New Saint Andrews College, Logos School, and Canon Press. He is a prolific author known for classical Christian education, postmillennial eschatology, and a satirical, combative writing style.

Wilson is a founder of the Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches (CREC), a small Reformed denomination for which Christ Church serves as the flagship congregation. The CREC now has member churches across the United States and internationally.

faqs.q: Is Doug Wilson a Christian nationalist?
faqs.a: Wilson has described himself as a Christian nationalist and wrote the book Mere Christendom advocating an explicitly Christian civil order. His influence drew national attention in 2025-2026 through ties to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who attends a church in Wilson's CREC and invited him to lead a Pentagon prayer service.

Wilson is a polarizing figure even among conservative evangelicals. Critics point to his co-authored booklet on American slavery, his strong patriarchal teachings on gender roles, and his handling of abuse-related church controversies in Moscow, while supporters value his cultural confidence, institution-building, and theological clarity.

Wilson has written dozens of books over four decades, including Recovering the Lost Tools of Learning (with a foreword role in launching classical Christian education), Reforming Marriage, and Mere Christendom. He also debated atheist Christopher Hitchens in the film Collision and blogs prolifically at Blog & Mablog.

name: Jonathan Leeman
bio: Jonathan Leeman is the editorial director of 9Marks, a ministry founded by Mark Dever to recover biblically faithful church practice. He holds a PhD from the University of Wales (UK) on the subject of church membership and discipline, and serves as a teaching pastor at Cheverly Baptist Church in suburban Washington, D.C. Leeman has written extensively on ecclesiology, congregational polity, the church-state relationship, and the public dimension of the local church. His books on church membership and church discipline are foundational texts within the 9Marks movement, and his more political work (How the Nations Rage, Political Church) has framed evangelical conversations about Christian engagement with public life.
education: University of Virginia (BA); Wales Evangelical School of Theology (PhD); Southern Baptist Theological Seminary (MDiv)
known_for: Shaping the 9Marks movement's teaching on church membership, church discipline, and congregational polity, and writing on Christianity and politics.
current_role: President and editorial director of 9Marks; elder at Cheverly Baptist Church (Washington, DC area)

faqs.a: Jonathan Leeman is the president and editorial director of 9Marks, the church-health ministry founded by Mark Dever, and an elder at Cheverly Baptist Church near Washington, DC. He holds a PhD in ecclesiology from the University of Wales and co-hosts the Pastors Talk podcast.

9Marks is a ministry that promotes nine biblical 'marks' of a healthy church, including expositional preaching, meaningful membership, and church discipline. Leeman edits its journal and book series and teaches adjunctively at several Southern Baptist and Reformed seminaries.

Leeman works within the Reformed Baptist stream of evangelicalism represented by 9Marks and Capitol Hill Baptist Church, which holds to a Reformed understanding of salvation. His own scholarly work focuses less on soteriology and more on ecclesiology, church authority, and political theology.

faqs.q: What is Jonathan Leeman known for?
faqs.a: Leeman is known for foundational 9Marks books on church membership and discipline, and for works on faith and politics such as How the Nations Rage and Political Church. He argues that the local church is a public, political community whose primary allegiance is to King Jesus.

name: Thomas Schreiner
bio: Thomas R. Schreiner is the James Buchanan Harrison Professor of New Testament Interpretation and associate dean of the School of Theology at The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary, where he has taught since 1997. He previously taught for eleven years at Bethel Theological Seminary and served as preaching pastor of Clifton Baptist Church in Louisville. Schreiner is known for his commentaries on Romans, Galatians, Hebrews, and 1-2 Peter & Jude (BECNT and Pillar series), and for his Pauline theology in Paul, Apostle of God's Glory in Christ. A complementarian and confessional Reformed Baptist, he has been a steady scholarly voice on justification by faith, perseverance, and the unity of the biblical canon in The King in His Beauty.
education: Western Oregon State College (BS); Western Conservative Baptist Seminary (MDiv, ThM); Fuller Theological Seminary (PhD)

name: Diane Langberg
bio: Diane Langberg is a clinical psychologist who has spent nearly five decades caring for trauma survivors and equipping the church to do the same. She directs Diane Langberg, PhD & Associates—a group practice in suburban Philadelphia—and serves on the executive board of the American Bible Society, the boards of GRACE (Godly Response to Abuse in the Christian Environment) and Mission:Network, and as a faculty member of Westminster Theological Seminary's School of Christian Counseling and Educational Foundation curriculum. Langberg is internationally recognized for her work with survivors of childhood sexual abuse, clergy abuse, and global trafficking, and for her prophetic critique of how power is misused inside Christian institutions. Her writing—especially Suffering and the Heart of God and Redeeming Power—has reframed the evangelical conversation around abuse, trauma-informed care, and the church's complicity in protecting power.

name: Carl Trueman
bio: Carl R. Trueman (born 1967) is a British-born historian and theologian who serves as professor of biblical and religious studies at Grove City College in Pennsylvania. He previously taught for nearly two decades at Westminster Theological Seminary, including as Paul Woolley Professor of Church History, and is a fellow at the Ethics and Public Policy Center. Trueman is best known for his cultural-historical analysis of modern selfhood and identity. His book The Rise and Triumph of the Modern Self traces the philosophical genealogy from Rousseau through the Romantics to today's expressive individualism and gender ideology, and has become one of the most widely cited evangelical books of the 2020s. His earlier work covers Reformation history, theology, and confessional Reformed identity.
education: University of Cambridge (MA); University of Aberdeen (PhD)
known_for: The Rise and Triumph of the Modern Self, a widely cited genealogy of expressive individualism and the modern identity revolution.
current_role: Professor of Biblical and Religious Studies at Grove City College (on loan to the University of Notre Dame as Busch Family Visiting Research Fellow for 2025-26); fellow at the Ethics and Public Policy Center

faqs.a: Trueman is an ordained minister in the Orthodox Presbyterian Church (OPC), a conservative confessional Presbyterian denomination. He is British-born and taught for nearly two decades at Westminster Theological Seminary before joining Grove City College in 2018.

faqs.q: What is Carl Trueman known for?
faqs.a: Trueman is best known for The Rise and Triumph of the Modern Self (2020), which traces how Western culture came to define identity by inner psychological feelings, particularly around sexuality and gender. Its shorter companion, Strange New World, has made the argument accessible to lay readers and become standard reading in evangelical circles.

Trueman is professor of biblical and religious studies at Grove City College in Pennsylvania. For the 2025-26 academic year he is serving as the Busch Family Visiting Research Fellow at the University of Notre Dame's Center for Citizenship and Constitutional Government.

faqs.q: Is Carl Trueman a historian or a theologian?
faqs.a: Both, though his training is as a church historian. He earned his PhD at Aberdeen, specialized in Reformation and post-Reformation studies (including work on John Owen), and applies that historical method to contemporary cultural analysis. He also writes regularly for First Things and World Opinions.

name: Jay Adams
bio: Jay Edward Adams (1929-2020) was an American Reformed pastor, professor, and author whose 1970 book Competent to Counsel launched the modern biblical counseling movement. A graduate of Johns Hopkins, Reformed Episcopal Seminary, and the University of Missouri, he taught practical theology at Westminster Theological Seminary in Philadelphia for many years and co-founded the Christian Counseling and Educational Foundation (CCEF). Adams argued that Scripture is sufficient for addressing the non-organic problems of living that secular psychology had claimed as its territory, and he proposed "nouthetic counseling"—from the Greek word noutheteo (to admonish or instruct)—as a biblically grounded alternative to the Freudian and Rogerian models then dominant. His work decisively shaped the curriculum of CCEF, the founding of the Association of Certified Biblical Counselors (ACBC), and the broader recovery of pastoral counseling within evangelical churches.
education: Johns Hopkins University (BA); Reformed Episcopal Seminary (BD); Temple University (STM); University of Missouri (PhD)

name: Sam Allberry
bio: Sam Allberry is a British-born pastor, author, and speaker who serves as associate pastor at Immanuel Church in Nashville, Tennessee, and as a senior lecturer in pastoral theology at Reformed Theological Seminary. He is a co-founder of Living Out, a ministry that helps Christians who experience same-sex attraction live faithfully under the lordship of Christ. An ordained Anglican minister and a celibate same-sex-attracted Christian, Allberry has become one of the most widely read evangelical voices on biblical sexuality, singleness, and the body. His book Is God Anti-Gay? has been translated into more than fifteen languages, and 7 Myths About Singleness reframes singleness as a gift rather than a deficiency within the church's life.
education: University of Oxford (BA); Wycliffe Hall, Oxford (BTh)

name: Christopher Yuan
bio: Christopher Yuan is an American speaker, author, and faculty member at Moody Bible Institute, where he has taught since 2008. A former dentist whose life unraveled into drug dealing, prison, and an HIV-positive diagnosis, he came to Christ in prison and has since devoted his ministry to teaching the church a biblical theology of sexuality. Yuan and his mother Angela co-wrote Out of a Far Country, the memoir of his journey and her parallel conversion. His later book Holy Sexuality and the Gospel and the accompanying Holy Sexuality Project have become widely used resources for parents, pastors, and same-sex-attracted Christians who want to think about sexuality through a biblical rather than identity-driven framework.
education: University of Louisville (DMD); Moody Bible Institute (MA); Wheaton College Graduate School (DMin)

name: Andy Stanley
bio: Andy Stanley (born May 16, 1958) is the founder and senior pastor of North Point Ministries, a network of churches based in Alpharetta, Georgia, with weekly attendance of more than 30,000. The son of First Baptist Atlanta pastor Charles Stanley, he founded North Point Community Church in 1995 and has become one of the most influential voices in American megachurch ministry. Stanley is widely known for his communication style, his focus on "unchurched" people, and his attempts to reframe Christian preaching around relevance to seekers. His ministry philosophy and willingness to depart from traditional evangelical positions—on topics from biblical inerrancy to LGBTQ inclusion—have made him a polarizing figure: celebrated by pragmatists for his cultural reach and critiqued by confessional evangelicals for what they see as theological compromise.
education: Georgia State University (BA); Dallas Theological Seminary (ThM)

name: Joni Eareckson Tada
bio: Joni Eareckson Tada (born October 15, 1949) is the founder and CEO of Joni and Friends International Disability Center, a global ministry to people affected by disability. A 1967 diving accident at age 17 left her a quadriplegic, and her subsequent journey through depression, faith, and vocation became the subject of her bestselling 1976 autobiography Joni and the 1979 motion picture of the same name. For nearly five decades Tada has spoken and written from a wheelchair about suffering, sovereignty, healing, and the dignity of disabled persons in the body of Christ. Joni and Friends provides wheelchairs to people in the developing world, trains churches in disability ministry, and runs Family Retreats for families affected by disability—and her writing has shaped how the evangelical world thinks about lament, providence, and embodiment.
education: Honorary doctorates from Westminster Theological Seminary, Lancaster Bible College, others

name: Sam Storms
bio: Sam Storms is the lead pastor for preaching and vision at Bridgeway Church in Oklahoma City and the founder of Enjoying God Ministries. Before pastoring he taught for many years at Wheaton College, and he has served as president of the Evangelical Theological Society. Storms is a leading voice within the "Reformed charismatic" stream of contemporary evangelicalism—holding to historic Reformed soteriology while affirming the present-day operation of the spiritual gifts described in 1 Corinthians 12-14. He has written extensively on eschatology (defending an amillennial position), the gifts of the Spirit, and Christian hedonism in the tradition of Jonathan Edwards and John Piper.
education: University of Oklahoma (BA); Dallas Theological Seminary (ThM); University of Texas at Dallas (PhD)

name: Roger Olson
bio: Roger E. Olson is professor emeritus of Christian theology and ethics at the George W. Truett Theological Seminary at Baylor University, where he taught from 1999 until his retirement. Before Baylor he taught for fifteen years at Bethel College in St. Paul, Minnesota. Olson is one of the most prominent contemporary defenders of Arminian theology against both Calvinism and open theism, and a careful historian of post-Reformation Protestant thought. His one-volume narrative The Story of Christian Theology has become a widely used seminary textbook, and his blog at Patheos is an active venue for accessible theological reflection on evangelical identity, soteriology, and the doctrine of God.
affiliation: George W. Truett Theological Seminary, Baylor University (emeritus)
education: Open Bible College (BA); North American Baptist Seminary (MA); Rice University (PhD)
known_for: Being contemporary evangelicalism's foremost defender of Arminian theology against Calvinism and writing the widely used textbook The Story of Christian Theology.
current_role: Professor Emeritus of Christian Theology and Ethics, George W. Truett Theological Seminary, Baylor University (retired December 2021); active blogger

faqs.a: No. Olson is contemporary evangelicalism's best-known defender of classical Arminianism and a vocal critic of Calvinism. His book Arminian Theology: Myths and Realities argues that Arminianism is a legitimate evangelical theology of grace, not the semi-Pelagianism its critics allege.

Olson is a Baptist who taught for over two decades at George W. Truett Theological Seminary, Baylor University's Baptist seminary, after fifteen years at Bethel College in Minnesota. He was raised Pentecostal before moving into Baptist life.

Yes, Olson retired from Truett Seminary in December 2021 and holds emeritus status. He remains active in theological writing through his long-running blog, where he continues series such as 'Why I Am an Evangelical Arminian Christian.'

faqs.q: What is Roger Olson known for?
faqs.a: Olson is known for The Story of Christian Theology, a standard seminary textbook of historical theology, and for his careful distinction between Arminianism and open theism. He describes himself as a 'post-conservative' evangelical who holds to orthodox doctrine while resisting fundamentalist boundary-drawing.

name: Tish Harrison Warren
bio: Tish Harrison Warren is an Anglican priest in the Anglican Church in North America (ACNA) and a writer whose work appears in The New York Times, Christianity Today, The Atlantic, and other outlets. She has served as a campus minister with InterVarsity at the University of Texas and Vanderbilt and as writer-in-residence at Resurrection South Austin. Warren writes from within the liturgical Christian tradition about the spiritual significance of ordinary embodied life—how making the bed, brushing teeth, drinking coffee, and eating leftovers can be sites of Christian formation. Her book Liturgy of the Ordinary won Christianity Today's 2018 Book of the Year, and her later Prayer in the Night reflects on the Compline prayer through her own experience of grief and miscarriage.
education: University of Texas at Austin (BA); Fuller Theological Seminary (MDiv)

name: Miroslav Volf
bio: Miroslav Volf (born September 25, 1956) is the Henry B. Wright Professor of Theology at Yale Divinity School and founding director of the Yale Center for Faith and Culture. A Croatian-born theologian, he was educated under Jürgen Moltmann at the University of Tübingen and has taught at Fuller Theological Seminary as well as Yale. Volf's work focuses on reconciliation, public faith, the human person, and the relationship between Christianity and Islam. His book Exclusion and Embrace—written in the wake of the wars in the former Yugoslavia—remains a landmark text on Christian theology of forgiveness and identity. More recent works (A Public Faith, Flourishing) address how religious communities can contribute to common life without coercion.
education: University of Tübingen (DrTheol, DrTheolHabil); Fuller Theological Seminary (MA)

name: Mark McMinn
bio: Mark R. McMinn is professor of psychology at George Fox University, where he serves as director of faith integration in the Graduate Department of Clinical Psychology. He previously taught at Wheaton College from 1993 to 2006, where he received teacher-of-the-year awards. He is board-certified by the American Board of Professional Psychology and a fellow of the American Psychological Association. McMinn is one of the most-cited evangelical voices on the integration of psychology, theology, and spirituality. His 1996 book Psychology, Theology, and Spirituality in Christian Counseling—a contemporary classic—argues that prayer, Scripture, sin, confession, forgiveness, and worship belong inside (not outside) the counseling room. His subsequent books extend that integrative project for both clinicians and pastors.

name: John Frame
bio: John M. Frame (born April 8, 1939) is professor emeritus of systematic theology and philosophy at Reformed Theological Seminary in Orlando, where he held the J.D. Trimble Chair until his retirement. He previously taught at Westminster Theological Seminary in Philadelphia and at Westminster Seminary California, where he was one of the founding faculty. Frame is best known for his "triperspectivalism"—the framework that approaches every theological question from normative, situational, and existential perspectives—and for his work as a presuppositional apologist in the tradition of Cornelius Van Til. His four-volume Theology of Lordship series and one-volume Systematic Theology have shaped a generation of Reformed pastors and theology students.
education: Princeton University (AB); Westminster Theological Seminary (BD); Yale University (MA, MPhil)

name: Clark Pinnock
bio: Clark H. Pinnock (1937-2010) was a Canadian Baptist theologian who taught for many years at McMaster Divinity College in Hamilton, Ontario, and previously at New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary, Trinity Evangelical Divinity School, and Regent College. Pinnock is best known for his theological pilgrimage from a strong defense of biblical inerrancy and Reformed theology in the 1960s to a much more open, Arminian-leaning theology in his later career. He became one of the most prominent advocates of "open theism," the view that the future is genuinely open and that God does not exhaustively foreknow free creaturely decisions, and contributed to the controversial 1994 volume The Openness of God. His later work also softened on inclusivism with respect to the unevangelized.
education: University of Toronto (BA); University of Manchester (PhD)
known_for: Being the leading evangelical proponent of open theism and co-authoring The Openness of God.
current_role: Deceased (1937-2010); was Professor Emeritus of Christian Interpretation, McMaster Divinity College

faqs.a: Clark H. Pinnock (1937-2010) was a Canadian Baptist theologian who taught at McMaster Divinity College in Hamilton, Ontario, from 1977 until his retirement in 2002, and earlier at New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary, Trinity Evangelical Divinity School, and Regent College. He died of a heart attack in August 2010 after announcing an Alzheimer's diagnosis earlier that year.

faqs.q: What is Clark Pinnock known for?
faqs.a: Pinnock is best known as a primary architect of open theism, the view that God does not exhaustively foreknow free future decisions, developed in the 1994 volume The Openness of God and his book Most Moved Mover. He also wrote A Wideness in God's Mercy, which took an inclusivist view of the unevangelized.

Early in his career Pinnock was a Calvinist and staunch defender of biblical inerrancy, but he underwent a well-documented theological pilgrimage toward Arminianism and eventually open theism. His shift made him one of the most controversial evangelical theologians of his generation.

faqs.q: How was Clark Pinnock viewed by mainstream evangelicals?
faqs.a: Pinnock remained a self-identified evangelical, but his open theism was sharply contested; the Evangelical Theological Society debated his membership in the early 2000s, ultimately retaining him. Many Reformed evangelicals regard open theism as outside the bounds of orthodoxy, while others credit Pinnock with raising honest questions about divine providence.

name: Andrew Walker
bio: Andrew T. Walker is associate professor of Christian ethics at The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary, fellow with the Ethics and Religious Liberty Commission of the SBC, and managing editor of WORLD Opinions. He previously served as director of policy studies at the ERLC. Walker writes at the intersection of Christian ethics, public theology, religious liberty, and political philosophy. His book God and the Transgender Debate has become a widely-used pastoral resource on biblical anthropology and gender, and his Liberty for All argues for religious liberty as a Christian principle that protects all people, not merely Christians.

name: David VanDrunen
bio: David VanDrunen is the Robert B. Strimple Professor of Systematic Theology and Christian Ethics at Westminster Seminary California, where he has taught since 2001. He is an ordained minister in the Orthodox Presbyterian Church and holds both a PhD in religious ethics from Northwestern and a JD from Loyola University Chicago. VanDrunen is the leading contemporary advocate of a Reformed two-kingdoms theology—the view that the redemptive kingdom of Christ (the church) and the common kingdom of God's providential rule over creation operate by distinct norms and ends. His work has reshaped Reformed conversations about politics, vocation, natural law, and the role of the church in public life.
education: Calvin College (BA); Westminster Theological Seminary (MDiv); Northwestern University (MA, PhD); Loyola University Chicago (JD)

name: Bill Hybels
bio: William Carlton Hybels (born December 12, 1951) is the founding pastor of Willow Creek Community Church in South Barrington, Illinois, which he led from its 1975 launch until his resignation in April 2018. Under his leadership Willow Creek became one of the largest and most-imitated churches in North America, and the Willow Creek Association (now the Global Leadership Network) trained hundreds of thousands of pastors worldwide in the seeker-sensitive model. Hybels resigned amid sexual misconduct allegations from multiple women that an independent review later found credible. The Willow Creek board acknowledged in 2018 that prior denials had been wrong and apologized. His pre-resignation books on leadership, evangelism, and church growth remain in wide circulation but are now read in light of subsequent revelations about his pastoral conduct.
education: Trinity College (BA); Trinity Evangelical Divinity School (MA)

name: Rick Warren
bio: Richard Duane Warren (born January 28, 1954) is the founding pastor of Saddleback Church in Lake Forest, California, which he started with his wife Kay in 1980. Saddleback grew into one of the largest churches in America, and Warren handed off the senior pastorate in 2022 to Andy Wood after more than four decades of leadership. Warren is best known for The Purpose Driven Life, a forty-day spiritual journey that has sold more than fifty million copies and become one of the bestselling nonfiction books in history. His earlier The Purpose Driven Church became the foundational text of a global ministry-training movement, and the P.E.A.C.E. Plan he and Kay launched mobilizes churches against poverty, illiteracy, disease, and corruption.
education: California Baptist University (BA); Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary (MDiv); Fuller Theological Seminary (DMin)

name: Lou Priolo
bio: Lou Priolo (1954-2023) was an American biblical counselor, author, and conference speaker who served full-time in biblical counseling for nearly forty years. A fellow in the Association of Certified Biblical Counselors (ACBC) and a member of the International Association of Biblical Counselors, he founded the nonprofit Competent to Counsel International, through which he trained pastors and laymen across the United States and overseas. Priolo authored more than a dozen counseling books for P&R Publishing and others, addressing anger, parenting, marriage, conflict, and people-pleasing. He was also the editor of the Resources for Biblical Living booklet series. Within the nouthetic counseling tradition pioneered by Jay Adams, Priolo's writing emphasized practical, sermon-on-the-mount-shaped applications of Scripture to the specific patterns of sinful and suffering human hearts.
education: Calvary Bible College (BA); Liberty University (MA); Calvary University (DD)

name: Robert Webber
bio: Robert Eugene Webber (1933-2007) was an American theologian known for his work on Christian worship and the early church. He spent much of his career as professor of theology at Wheaton College (1968-2000) and later as the Myers Professor of Ministry at Northern Seminary in Lombard, Illinois. He also founded and served as president of the Institute for Worship Studies in Orange Park, Florida (now The Robert E. Webber Institute for Worship Studies). Webber wrote more than forty books and is best known for the Ancient-Future series, which argues that recovering practices from the early and patristic church—creedal confession, the church year, the Eucharist, embodied liturgy—is essential for the witness of evangelical Christianity in a postmodern age. He played a key role in the Convergence Movement, blending evangelical, charismatic, and liturgical streams of worship.
affiliation: Northern Seminary / Institute for Worship Studies
education: Bob Jones University (BA); Reformed Episcopal Seminary (BD); Covenant Theological Seminary (ThM); Concordia Theological Seminary (ThD)

name: Alan Hirsch
bio: Alan Hirsch is an Australian-born author, missional church strategist, and serial entrepreneur whose work focuses on reactivating apostolic movements and equipping the body of Christ for cultural mission. He is the founding director of the Forge Mission Training Network, founder of 5Q Collective and 100Movements, and co-founder of the Wheaton College M.A. in Missional Church Movements. Hirsch's books develop a five-fold ministry framework (the APEST/5Q model) drawn from Ephesians 4:11—apostles, prophets, evangelists, shepherds, and teachers—as essential for the church to recover its missional capacity. The Forgotten Ways argues that the underground Chinese church and the early church share six core elements (mDNA) that today's institutional Western church has lost.

name: Eugene Peterson
bio: Eugene Hoiland Peterson (1932-2018) was an American Presbyterian pastor, scholar, poet, and translator best known for his contemporary-language paraphrase of the Bible, The Message. He pastored Christ Our King Presbyterian Church in Bel Air, Maryland, for nearly thirty years (1962-1991) before serving as professor of spiritual theology at Regent College in Vancouver until his retirement in 2006. Peterson's pastoral writing—shaped by long obedience, the spiritual disciplines, and a deep suspicion of the celebrity-and-program culture of American evangelicalism—has reframed how a generation of pastors think about their vocation. His five-volume Spiritual Theology series and his memoir The Pastor remain standard reading in pastoral theology courses, and The Message has been read in churches and homes around the world.
education: Seattle Pacific University (BA); New York Theological Seminary (STB); Johns Hopkins University (MA)

name: Richard Foster
bio: Richard J. Foster (born May 11, 1942) is a Quaker theologian and author whose 1978 book Celebration of Discipline introduced a generation of evangelicals to the classical disciplines of the Christian spiritual life. A graduate of George Fox College and Fuller Seminary, he founded Renovaré in 1988 to renew the church through engagement with the historic streams of Christian spirituality. Foster's writing recovers practices long associated with monasticism, contemplative prayer, and the Roman Catholic and Orthodox traditions—solitude, silence, fasting, simplicity, study, confession, worship, service—and frames them as gifts available to all Christians. While his work has been welcomed by many evangelicals as a corrective to programmatic discipleship, it has also been critiqued by some Reformed writers concerned about its mystical sources and its treatment of the means of grace.
education: George Fox College (BA); Fuller Theological Seminary (DPS)

name: David Platt
bio: David Platt (born December 11, 1978) is a Baptist pastor, author, and missionary advocate who founded Radical, a missions organization equipping believers to make disciples of all the nations. He served as senior pastor of The Church at Brook Hills in Birmingham, Alabama (2006-2014), as president of the International Mission Board of the SBC (2014-2018), and as lead pastor of McLean Bible Church in metro Washington, D.C. (2017-2024). Platt's first book Radical: Taking Back Your Faith from the American Dream became a New York Times bestseller and pressed evangelicals to examine the comforts and compromises of American Christian discipleship. His subsequent ministry has emphasized the unreached peoples of the world, costly Christian generosity, and an unflinching call to surrender wealth, ambition, and security for the sake of the gospel.
education: University of Georgia (BA); New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary (MDiv, ThM, PhD)

name: Tim Challies
bio: Tim Challies is a Canadian Reformed Baptist pastor, author, and blogger who has written daily at Challies.com since 2003, making him one of the longest-running and most-read evangelical bloggers in the English-speaking world. He serves as a pastor at Grace Fellowship Church in Toronto and is a co-founder of Cruciform Press. Challies's books span topics from biblical discernment and pornography to visual theology and family devotions, and his Visual Theology project translates complex doctrinal categories into accessible infographic-style charts and books. After the unexpected death of his twenty-year-old son Nick in 2020, Challies published Seasons of Sorrow, a year-long journal of grief that has become a widely-read companion for bereaved Christians.

name: James K.A. Smith
bio: James K.A. Smith is professor of philosophy at Calvin University, where he holds the Gary & Henrietta Byker Chair in Applied Reformed Theology and Worldview. He served for many years as the editor-in-chief of Image journal and previously edited Comment magazine, and he is a senior fellow at Cardus. Smith's Cultural Liturgies trilogy (Desiring the Kingdom, Imagining the Kingdom, Awaiting the King) argues that human beings are fundamentally lovers shaped by the embodied liturgies they participate in—both ecclesial and secular—rather than primarily thinkers. His more popular-level work (You Are What You Love, On the Road with Saint Augustine, How (Not) to Be Secular) has translated those arguments to a broad evangelical audience and reframed conversations about formation, worship, and modern selfhood.
education: Westminster Theological Seminary (MA); Institute for Christian Studies (MA); Villanova University (PhD)

name: Derek Rishmawy
bio: Derek Zaglul Rishmawy is a Reformed University Fellowship (RUF) campus minister at the University of California, Irvine, and holds a PhD in systematic theology from Trinity Evangelical Divinity School. He is a contributor and former editor at Mere Orthodoxy, a contributing writer at The Gospel Coalition and Christianity Today, and a co-host of the Mere Fidelity podcast with Matthew Lee Anderson and Andrew Wilson. Rishmawy writes at his blog Reformedish and across evangelical outlets on systematic theology, Reformed orthodoxy, doctrine of God, and the cultural questions of younger evangelical readers. His academic work focuses on the relation between Christology and theology proper in classical Reformed thought.
education: California State University Long Beach (BA); Talbot School of Theology (MA); Trinity Evangelical Divinity School (PhD)

name: John Lennox
bio: John Carson Lennox (born November 7, 1943) is emeritus professor of mathematics at the University of Oxford and emeritus fellow in mathematics and philosophy of science at Green Templeton College, Oxford. A Northern Irish-born mathematician, he has published on group theory and serves as a senior teaching fellow at the Oxford Centre for Christian Apologetics. Lennox is one of the most prominent contemporary apologists for Christianity from within the world of mathematics and the natural sciences, and has publicly debated Richard Dawkins, Christopher Hitchens, Peter Singer, and Michael Shermer. His books address creation and evolution (Seven Days That Divide the World), the new atheism (God's Undertaker, Gunning for God), the problem of evil, and—most recently—the philosophical and theological challenges of artificial intelligence (2084).
affiliation: University of Oxford (emeritus); Oxford Centre for Christian Apologetics
education: University of Cambridge (MA, PhD); University of Wales (DSc); University of Oxford (DPhil, DD)
known_for: Defending the rationality of Christian faith in public debates with Richard Dawkins and Christopher Hitchens and writing on science, God, and artificial intelligence.
current_role: Emeritus Professor of Mathematics, University of Oxford; Christian apologist and author

faqs.a: John Lennox (born 1943) is a Northern Irish mathematician and Christian apologist who is emeritus professor of mathematics at the University of Oxford. He is one of the best-known contemporary defenders of the compatibility of science and Christian faith, and in 2026 he published his autobiography, My Story.

faqs.q: What is John Lennox known for?
faqs.a: Lennox is known for his public debates with prominent atheists including Richard Dawkins, Christopher Hitchens, and Michael Shermer, and for books such as God's Undertaker: Has Science Buried God? and 2084, which addresses artificial intelligence from a Christian perspective.

faqs.q: What is John Lennox's view on evolution and Genesis?
faqs.a: In Seven Days That Divide the World, Lennox argues that Genesis 1 does not require a young earth and that Christians can hold to an ancient universe while affirming the historicity of Adam and Eve. He is critical of unguided naturalistic evolution as an explanation for life's origin and human uniqueness.

Yes. Though retired from his Oxford mathematics post, Lennox continues to write, lecture, and appear in high-profile conversations, including a 2026 appearance on The Diary of a CEO podcast and a 2025 dialogue with agnostic commentator Alex O'Connor. His recent work focuses on AI, transhumanism, and the search for meaning.

name: Matthew Stanford
bio: Matthew S. Stanford is the chief executive officer of the Hope and Healing Center & Institute in Houston and adjunct professor of psychiatry at Baylor College of Medicine and Houston Methodist Hospital's Institute for Academic Medicine. He earned his doctorate in behavioral neuroscience at Baylor University and completed a post-doctoral fellowship at the University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston. Stanford has worked clinically with patients struggling with aggression, personality disorders, post-traumatic stress disorder, substance dependence, bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia, and his research on the interplay between psychology and faith has been featured in The New York Times, USA Today, and Christianity Today. His writing equips pastors and churches to support those with serious mental illness without abandoning either clinical realism or biblical hope.
affiliation: Hope and Healing Center & Institute, Houston
education: Baylor University (PhD); University of Texas Medical Branch (postdoc)

name: Kay Warren
bio: Kay Warren is the co-founder of Saddleback Church in Lake Forest, California (with her husband Rick), an international speaker, Bible teacher, and one of the most prominent evangelical advocates for people living with mental illness. After her son Matthew took his life in 2013, she founded the Hope for Mental Health Initiative at Saddleback in 2014 and the BREATHE ministry in 2019 to support parents of children with serious mental illness. Warren writes and speaks on mental health, suffering, joy, and the privilege of pastoral life. Her work has helped shift evangelical conversation about mental illness away from stigma and toward a posture that combines biblical hope, clinical care, and church community.
affiliation: Hope for Brighter Tomorrows / Saddleback Church
denomination: Evangelical (Saddleback Church, a Baptist-rooted congregation that was part of the Southern Baptist Convention until 2023)
known_for: Co-founding Saddleback Church with Rick Warren and becoming one of evangelicalism's leading mental health advocates after her son Matthew's suicide in 2013.
current_role: President of Hope for Brighter Tomorrows (since 2024); co-founder of Saddleback Church

faqs.a: Kay Warren co-founded Saddleback Church in Lake Forest, California, with her husband Rick Warren in 1980 and served there until his retirement from senior leadership in 2022. She is an author, international speaker, and advocate on mental health and HIV/AIDS.

faqs.q: What happened to Kay Warren's son?
faqs.a: Her youngest son, Matthew, died by suicide in April 2013 at age 27 after a lifelong struggle with mental illness. That loss led Kay to found Saddleback's Hope for Mental Health Initiative in 2014 and the BREATHE ministry for parents of children with serious mental illness in 2019.

faqs.q: What does Kay Warren do now?
faqs.a: In 2024 she became president of Hope for Brighter Tomorrows, a nonprofit equipping families and churches to address mental health challenges. She continues to speak and write on mental illness, grief, suicide prevention, and finding joy amid suffering.

faqs.q: What is Kay Warren known for writing?
faqs.a: Her books include Choose Joy: Because Happiness Isn't Enough, Dangerous Surrender, and Say Yes to God. Her writing draws on her experiences with global HIV/AIDS advocacy, her son's mental illness and death, and decades of pastoral ministry at Saddleback.

name: William Lane Craig
bio: William Lane Craig (born August 23, 1949) is research professor of philosophy at Houston Christian University and professor of philosophy at Talbot School of Theology, Biola University. He holds two earned doctorates—one in philosophy from the University of Birmingham and one in theology from the University of Munich, where he studied under Wolfhart Pannenberg—and is the founder of Reasonable Faith. Craig is one of the most prolific and widely-debated Christian apologists of the past half-century, best known for his contemporary defense of the kalam cosmological argument and the historicity of Jesus's resurrection. He has debated atheists including Christopher Hitchens, Sam Harris, and Lawrence Krauss, and his more recent work has addressed the historical Adam and the doctrine of the atonement.
affiliation: Houston Christian University / Talbot School of Theology
education: Wheaton College (BA); Trinity Evangelical Divinity School (MA); University of Birmingham (PhD); Ludwig Maximilians-Universität München (DTheol)

name: Alvin Plantinga
bio: Alvin Plantinga (born November 15, 1932) is the John A. O'Brien Professor Emeritus of Philosophy at the University of Notre Dame and was previously the William Harry Jellema Professor of Philosophy at Calvin College. A Reformed Christian philosopher, he is widely credited with leading the renaissance of analytic Christian philosophy in the latter half of the twentieth century. Plantinga's most influential work develops the "free will defense" against the logical problem of evil; advances Reformed epistemology, on which belief in God can be properly basic; and culminates in his Warrant trilogy, where he argues that Christian belief, if true, is warranted. His later book Where the Conflict Really Lies argues that the genuine conflict is between naturalism and science, not between Christianity and science.
education: Calvin College (AB); University of Michigan (MA); Yale University (PhD)

name: Os Guinness
bio: Os Guinness (born 1941 in Hsiang Cheng, China, the son of medical missionaries) is an English social critic, author, and Christian apologist who holds a doctorate from Oxford. A great-great-great-grandson of Arthur Guinness, the Dublin brewer, he was deeply shaped by his time at L'Abri Fellowship in Switzerland under Francis Schaeffer and has been a senior fellow at the Trinity Forum since the late 1980s. Guinness writes at the intersection of Christianity and the public square, addressing themes of vocation, freedom, religious liberty, and the cultural dynamics of late modern Western societies. His book The Call has become a classic on Christian vocation, and his more recent A Free People's Suicide and Last Call for Liberty argue that ordered liberty in the American republic depends on the moral and religious foundations its founders assumed.
education: University of London (BD); Oriel College, Oxford (DPhil)
tradition: Evangelical; shaped by Francis Schaeffer's L'Abri Fellowship
known_for: Writing The Call and dozens of books on vocation, freedom, and the crisis of the American republic, and articulating a Christian vision for public life in late modernity.
current_role: Author and social critic; co-founder and emeritus fellow, The Trinity Forum

faqs.a: Os Guinness (born 1941 in China to medical missionary parents) is an English author, social critic, and Christian apologist with a doctorate from Oxford. He co-founded The Trinity Forum in 1991 and has written or edited more than thirty-five books on faith, culture, and public life.

faqs.q: Is Os Guinness related to the Guinness brewing family?
faqs.a: Yes. He is a descendant of Arthur Guinness, the eighteenth-century Dublin brewer. His own branch of the family became known for missionary and philanthropic work, and Os was born in China where his parents served as medical missionaries.

faqs.q: What is Os Guinness known for?
faqs.a: Guinness is best known for The Call, a modern classic on Christian vocation, and for books such as Last Call for Liberty and A Free People's Suicide, which argue that American freedom depends on the moral and religious foundations assumed by its founders. In 2026 he received the William Wilberforce Award at the Colson Center National Conference.

Guinness was deeply influenced by his years at L'Abri Fellowship in Switzerland under Francis Schaeffer, as well as by sociologist Peter Berger's work on modernity. His writing combines Christian apologetics with social analysis of Western culture and the public square.

name: Greg Boyd
bio: Gregory A. Boyd (born June 2, 1957) is the senior pastor of Woodland Hills Church in St. Paul, Minnesota, and the founder and president of ReKnew, a ministry that engages questions of theology, suffering, nonviolence, and Christ-centered hermeneutics. He previously served as professor of theology at Bethel University for sixteen years. Boyd is one of the most prominent contemporary defenders of "open theism" (the view that the future is partly settled and partly open, even to God) and of a strong Christian pacifism. His two-volume Crucifixion of the Warrior God develops a cruciform hermeneutic for reading Old Testament violence in light of the cross, and his earlier The Myth of a Christian Nation argued—controversially—against the fusion of evangelical Christianity with American political identity.
affiliation: Woodland Hills Church, St. Paul, MN
education: University of Minnesota (BA); Yale Divinity School (MDiv); Princeton Theological Seminary (PhD)

name: Kevin Vanhoozer
bio: Kevin J. Vanhoozer (born 1957) is research professor of systematic theology at Trinity Evangelical Divinity School, where he holds the Research Professorship of Systematic Theology. He has previously taught at the University of Edinburgh, Trinity (where he held the Blanchard Chair) and Wheaton College Graduate School, and is one of the most influential contemporary evangelical voices on hermeneutics and theological method. Vanhoozer's work develops a "canonical-linguistic" theology—an approach that treats theology as an ongoing dramatic engagement with the canon of Scripture rather than primarily a system of propositions. His Is There a Meaning in This Text? and The Drama of Doctrine reframe debates about authorial intent, postmodern hermeneutics, and the role of doctrine in the church's life.
education: Westmont College (BA); Westminster Theological Seminary (MDiv); University of Cambridge (PhD)

name: Soong-Chan Rah
bio: Soong-Chan Rah is the Robert Boyd Munger Professor of Evangelism at Fuller Theological Seminary, a position he assumed in 2021. Previously he served for more than fifteen years as the Milton B. Engebretson Professor of Church Growth and Evangelism at North Park Theological Seminary in Chicago, and he was the founding senior pastor of the Cambridge Community Fellowship Church in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Rah is one of the most-read evangelical voices on race, the multi-ethnic church, and the recovery of biblical lament. His Prophetic Lament: A Call for Justice in Troubled Times reads the book of Lamentations as a needed corrective to American triumphalism, and his The Next Evangelicalism argues that the future of the church lies with the global majority and immigrant communities rather than with the Western white evangelical mainstream.
education: Columbia University (BA); Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary (MDiv, DMin); Harvard University (ThM); Duke University (ThD)

name: Denny Burk
bio: Denny Burk is professor of biblical studies and ethics at Boyce College, the undergraduate school of The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary, where he also directs the Center for Gospel and Culture. He serves as president of the Council on Biblical Manhood and Womanhood (CBMW) and is an associate pastor at Kenwood Baptist Church in Louisville, Kentucky. Burk writes on biblical interpretation, Christian ethics, biblical anthropology, and church-state issues from a complementarian and confessional Reformed Baptist perspective. His book What Is the Meaning of Sex? frames biblical sexual ethics around the telos of marriage, and his co-authored Transforming Homosexuality argues for the biblical possibility of change in same-sex desire.
affiliation: Boyce College / Council on Biblical Manhood and Womanhood
education: Criswell College (BA); The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary (MDiv, PhD)

name: Matthew Vines
bio: Matthew Vines is the founder and executive director of The Reformation Project, an organization that advocates for the inclusion of LGBTQ Christians in evangelical churches without rejecting biblical authority. He took a leave of absence from Harvard in 2010 to research the biblical texts on same-sex relationships, and a 2012 video of his talk "The Gay Debate: The Bible and Homosexuality" went viral on YouTube. Vines's 2014 book God and the Gay Christian became one of the most prominent examples of the "affirming" hermeneutic within the evangelical conversation about sexuality.
