His arguments have been answered in detail by complementarian scholars (e.g., the Southern Seminary volume God and the Gay Christian? edited by Albert Mohler), and Vines remains a central reference point in ongoing evangelical debates about marriage and sexuality.
role: Author & Founder of The Reformation Project

name: Thabiti Anyabwile
bio: Thabiti Anyabwile is a Reformed Baptist pastor and author who serves as senior pastor of Anacostia River Church in Washington, D.C., a congregation he helped plant in 2017 in partnership with Capitol Hill Baptist Church. A former Muslim, he previously served as senior pastor of First Baptist Church of Grand Cayman and was an assistant pastor at Capitol Hill Baptist under Mark Dever. Anyabwile is a council member with The Gospel Coalition and a longtime contributor to the 9Marks ministry. His writing engages the African-American church tradition, Reformed soteriology, and questions of racial reconciliation, justice, and complementarity in church life. Reviving the Black Church and The Faithful Preacher recover lessons from earlier black Reformed pastors for the present day.

name: Stanley Hauerwas
bio: Stanley Hauerwas (born July 24, 1940) is the Gilbert T. Rowe Professor Emeritus of Divinity and Law at Duke Divinity School, where he taught from 1984 until his retirement. He previously taught at the University of Notre Dame and was named "America's best theologian" by Time magazine in 2001. Although he comes from the Methodist tradition and is influenced by Mennonite ethics (especially John Howard Yoder), Hauerwas's communitarian and pacifist theology has shaped a wide swath of evangelical thinking about the church as polis, the formation of Christian character, and Christian witness in a post-Christendom culture. His co-authored Resident Aliens (with Will Willimon) is one of the most-read books on the post-Christendom church.
education: Southwestern University (BA); Yale Divinity School (BD); Yale University (MA, MPhil, PhD)

name: Paul Tripp
bio: Paul David Tripp is a pastor, author, and international conference speaker who is the founder and president of Paul Tripp Ministries. He has been a faculty member at the Christian Counseling and Educational Foundation (CCEF) and Westminster Theological Seminary, served as executive director of the Center for Pastoral Life and Care in Fort Worth, Texas, and is a current pastor at Tenth Presbyterian Church in Philadelphia. Tripp's ministry brings the daily relevance of the gospel into the routine of human life through writing, teaching, and speaking. His books on parenting (Age of Opportunity), marriage (What Did You Expect?), pastoral life (Dangerous Calling, Lead), and the Christian life (New Morning Mercies) have become widely-used resources for both individual readers and small groups within evangelical and Reformed congregations.
education: Columbia Bible College (BA); Reformed Episcopal Seminary (MDiv); Westminster Theological Seminary (DMin)

name: Barry York
bio: Barry York is a pastor and theological writer who has contributed to Reformed Christian publications and communities. He is known for his thoughtful engagement with Scripture and Reformed theology, offering insights for contemporary Christian living.

name: Kevin Bauder
bio: Kevin Bauder is a theologian and educator known for his work in fundamentalism and evangelical ecclesiology. As president of Central Baptist Theological Seminary, he has contributed significantly to contemporary discussions on Baptist identity, separation, and biblical Christianity.

name: Wendy Alsup
bio: Wendy Alsup is a Bible teacher and author who helps Christian women understand Scripture through a practical, theological lens. Her writing focuses on equipping believers to think deeply about their faith and apply biblical truth to everyday life.

books.title: Pray Big: Inviting God Into Your Greatest Dreams and Deepest Concerns
Is the Homosexual My Neighbor? Revised Edition
Missional Motherhood: The Everyday Ministry of Motherhood in the Grand Plan of God
Search the Scriptures Bible Study Series

name: Derek King
bio: Derek King is a thoughtful Christian writer and content curator with a passion for helping believers deepen their faith through quality resources. Based at Lewis House, Derek works to bring together meaningful Christian perspectives and biblical wisdom for contemporary audiences.

name: Luke Stamps
bio: Luke Stamps is a writer and theologian who engages contemporary culture through a Christian worldview. He contributes to various Christian publications and platforms, exploring themes of faith, theology, and cultural commentary.

name: Shane Morris
bio: Shane Morris is a writer and cultural commentator who explores the intersection of faith, culture, and contemporary issues from a Christian worldview perspective. He has contributed to various Christian publications and media platforms, helping audiences navigate cultural conversations through a biblical lens.
affiliation: BreakPoint, The Colson Center for Christian Worldview

name: Ryan Bangert
bio: Ryan Bangert is senior vice president for strategic initiatives and special counsel to the president at Alliance Defending Freedom, a Christian legal ministry defending religious liberty. A graduate of SMU's law school, he previously served in the Texas and Missouri attorney general offices, and writes on faith, law, and culture for outlets including the ERLC and American Reformer.

name: Lizzie Dearden
bio: Lizzie Dearden is a journalist and foreign correspondent known for her reporting on international security, terrorism, and religious extremism. Her investigative work has informed global conversations on complex geopolitical issues with careful attention to factual detail and human impact.

name: Nesrine Malik
bio: Nesrine Malik is a Sudanese-British journalist and commentator known for her incisive writing on politics, religion, and social issues. Her work often explores the intersection of faith, identity, and contemporary culture from a thoughtful, critical perspective.

books.title: We Need New Stories: Challenging the Toxic Myths Behind Our Age

name: Annie Linskey
bio: Annie Linskey is an investigative journalist known for her in-depth reporting on politics and social issues. While not primarily known as a Christian author, her work often explores themes relevant to faith communities, including issues of justice, accountability, and leadership.

name: Brett McCracken
bio: Brett McCracken is a writer and editor known for thoughtfully engaging contemporary culture from a Christian perspective. He explores how faith intersects with entertainment, technology, and modern life, helping Christians navigate cultural decisions with wisdom and discernment.

books.title: Uncomfortable: The Life and Times of William F. Buckley Jr.
Gray Matters: Navigating the Space Between Legalism and Liberty
Entertaining Ourselves to Death: How Television and Entertainment Values Are Reshaping Our Faith
The Revolt of the Elites: And the Betrayal of Democracy

name: Wesley Hill
bio: Wesley Hill is Associate Professor of New Testament at Western Theological Seminary and a leading evangelical voice on celibate gay Christian life. A founding contributor to the Spiritual Friendship project, he has written candidly about holding to a traditional Christian sexual ethic while also calling the church to richer practices of friendship, kinship, and belonging. His scholarly work centers on Pauline theology, particularly Trinitarian readings of Paul.
education: PhD in New Testament, Durham University

name: J.D. Greear
bio: J.D. Greear is the lead pastor of The Summit Church, a multi-site congregation in the Raleigh-Durham region of North Carolina, and served as president of the Southern Baptist Convention from 2018 to 2021. Under his leadership the Summit has emphasized church planting, sending out hundreds of pastors and missionaries. Greear writes and speaks frequently on the centrality of the gospel for Christian growth and on the recovery of Great Commission urgency in local churches.
education: PhD in Theology, Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary

books.title: Stop Asking Jesus Into Your Heart
What Are You Going to Do With Your Life?

name: Andreas Köstenberger
bio: Andreas Köstenberger is Research Professor of New Testament and Biblical Theology at Midwestern Baptist Theological Seminary and founder of Biblical Foundations. A prolific scholar in Johannine studies, biblical theology, and the doctrine of marriage and family, he has authored or edited more than fifty books and serves as editor of the Journal of the Evangelical Theological Society. His complementarian writing on family and his defense of the historic canon make him a frequently cited evangelical voice.
education: PhD in New Testament, Trinity Evangelical Divinity School

books.title: A Theology of John's Gospel and Letters
The Cradle, the Cross, and the Crown

name: O. Palmer Robertson
bio: O. Palmer Robertson is Director and Principal of African Bible University in Uganda and Professor Emeritus at Knox Theological Seminary, where he taught for many years. A Reformed covenant theologian, his book The Christ of the Covenants has shaped a generation of pastors' understanding of the unity of Scripture across both testaments. He has also written widely on prophetic literature, Israel and the church, and the wisdom books.

books.title: Understanding the Land of the Bible

known_for: The Christ of the Covenants, a standard text arguing that God's successive covenants form one unified plan of redemption culminating in Christ.
current_role: Founder of Consummation Ministries (since 2019); previously director and principal of African Bible University, Uganda (2004-2019)

faqs.a: O. Palmer Robertson (born 1937) is an American Reformed theologian and Old Testament scholar who taught at Reformed, Westminster, Covenant, and Knox seminaries and spent 27 years in Africa, including as director and principal of African Bible University in Uganda. He returned to the United States in 2019 and founded Consummation Ministries, where he continues to write.

faqs.q: What is O. Palmer Robertson known for?
faqs.a: He is best known for The Christ of the Covenants (1980), which traces the unity of God's covenants from creation to Christ and has shaped generations of pastors' covenant theology. Other works include The Israel of God, The Christ of the Prophets, and The Flow of the Psalms.

faqs.q: What is O. Palmer Robertson's view on Israel and the church?
faqs.a: Robertson argues in The Israel of God that the church is the continuation and fulfillment of God's covenant people rather than a parenthesis in God's plan for ethnic Israel. His covenantal reading stands in deliberate contrast to dispensationalist frameworks that keep Israel and the church on separate tracks.

faqs.q: Is O. Palmer Robertson still writing?
faqs.a: Yes. Through Consummation Ministries he has continued producing a multi-volume New Testament biblical theology, Christ of the Consummation, written from a redemptive-historical perspective.

name: Mark Vroegop
bio: Mark Vroegop is the lead pastor of College Park Church in Indianapolis and a frequent writer on the lost Christian practice of lament. His book Dark Clouds, Deep Mercy has helped pastors, counselors, and ordinary believers learn to bring grief honestly to God using the language of the Psalms and Lamentations. He also writes on racial reconciliation and on how lament can rebuild trust in fractured communities.

name: Robert Letham
bio: Robert Letham is Professor of Systematic and Historical Theology at Union School of Theology in Wales. A Welsh Presbyterian and one of the most respected Reformed systematicians of his generation, his work on the Trinity, union with Christ, and the Westminster Assembly is widely used in seminary classrooms across the Reformed world. His Systematic Theology is increasingly cited as a major contemporary contribution to evangelical dogmatics.

name: Stephen Wolfe
bio: Stephen Wolfe is a political theorist whose 2022 book The Case for Christian Nationalism became one of the most controversial evangelical publications of the decade, sparking widespread debate over the proper relationship between Christianity and civil government. Drawing on the Reformed natural-law and magisterial-Protestant tradition, Wolfe argues for a self-consciously Christian political order, a position critics from across the evangelical spectrum have engaged at length. He writes regularly on theology, politics, and culture.
education: PhD in Political Theory, Louisiana State University

name: Don Whitney
bio: Donald S. Whitney is Professor of Biblical Spirituality and Associate Dean at The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary, where he founded the Center for Biblical Spirituality. His Spiritual Disciplines for the Christian Life has become a modern evangelical classic on prayer, Bible intake, fasting, worship, and the historic means by which God forms believers. His shorter works on family worship and praying the Bible have shaped daily devotional life in countless evangelical homes.

books.title: Spiritual Disciplines for the Christian Life
Ten Questions to Diagnose Your Spiritual Health
How Can I Be Sure I'm a Christian?

name: Joel C. Rosenberg
bio: Joel C. Rosenberg is an evangelical author, geopolitical analyst, and founder of The Joshua Fund, a ministry that mobilizes prayer and humanitarian aid for Israel and her neighbors. A messianic believer, he has written more than twenty New York Times bestselling political thrillers and non-fiction works on Bible prophecy, the modern Middle East, and U.S.–Israel relations, and he interviews regional heads of state through his All Israel News and All Arab News platforms.
affiliation: The Joshua Fund / All Israel News

name: Paul Helm
bio: Paul Helm is a British philosopher of religion and one of the most sophisticated Reformed Calvin interpreters writing in English. He served for many years as J. I. Packer Professor of Theology and Philosophy at Regent College in Vancouver and previously taught philosophy at the University of Liverpool and King's College London. His writing on divine providence, eternity, and the philosophical theology of John Calvin has shaped contemporary Reformed engagement with analytic philosophy.

name: Tony Reinke
bio: Tony Reinke is a senior writer for Desiring God and host of the Ask Pastor John podcast. He writes at the intersection of theology, technology, and culture, urging believers to think Christianly about smartphones, social media, and the spectacle-driven attention economy. His book 12 Ways Your Phone Is Changing You has become a standard reference for Christians thinking about digital formation.
role: Author & Senior Writer at Desiring God

books.title: 12 Ways Your Phone Is Changing You
God, Technology, and the Christian Life

name: Jack Deere
bio: Jack Deere is a former cessationist professor of Old Testament at Dallas Theological Seminary who, after experiencing what he describes as a fresh encounter with the Spirit, became a leading evangelical voice for continuationism. His Surprised by the Power of the Spirit and Surprised by the Voice of God laid out a biblical case for the present-day operation of spiritual gifts. His memoir Even in Our Darkness recounts decades of personal grief alongside a continuing pursuit of Christ.

books.title: Surprised by the Power of the Spirit
Surprised by the Voice of God
Why I Am Still Surprised by the Power of the Spirit
The Beginner's Guide to the Gift of Prophecy

name: Ruth Haley Barton
bio: Ruth Haley Barton is the founding president of the Transforming Center, an evangelical ministry devoted to spiritual formation for pastors and leaders. Drawing on contemplative Christian streams while remaining rooted in evangelical convictions, she has written widely on solitude, silence, sabbath, and corporate discernment. Her work has helped many pastors recover sustainable rhythms of leadership grounded in their own life with God.
education: DMin in Spiritual Formation, Northern Baptist Seminary

books.title: Strengthening the Soul of Your Leadership
Embracing Rhythms of Work and Rest

denomination: Evangelical (interdenominational; formerly on staff at Willow Creek Community Church)
known_for: Bringing contemplative practices — solitude, silence, sabbath, discernment — into evangelical leadership culture through books like Sacred Rhythms and Strengthening the Soul of Your Leadership.
current_role: Founding president/CEO of the Transforming Center

faqs.a: Ruth Haley Barton is a spiritual director, teacher, and founding president of the Transforming Center, a ministry near Chicago devoted to the spiritual formation of pastors and Christian leaders. She previously served as associate director of spiritual formation at Willow Creek Community Church and trained at the Shalem Institute for Spiritual Formation.

The Transforming Center, founded by Barton in 2000, offers retreats and two-year 'Transforming Community' experiences that guide pastors and leaders through spiritual practices such as solitude, silence, sabbath, and communal discernment. It serves leaders from a wide range of denominations.

faqs.q: What books has Ruth Haley Barton written?
faqs.a: Her best-known books include Sacred Rhythms, Invitation to Solitude and Silence, Strengthening the Soul of Your Leadership, and Pursuing God's Will Together. They focus on sustainable rhythms of life with God for people in ministry leadership.

Yes, though she draws deeply from contemplative and monastic streams of the broader Christian tradition. Her work is sometimes questioned by evangelicals wary of contemplative spirituality, while many pastors credit it with saving their ministries from burnout.

name: John Ortberg
bio: John Ortberg is a popular evangelical author whose books on spiritual formation have sold millions of copies, drawing heavily on the work of his mentor Dallas Willard. He served for many years as senior pastor at Menlo Church before resigning in 2020 in connection with how the church handled an issue involving a family member; he has since launched the Become New teaching ministry. His writing on practical apprenticeship to Jesus remains widely read.
education: PhD in Clinical Psychology, Fuller Theological Seminary

books.title: If You Want to Walk on Water, You've Got to Get Out of the Boat
God Is Closer Than You Think

name: Adele Calhoun
bio: Adele Ahlberg Calhoun is a spiritual director, retreat leader, and pastor of spiritual formation at Highrock Church in Arlington, Massachusetts. Her Spiritual Disciplines Handbook catalogs more than fifty classical Christian practices and has become a standard reference in seminaries, churches, and small groups looking to recover historic disciplines for ordinary discipleship. She writes and teaches on identity, calling, and the formation of leaders.

name: Ken Shigematsu
bio: Ken Shigematsu is the senior pastor of Tenth Church in Vancouver, one of the largest churches in Canada, and an author known for integrating ancient monastic wisdom with everyday discipleship. His book God in My Everything proposes a personal rule of life as a framework for sustainable spiritual formation in busy modern lives. He writes regularly on identity, ambition, and the inner life of leaders.

name: Brian McLaren
bio: Brian McLaren is an author, speaker, and former pastor who became one of the central public faces of the early-2000s emergent church movement. Once identified as evangelical, he has since moved toward a self-described progressive and post-evangelical theology, calling for what he frames as a more generous, justice-oriented Christianity. His work continues to be cited as a touchstone in evangelical conversations about deconstruction, doctrinal boundaries, and the future of the faith.
education: MA in English, University of Maryland

books.title: We Make the Road by Walking

denomination: Formerly non-denominational evangelical; now identifies with progressive/post-evangelical Christianity
known_for: Being the leading voice of the early-2000s emergent church movement and, through books like A New Kind of Christian and A Generous Orthodoxy, of the shift toward progressive, post-evangelical Christianity.
current_role: Dean of Faculty at the Center for Action and Contemplation; author and speaker

faqs.a: Brian McLaren (born 1956) is an author, speaker, and former pastor of Cedar Ridge Community Church in Maryland. He became the central public face of the emergent church movement in the early 2000s and now serves as Dean of Faculty at Richard Rohr's Center for Action and Contemplation.

faqs.q: Is Brian McLaren still an evangelical?
faqs.a: No, not in the conventional sense. McLaren was once identified as evangelical but has moved to a self-described progressive, post-evangelical position, affirming same-sex relationships and questioning traditional teachings on hell, atonement, and biblical authority. Most mainstream evangelical leaders regard his later views as outside evangelical orthodoxy, and his books are frequently cited in evangelical discussions of 'deconstruction.'

faqs.q: What is Brian McLaren known for?
faqs.a: McLaren is best known for A New Kind of Christian (2001) and A Generous Orthodoxy (2004), which framed the emergent church conversation, and later works like The Great Spiritual Migration and Faith After Doubt. He has written more than 20 books on the future of Christianity.

faqs.q: What does Brian McLaren do at the Center for Action and Contemplation?
faqs.a: McLaren serves as Dean of Faculty at the Center for Action and Contemplation, the contemplative organization founded by Franciscan priest Richard Rohr in Albuquerque. He is core faculty of its Living School, writes for its Daily Meditations, and hosts the podcast Learning How to See.

name: Michael Frost
bio: Michael Frost is an Australian missiologist, vice principal of Morling College in Sydney, and one of the leading voices in the global missional church conversation. With Alan Hirsch he co-authored The Shaping of Things to Come, an influential argument for a more incarnational, sent-out posture for Western churches. His Surprise the World introduces the BELLS rhythm of mission as a simple framework for everyday witness in post-Christian contexts.
education: PhD in Theology, Australian College of Theology

books.title: The Shaping of Things to Come

name: Jonathan Wilson-Hartgrove
bio: Jonathan Wilson-Hartgrove is a writer, activist, and co-founder of the Rutba House, an intentional Christian community in Durham, North Carolina that helped shape the New Monasticism movement. He co-authored Common Prayer: A Liturgy for Ordinary Radicals with Shane Claiborne and Enuma Okoro. His later writing on race, Christian nationalism, and the recovery of a justice-shaped gospel has placed him at the intersection of evangelicalism and the broader American church.

name: Walter Brueggemann
bio: Walter Brueggemann is William Marcellus McPheeters Professor of Old Testament Emeritus at Columbia Theological Seminary and one of the most prolific and widely read Hebrew Bible scholars of the past half century. Though he writes from a mainline Protestant location, his Theology of the Old Testament, The Prophetic Imagination, and his work on the Psalms are widely used and engaged in evangelical seminaries, especially on lament, prophetic critique, and the practice of sabbath.

name: Robin Parry
bio: Robin Parry is a British theologian and longtime acquisitions editor at Wipf and Stock Publishers. Writing originally under the pen name Gregory MacDonald, his book The Evangelical Universalist sparked sustained debate within evangelicalism over hopeful universalism, the doctrine of hell, and the scope of final salvation. His later writing has covered Trinitarian worship, biblical lament, and the early-church reception of universalist hope.
education: PhD in Theology, University of Gloucestershire

name: Thomas Jay Oord
bio: Thomas Jay Oord is an American theologian and director of the doctoral program at Northwind Theological Seminary, working from a Wesleyan-Holiness background. He is one of the most prolific contemporary advocates for open and relational theology, arguing in The Uncontrolling Love of God and God Can't that divine love is essentially uncontrolling and incompatible with classical determinism. His work is regularly engaged — and contested — in evangelical debates over providence, evil, and divine power.
education: PhD in Religion, Claremont Graduate University
denomination: Wesleyan/Nazarene background (removed from ordained ministry in the Church of the Nazarene in 2024 over his LGBTQ+ advocacy)
tradition: Open and relational theology; Wesleyan-Holiness, process-influenced
known_for: Advocating 'open and relational theology' and the thesis of The Uncontrolling Love of God and God Can't — that God's love is inherently uncontrolling and God cannot unilaterally prevent evil.
current_role: Director of the doctoral program in Open and Relational Theology at Northwind Theological Seminary; director of the Center for Open and Relational Theology

faqs.q: What is Thomas Jay Oord's theology?
faqs.a: Oord is the leading contemporary advocate of open and relational theology, which holds that the future is genuinely open, that God experiences time with creatures, and that God's love is essentially uncontrolling. He coined the term 'amipotence' to describe divine power as the power of love rather than coercive omnipotence.

faqs.q: What denomination is Thomas Jay Oord?
faqs.a: Oord spent his career in the Church of the Nazarene, teaching sixteen years at Northwest Nazarene University. In July 2024 the denomination removed his ordination credentials after church proceedings related to his advocacy for LGBTQ+ inclusion, an outcome he has publicly discussed.

faqs.q: Is Thomas Jay Oord an evangelical?
faqs.a: Oord comes from the Wesleyan-Holiness wing of evangelicalism, but his signature positions — open theism, a God who 'can't' unilaterally stop evil, and LGBTQ+ affirmation — place him well outside the evangelical mainstream. Most evangelical theologians engage his work critically, and debates over open theism led to challenges to open theists' membership in the Evangelical Theological Society in the early 2000s.

faqs.q: What is Thomas Jay Oord known for writing?
faqs.a: His most influential books are The Uncontrolling Love of God (2015), God Can't (2019), and Open and Relational Theology (2021). He has authored or edited dozens of volumes and leads doctoral students at Northwind Theological Seminary, an online seminary.

name: Kristin Kobes Du Mez
bio: Kristin Kobes Du Mez is Professor of History at Calvin University and the author of the New York Times bestseller Jesus and John Wayne, a historical account of how white American evangelicals fused conservative politics, militant masculinity, and church culture across the twentieth century. The book has been a flashpoint in evangelical debates over abuse, power, and political identity. She writes a widely-read newsletter on religion, gender, and politics.
education: PhD in History, University of Notre Dame

name: Dominique DuBois Gilliard
bio: Dominique DuBois Gilliard serves as Director of Racial Righteousness and Reconciliation for the Evangelical Covenant Church and is a frequent voice on biblical justice, mass incarceration, and the church's racial witness. His Rethinking Incarceration applies a theological lens to the U.S. criminal-justice system, while Subversive Witness reads the privilege of biblical figures as a model for faithful contemporary advocacy.

name: Mika Edmondson
bio: Mika Edmondson is a Reformed pastor in the Presbyterian Church in America and a public theologian whose work brings together Reformed dogmatics, the Black church tradition, and a robust account of biblical justice. His book The Power of Unearned Suffering reads Martin Luther King Jr.'s theology of suffering through a Reformed lens. He speaks and writes regularly on race, ecclesiology, and the gospel's implications for public witness.
affiliation: City Church Atlanta (PCA) / Coalition for Christian Outreach
education: PhD in Systematic Theology, Calvin Theological Seminary

name: Brandon D. Crowe
bio: Brandon D. Crowe is a New Testament scholar and theologian who specializes in biblical studies and Christology. He is known for his thoughtful exploration of Scripture and its application to Christian faith and practice.

books.title: The Last Adam: A Theology of the Obedient Life of Jesus in the Gospels
Risen Lord: The Work of the Ascension and Exaltation of Jesus Christ

name: Daniel Guzmán
bio: Daniel Guzmán is a Christian writer and communicator dedicated to exploring faith, culture, and spiritual growth for contemporary audiences. His work focuses on helping believers navigate modern challenges through a biblical worldview.

name: Barry Waugh
bio: Barry Waugh is a Christian author and speaker dedicated to helping believers deepen their faith and biblical understanding. His writing focuses on practical application of Scripture and spiritual growth for modern Christians.

name: Michael Porter
bio: Michael Porter is a renowned business strategist and economist whose work on competitive advantage and industry analysis has influenced leaders across sectors worldwide. While not primarily known as a Christian author, his frameworks on purpose-driven strategy and organizational values resonate with Christian business leaders seeking to align profit with purpose.
education: Ph.D. in Business Economics, Harvard University

books.title: Competitive Advantage: Creating and Sustaining Superior Performance
The Five Competitive Forces That Shape Strategy

name: Marc Sims
bio: Marc Sims (MDiv, The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary; BA, Moody Bible Institute) is the preaching pastor of Quinault Baptist Church in Kennewick, Washington. A Reformed pastor, he writes on Bible, theology, and culture through his blog and Substack and contributes to The Gospel Coalition.

name: Kristian Andersen
bio: Kristian Andersen is a researcher and scientist who has contributed to discussions on faith, science, and origins within Christian communities. His work explores the intersection of scientific discovery and theological understanding, engaging thoughtfully with questions that matter to believers seeking to integrate faith with modern knowledge.

name: James Drimalla
bio: James Drimalla is a Christian author and speaker dedicated to helping believers grow in their faith and understanding of Scripture. His work focuses on practical spiritual growth and biblical teaching for modern Christians.

name: Megan Specia and Koba Ryckewaert
bio: Megan Specia and Koba Ryckewaert are journalists and reporters known for their work covering international news and humanitarian stories. Their reporting often explores the human dimension of global events, bringing attention to communities and voices that deserve Christian compassion and understanding.

name: John Eligon
bio: John Eligon is an award-winning journalist and author known for his thoughtful coverage of race, religion, and American culture. His work has appeared in major publications and explores the intersection of faith, identity, and contemporary social issues with nuance and compassion.

name: Golden Matonga and Matthew Mpoke Bigg
bio: Golden Matonga is a Malawian investigative journalist and director of investigations at the Platform for Investigative Journalism in Lilongwe; his reporting has appeared in the New York Times, the Financial Times, and the Mail & Guardian, and he has contributed to ICIJ investigations including the Pandora Papers. Matthew Mpoke Bigg is a New York Times journalist who has served as the paper's East Africa bureau chief in Nairobi.

name: E. J. Hutchinson
bio: E. J. Hutchinson is a scholar and writer focused on classical education, theology, and the intersection of faith and learning. His work emphasizes the importance of Christian intellectual formation and the study of ancient texts within a faith perspective.

books.title: Reading the Gospels Wisely: A Narrative and Theological Introduction

name: Keith Mathison
bio: Keith Mathison is a Reformed theologian and author known for his accessible writings on Christian doctrine and biblical interpretation. He has contributed significantly to contemporary Reformed theology through his books and articles, helping believers understand the foundations of their faith.
education: Master of Arts in Religion, Reformed Theological Seminary

books.title: The Shape of Things to Come: A Study of Systematic Eschatology
Given For You: Reclaiming Calvin's Doctrine of the Lord's Supper

name: Michael Hidalgo
bio: Michael Hidalgo is a pastor, author, and spiritual director who has dedicated his ministry to helping Christians integrate their faith into everyday life. He has served as a lead pastor and has written extensively on discipleship, spiritual formation, and living out biblical values in a secular culture. His work encourages believers toward deeper commitment to Christ and authentic Christian community.

name: Alyson Punzi
bio: Alyson Punzi (BA, Cedarville University) is the author of He Always Hears: A Story of Loss and the Hope of Things Made New, a picture book that teaches children to lament and rest on God's promises. Widowed when her pastor husband died suddenly of leukemia, she writes on grief, lament, and single motherhood for The Gospel Coalition and Risen Motherhood. She and her daughter live in small-town Ohio and belong to Grace Baptist Church.

name: Bekah McCallum
bio: Bekah McCallum is a Christian author and speaker passionate about helping women navigate faith, motherhood, and modern life with biblical wisdom. She writes thoughtfully about grace, discipleship, and the everyday challenges of following Jesus in contemporary culture.

name: Andrew Barber
bio: Andrew Barber (MDiv, Covenant Theological Seminary) is the English department chair at The Stony Brook School on Long Island and a regular contributor to The Gospel Coalition and Mere Orthodoxy. He writes primarily on film and culture from a Christian perspective, with work also appearing in Christianity Today.

name: Jim Tankersley
bio: Jim Tankersley is an economics reporter and columnist who brings thoughtful analysis to complex policy issues affecting American families. His work explores how economic decisions impact faith communities and everyday life, offering readers a Christian perspective on financial stewardship and social responsibility.

name: David Luhnow
bio: David Luhnow is a journalist and author known for his investigative reporting on Latin America and international affairs. While not primarily a Christian content creator, his work often explores themes of faith, culture, and social justice that resonate with thoughtful Christian readers.
affiliation: The Wall Street Journal, The New Yorker

name: Michael Schwirtz and Tomas Dapkus
bio: Michael Schwirtz and Tomas Dapkus are journalists who have reported extensively on religious freedom, persecution, and faith communities around the world. Their investigative work has brought important stories of Christian witness and resilience to global audiences through major publications.

name: Adam Gabbatt
bio: Adam Gabbatt is a journalist and reporter known for his work covering news and cultural issues with thoughtful analysis. He has contributed to major publication

name: Adam Kipp
bio: Adam Kipp is lead pastor of Living Hope Church in Gambrills, Maryland, which he joined in 2021 after twelve years of ministry at Mercy Hill in Charlotte. A graduate of the Sovereign Grace Pastors College, he earned his MDiv from The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary in 2018.

name: Blake Long
bio: Blake Long (MTS, Midwestern Baptist Theological Seminary) is the writer behind Theology & Life, a Reformed evangelical blog and newsletter he has published for several years. He is the author of 'Gospel Smugness' and 'Taking No for an Answer,' and serves as a small group leader at Sovereign Grace Bible Church.
known_for: Writing accessible Reformed devotional and theological content, including the books Gospel Smugness and Daily Calvinism.
current_role: Writer at Theology & Life; serves at a nonprofit organization

faqs.a: Blake Long is a Christian writer who runs the Theology & Life blog and newsletter. He earned a Master of Theological Studies in Preaching and Pastoral Ministry from Midwestern Baptist Theological Seminary and works at a philanthropic nonprofit while writing on theology and the Christian life.

Long is the author of Gospel Smugness, Taking No for an Answer, and Daily Calvinism. His articles have appeared at The Gospel Coalition, Challies.com, For the Church, 9Marks, and other Reformed evangelical outlets.
Yes. Long writes from a Reformed, Calvinistic perspective, reflected in works like Daily Calvinism, while emphasizing that sound doctrine should produce humility and love rather than pride.

name: Brittany Allen
bio: Brittany Allen is a writer and contributor to The Gospel Coalition who reflects candidly on grief, suffering, chronic illness, and motherhood in light of the gospel. Having written on miscarriage and loss, she seeks to offer biblical hope and comfort to those walking through hardship.

name: Jacob Crouch
bio: Jacob Crouch is a Christian writer whose essays on discipleship, worship, and everyday faithfulness appear at The Bee Hive, the writing ministry connected to New Life Bible Fellowship in Tucson, Arizona, and are regularly republished at The Aquila Report. His pieces address topics such as the fear of man, loneliness, and the ordinary rhythms of life in the local church.

name: Jessica Burke
bio: Jessica Burke is a writer and former public-school teacher who homeschools her five children in North Carolina, where her family helped plant their church. A regular contributor at Story Warren, her writing has also appeared at the ERLC, For The Church, and the CiRCE Institute.

name: Mathew Santhosh Thomas
bio: Dr. Mathew Santhosh Thomas is a physician who works part-time in a mission hospital and with the International Christian Medical and Dental Association. He contributes articles on faith, ministry, and parenting to The Gospel Coalition India, and lives in Kottayam, Kerala, with his wife, Saira.
known_for: Leading Emmanuel Hospital Association, a fellowship of Christian hospitals serving the poor across North and Central India.
current_role: Physician; serves part-time in mission hospital work and with the International Christian Medical and Dental Association (ICMDA)

faqs.a: Dr. Mathew Santhosh Thomas is an Indian physician and Christian healthcare leader based in New Delhi. He served in hospital leadership roles with Emmanuel Hospital Association from 1992, including as its Chief Functionary, and now works part-time in mission hospital settings and with the International Christian Medical and Dental Association.

Emmanuel Hospital Association (EHA) is a fellowship of Christian hospitals and community health programs in India that serves people regardless of race, caste, creed, or religion, with a focus on the poor and marginalized in North, North-East, and Central India. It carries out its work 'in the name and spirit of Jesus Christ.'

faqs.q: What does Mathew Santhosh Thomas write about?
faqs.a: He contributes articles to The Gospel Coalition India on topics such as serving Christ as a healthcare professional, navigating corruption with integrity, and durable Christian leadership. His writing draws on decades of experience in Indian medical missions.

name: Paul Levy
bio: Paul Levy is a thoughtful Christian writer and curator focused on biblical wisdom and spiritual formation. His work emphasizes the integration of faith with eve

name: RELEVANT
bio: RELEVANT is a magazine and media company covering faith, culture, and intentional living for Christians in their 20s and 30s. Founded in 2000 by Cameron Strang, the Florida-based publication produces articles, podcasts, and digital content exploring music, film, justice, and spiritual life, and staff-bylined pieces represent the collective work of its editorial team.

name: RELEVANT Staff
bio: RELEVANT Staff represents the editorial team at RELEVANT Magazine, a publication dedicated to equipping Christians to live out their faith in culture. The staff

name: Robert Mackey
bio: Robert Mackey is a writer and editor at The Guardian who previously spent years at The New York Times, where he anchored the paper's breaking-news blog The Lede, and later served as a senior writer at The Intercept. A Mirror Award winner, he specializes in making sense of world events through close reading of firsthand accounts, images, and video shared by witnesses.

name: Sarah Eekhoff Zylstra
bio: Sarah Eekhoff Zylstra is a senior writer at The Gospel Coalition, where she covers faith, culture, and the global church. She brings thoughtful analysis and rep

name: Beautiful Christian Life Staff
bio: The Beautiful Christian Life is a collaborative platform dedicated to sharing biblical wisdom, spiritual encouragement, and practical Christian living resources. Their team works together to curate and create content that helps believers grow deeper in their faith and understand Scripture more fully.

name: Mike McGarry
bio: Mike McGarry is an experienced educator and test prep specialist known for his work in helping students master standardized testing and academic skills. He brings a practical, accessible approach to complex subjects and has built a reputation for clear communication and student-centered instruction.

name: Rob Tervet
bio: Rob Tervet is a UK-based pastor who serves with Christ Community Church in Attleborough, Norfolk, part of the Relational Mission family of churches in the Newfrontiers stream. He is also a worship songwriter and has written for The Gospel Coalition on hope and the Christian life.

name: Omar Abdel-Baqui
bio: Omar Abdel-Baqui is a writer and content creator focused on Christian theology and apologetics. He engages with contemporary faith questions through a thoughtful, analytical lens.

name: Jenny Hietbrink
bio: Jenny Hietbrink is a Christian author and speaker dedicated to helping believers deepen their faith and understanding of Scripture. Through her writing and teaching, she encourages readers to encounter God's Word in fresh and transformative ways.

name: Stephen Spinnenweber
bio: Stephen Spinnenweber (MDiv, Greenville Presbyterian Theological Seminary) has served as pastor of Westminster Presbyterian Church (PCA) in Jacksonville, Florida, since 2019. A council member of the Gospel Reformation Network, he hosts podcasts on the Westminster Standards and writes on Reformed theology and the moral law.

name: Peter Mead
bio: Peter Mead is a Bible teacher and author known for his accessible approach to Scripture and pastoral insights. He has served in various ministry contexts and is recognized for his work helping Christians engage more deeply with God's Word through thoughtful exposition and application.
affiliation: Sola Network; Various churches and ministry organizations

books.title: Pleased to Dwell: Old Testament Meditations for New Testament Christians

name: Matt Boga
bio: Matt Boga is an associate pastor at Reality Church of Stockton in California and a student at Western Seminary. He writes for outlets including The Gospel Coalition and Modern Reformation, and blogs at The Drawing Board, reflecting on theology and the Christian life.

name: Skylar Spradlin
bio: Skylar Spradlin is the lead pastor of Trinity Baptist Church in Weatherford, Oklahoma, and has pursued an MDiv at The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary. He writes on pastoral ministry and the health of the local church for outlets such as For The Church and the Baptist Messenger of Oklahoma.

name: Betsy Childs Howard
bio: Betsy Childs Howard is a writer and editor who contributes regularly to The Gospel Coalition and other Christian publications. She explores themes of faith, family, and Christian living with thoughtfulness and grace, helping readers navigate their spiritual journeys with biblical wisdom.

name: Adrienne Matei
bio: Adrienne Matei is a writer and journalist who explores themes of faith, culture, and identity. Her work has appeared in various publications where she examines contemporary issues through thoughtful, nuanced perspectives.

name: Pragati K.B.
bio: Pragati K.B. is a reporter for The New York Times based in India, covering gender, labor, caste, culture, and their intersections. She trained in anthropology at the University of Oxford, journalism at the Asian College of Journalism in Chennai, and law at National Law University, Jodhpur, and her earlier bylines include The Hindu, The Caravan, and The Wire.

name: Vera Bergengruen
bio: Vera Bergengruen is a German-American author and journalist known for her thoughtful writing on faith, culture, and contemporary issues from a Christian perspective. Her work has appeared in major Christian and secular publications, where she explores the intersection of belief and modern life with nuance and insight.
affiliation: Christianity Today, The Atlantic, Religion News Service

name: Lyndon Jost
bio: Lyndon Jost (PhD, University of Toronto) is associate pastor of Christ Church Toronto (PCA) and director of the Reformed House of Studies at Wycliffe College, University of Toronto. He is the author of 'Transfiguring Headship: A Figural Theology of Gender' and contributes to The Gospel Coalition Canada.

name: Brian Pell
bio: Brian Pell (MA, Denver Seminary) is a pastor with Vintage Church in the Chapel Hill and Carrboro area of North Carolina, a congregation in the Acts 29 network. A graduate of Grove City College, he writes on Christianity, politics, and culture for outlets such as Mere Orthodoxy.

name: Brad Edwards
bio: Brad Edwards is a Christian author and speaker known for his work on biblical leadership and spiritual formation. He has contributed to various Christian publications and speaks at churches and conferences on topics related to faith, discipleship, and Christian living.

name: Caleb Cangelosi
bio: Caleb Cangelosi is the senior pastor of Pear Orchard Presbyterian Church (PCA) in Ridgeland, Mississippi, and the founder of Log College Press, a ministry recovering the writings of historic American Presbyterians. He contributes to Tabletalk and Ligonier Ministries and writes on Reformed theology and church history.

name: Tyler Hurst
bio: Tyler Hurst (PhD, The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary) is an associate pastor of Journey Church in Tucson, Arizona. He writes on theology, culture, and Christian formation, his essays and book reviews appear at The Gospel Coalition and the Ethics and Religious Liberty Commission, and he publishes a newsletter, The Musings of Tyler Hurst, on Substack.

name: Phil Cotnoir
bio: Phil Cotnoir is a Christian author and communicator dedicated to helping believers deepen their faith and understanding of Scripture. His work focuses on making biblical truth accessible and practical for modern Christians seeking spiritual growth.

name: William Boekestein
bio: William Boekestein is a Reformed pastor and author who has served churches in the evangelical tradition while contributing to Christian publishing. He brings theological depth and pastoral wisdom to his writing on faith, Scripture, and Christian living.
affiliation: Reformation Heritage Books; Christ Covenant Church

books.title: Comfort in Sorrow: The Psalms of Lament
Day by Day in God's Kingdom

name: Elisabetta Povoledo
bio: Elisabetta Povoledo is a journalist and Rome correspondent known for her coverage of Vatican affairs and religious news for major international publications. Her reporting offers insights into the Catholic Church's activities, papal developments, and the intersection of faith and culture in contemporary society.
known_for: Decades of reporting on Italy, the Vatican, and the Catholic Church for The New York Times.
current_role: Reporter, The New York Times, based in Rome, covering Italy and the Vatican

faqs.a: Elisabetta Povoledo is a Rome-based reporter for The New York Times who has covered Italy and the Vatican for decades, including papal transitions, Vatican documents, and Italian culture.

faqs.q: Is Elisabetta Povoledo a Christian author?
faqs.a: No. Povoledo is a mainstream news journalist covering the Vatican as a beat, and her public work does not indicate a personal religious affiliation. Her byline appears in Christian news digests because of her coverage of the Catholic Church.
She covers the Vatican, the papacy, and Italian news and culture from Rome, reporting on events such as papal elections and major decisions of the Catholic Church.

name: Lara Seligman
bio: Lara Seligman is a national security correspondent and journalist who covers defense, military affairs, and foreign policy. While not primarily known as a Christian content creator, her reporting often touches on faith-based perspectives in global affairs and humanitarian contexts.

name: Mia Staub
bio: Mia Staub is senior editorial project manager at Christianity Today, where she helps coordinate the magazine's editorial operations and contributes reporting, reviews, and newsletter writing. Based in Los Angeles, she is pursuing a master's degree in theology of public life and justice through Princeton Theological Seminary.

name: Kendall Lankford
bio: Kendall Lankford is a Reformed pastor and church planter who serves as lead pastor of The Shepherd's Church in Massachusetts. A biblical counselor, he hosts The PRODCAST and writes and speaks on theology, discipleship, and cultural engagement from a confessionally Reformed perspective.

name: Chandler Vannoy
bio: Chandler Vannoy is a pastor and podcaster who co-hosts the Unseen Leadership Podcast, featuring conversations with church leaders on ministry and leadership. He writes on Scripture and the Christian life at his personal site.

name: Daniel Nealon
bio: Daniel Nealon (ThM, Vanderbilt University) is senior pastor of Deer Creek Church (PCA) in Littleton, Colorado, and author of the Deer Creek Catechism. He contributes to reformation21, writing on Reformed theology and current issues facing the church.

name: Christina Fox
bio: Christina Fox is a writer and speaker who addresses faith, family, and the Christian life with warmth and biblical insight. She contributes to various Christian publications and platforms, helping readers navigate motherhood, marriage, and spiritual growth from a Reformed perspective.

books.title: Risen Motherhood: Gospel Hope for the Daily Grind
A Holy Calling: Sanctification for Stay-at-Home Moms
Journeying Through Proverbs: A 31-Day Journey with God's Wisdom

name: Wil Moore
bio: Wil Moore serves at Long Hollow Baptist Church in Hendersonville, Tennessee, where he has led both student ministry and men's ministry, building a relational approach to discipling men around connection, community, and content. A graduate of The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary, he speaks for Student Leadership University and writes on men's discipleship for outlets including Lifeway.

name: Joe Carter
bio: Joe Carter is a senior editor at The Gospel Coalition and a prolific Christian writer and editor known for making complex theological and cultural topics accessible to evangelical audiences. With a background in journalism and ministry, he brings both analytical rigor and pastoral concern to issues at the intersection of faith, culture, and public life.
education: Master of Arts in Theological Studies, Southern Baptist Theological Seminary

books.title: How to Argue Like Jesus: Learning Persuasion from History's Greatest Communicator
The Unspoken Rules of Evangelical Christianity

name: Paul Vieira
bio: Paul Vieira is a reporter in The Wall Street Journal's Canada bureau, based in Ottawa, where he covers the Canadian economy, trade, energy policy, and cross-border relations with the United States. A journalism graduate of Ryerson University in Toronto, he previously reported on business and finance for the National Post and The Globe and Mail.

name: Robbie Gramer
bio: Robbie Gramer is a journalist and foreign policy correspondent known for his reporting on international affairs and geopolitical issues. While his primary work focuses on secular news outlets, his analytical approach to global events and ethical journalism reflects values that resonate with thoughtful Christian readers interested in understanding world events through a principled lens.

name: Lynsey Chutel and Claire Moses
bio: Lynsey Chutel is an award-winning journalist covering African affairs and global development, while Claire Moses is a culture reporter and writer. Together and individually, they have contributed thoughtful reporting on social issues, human interest stories, and cultural trends to major publications.

name: David E. Sanger
bio: David E. Sanger is a renowned national security correspondent and bestselling author who has spent decades investigating complex geopolitical issues affecting America and the world. His meticulously researched works examine the intersection of technology, politics, and global power dynamics with clarity and insight. For Christian readers interested in understanding contemporary world events through an informed journalistic lens, Sanger's analyses provide valuable context for informed citizenship and prayer.

books.title: The Perfect Weapon: War, Sabotage, and Fear in the Cyber Age
Confront and Conceal: Obama's Secret Wars and Surprising Use of American Power
The Madman in the Middle: Trump, Iran, and the End of the Nuclear Deal
New Cold Wars: China's Rise, Russia's Invasion, and America's Struggle to Defend the West

known_for: Four decades of national security reporting, three Pulitzer Prize-winning teams, and bestselling books including New Cold Wars.
current_role: White House and National Security Correspondent, The New York Times

faqs.a: David E. Sanger is a White House and national security correspondent for The New York Times, where he has reported for more than four decades and contributed to three Pulitzer Prize-winning teams. He revealed the 'Olympic Games' Stuxnet cyberattack on Iran's nuclear program.

faqs.q: What books has David Sanger written?
faqs.a: His books include New Cold Wars: China's Rise, Russia's Invasion and America's Struggle to Defend the West (2024), The Perfect Weapon (2018), Confront and Conceal (2012), and The Inheritance (2009), several of which were New York Times bestsellers.

faqs.q: Is David Sanger a Christian author?
faqs.a: No. Sanger is a mainstream national security journalist, and his work does not address religion or indicate a religious affiliation. His reporting is sometimes shared in Christian publications for its analysis of world events relevant to informed citizenship.

name: Dean Davis
bio: Dean Davis is a respected Christian author and theologian known for his clear, accessible writing on biblical topics and Christian living. His work emphasizes biblical faithfulness and practical application of Scripture for modern believers.

name: Christopher Cook
bio: Christopher Cook is a writer and Christian thought leader who contributes to various faith-based publications and platforms. His work engages contemporary issues through a biblical lens, offering thoughtful perspective for modern Christian audiences.

name: Bruce Henning
bio: Bruce Henning is a Christian author and speaker dedicated to helping believers deepen their faith and understanding of Scripture. His work focuses on practical Christian living and spiritual growth for contemporary audiences.

name: Jackie Gibson
bio: Jackie Gibson is an author who serves alongside her husband, Jonathan Gibson, at Westminster Theological Seminary in Philadelphia. A mother of four, she wrote 'You Are Still a Mother: Hope for Women Grieving a Stillbirth or Miscarriage' out of her own experience of loss, offering comfort rooted in the gospel.

name: Scott Yenor
bio: Scott Yenor is a political philosopher and professor who writes thoughtfully about family, culture, and political order from a Christian perspective. His work examines how faith and traditional values intersect with contemporary social and political challenges.
affiliation: Boise State University; The American Conservative; Public Discourse
education: Ph.D. in Government, Claremont Graduate University

books.title: Family and the Politics of Modernity

name: Ramon Presson
bio: Ramon Presson is a licensed marriage and family therapist and author who writes about relationships, faith, and personal growth from a Christian perspective. His work helps couples and families navigate life's challenges through practical wisdom rooted in biblical principles.

books.title: Fail Together: How to strengthen your relationship when life gets messy
The Relational Soul: Moving from False Self to Authentic Self

name: James T. Areddy
bio: James T. Areddy is a journalist and writer known for his reporting on economics, business, and cultural trends. His work appears in major publications where he brings thoughtful analysis to contemporary issues affecting society and faith communities.

name: Scott McClellan
bio: Scott McClellan is a former White House Press Secretary and author who has written extensively about his experiences in government and his spiritual journey. His work offers insights into faith, integrity, and redemption from a uniquely informed perspective.

books.title: What Happened: Inside the Bush White House and Washington's Culture of Deception

name: Audrey Finken
bio: Audrey Finken is a writer and book reviewer who contributes to The Gospel Coalition, engaging readers with thoughtful reflections on prayer, theology, and the Christian life. She is a member of Bethel Baptist Church in Quebec, Canada.

name: Emily Van Dixhoorn
bio: Emily Van Dixhoorn is a scholar and writer focused on Reformed theology and church history. She brings academic rigor to exploring the depths of Christian doctrine and its practical implications for modern believers.

name: Bob Stevenson
bio: Bob Stevenson serves as lead pastor of Village Baptist Church in Aurora, Illinois, and writes for outlets including The Gospel Coalition and Mere Orthodoxy. He holds an MDiv from Trinity Evangelical Divinity School and has pursued graduate study in sociology at Loyola University Chicago. He and his wife are parents of four.

name: Jordan B. Cooper
bio: Jordan B. Cooper is a Lutheran pastor and theological writer known for his thoughtful engagement with contemporary Christian issues and classical Christian theology. Through his writing and ministry, he seeks to help believers understand their faith more deeply and live out their convictions with integrity in a changing culture.

name: Lauren Washer
bio: Lauren Washer is a writer whose work appears at The Gospel Coalition and Risen Motherhood, where she reflects on faith, motherhood, and everyday discipleship. She serves in women's ministry at Trinity Presbyterian Church (PCA) in Norfolk, Virginia.

name: Pete Hurst
bio: Kerry W. 'Pete' Hurst is a Reformed pastor and a graduate of King College and Reformed Theological Seminary. He served as senior pastor of Calvary Reformed Presbyterian Church in Hampton, Virginia, for 28 years and ministered in the PCA for over four decades before transferring to the OPC; he writes at his blog 'God's Fool.'

name: Bill Peacock
bio: Bill Peacock is a Christian writer and policy analyst who has contributed to conversations about faith, culture, and public issues. His work engages readers with thoughtful perspectives on how Christian values intersect with contemporary society.

name: Britta Lokting
bio: Britta Lokting is a writer and content creator focused on Christian living and faith development. Her work encourages readers to deepen their relationship with God through practical, biblically-grounded insights.

name: John Yoon and Muktita Suhartono
bio: John Yoon and Muktita Suhartono are journalists and writers who have contributed to major Christian and mainstream publications covering faith, culture, and social issues. Their work explores the intersection of Christianity with contemporary life and global perspectives.

name: Stephen Bates
bio: Stephen Bates is a British author and journalist who has written extensively on religion, culture, and social issues from a thoughtful Christian perspective. His work examines the intersection of faith and contemporary society with both critical insight and pastoral sensitivity.

books.title: A Church at War: Anglicans and Homosexuality
Battleground Britain: The New Political Conflict

name: Julie Smyth
bio: Julie Smyth is a freelance journalist whose reporting on faith, life, and culture has appeared in evangelical outlets including Christianity Today and WORLD. Her stories range from profiles of pro-life ministry and a former Planned Parenthood director's change of heart to features on discipleship and the faith journeys of Christians around the world.

name: Cameron Cole
bio: Cameron Cole is a pastor and author dedicated to helping young people understand their identity and purpose in Christ. He has worked extensively in youth ministry and discipleship, addressing topics like faith, identity, and spiritual growth for emerging generations.

books.title: Therefore I Have Hope: 12 Reasons Faith Makes Sense
The Story Formed Life: How the Bible Shapes Identity and Purpose
Created for Purpose: Discovering Why You Matter in God's Grand Story

name: Anna Meade Harris
bio: Anna Meade Harris is a writer and content creator focused on Christian living and spiritual formation. Her work explores faith, discipleship, and the practical application of Scripture to everyday life. She contributes to various Christian publications and platforms seeking to help believers grow deeper in their relationship with Christ.

name: Danny Kwon
bio: Danny Kwon is a pastor and Christian communicator dedicated to helping believers grow in their faith and understanding of Scripture. Through his teaching and writing, he seeks to make biblical truths accessible and transformative for modern audiences.

name: Isaiah Marshall
bio: Isaiah Marshall is an evangelical spoken word artist, author, and speaker who communicates the gospel through creative arts. He serves as Director of Ministry Development for Rooted Ministry and has been a chaplain in the Air Force Reserve for over a decade. He wrote 'Identity Theft: Reclaiming the Truth in the Midst of Lies' and hosts the 'Front Runner' podcast.

name: Chelsea Kingston Erickson
bio: Chelsea Kingston Erickson is a Christian author and speaker who writes about faith, discipleship, and spiritual growth. Her work encourages believers to deepen their relationship with Christ and live out their faith authentically in everyday life.

name: FM AI
bio: FM AI is an artificial intelligence assistant designed to help Christian content creators, researchers, and readers engage with Scripture and faith-based material. While not a human author, FM AI serves as a helpful tool for those seeking to deepen their understanding of Christian theology, biblical study, and spiritual growth.

name: Al Gooderham
bio: Al Gooderham is a pastor at Grace Church in Doncaster, England, where he preaches and writes on discipleship, church planting, and living wholeheartedly for Jesus. He blogs regularly on ministry and Bible exposition and contributes resources to 20schemes Equip.

name: Stephen Unthank
bio: Stephen Unthank (MDiv, Capital Bible Seminary) serves at Greenbelt Baptist Church in Greenbelt, Maryland, just outside Washington, DC. He teaches Bibliology and hermeneutics at Rockbridge Classical Christian Academy and theology at Faith Theological Seminary, and he is a regular contributor to Reformation21 and Place for Truth. He lives in Maryland with his wife and two children.

name: Jim Newheiser
bio: Jim Newheiser is a pastor and biblical counselor who has devoted his ministry to helping Christians find practical wisdom from Scripture for life's deepest struggles. He is known for his accessible teaching on biblical counseling and his commitment to equipping the church with Christ-centered approaches to personal transformation.
affiliation: Grace Church of the Valleys (Santa Clarita, CA)

books.title: Putting On Christ: Genuine Transformation in Everyday Life
When Sinners Say 'I Do': Discovering the Power of the Gospel for Marriage

name: Chase Krug
bio: Chase Krug (PhD, Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary) is lead pastor of New Century Church in Roanoke, Virginia. He writes on marriage, purity, and Christian formation for publications including Mere Orthodoxy and Modern Reformation, with essays exploring how marriage points to Christ and the church and why sexual purity must be personal rather than merely legalistic. He and his wife have two children.

name: Ronald Dodson
bio: Ronald Dodson is a Christian author and educator dedicated to helping believers grow in their faith and understanding of Scripture. Through his writings and teachings, he encourages readers to deepen their relationship with Christ and apply biblical principles to everyday life.

name: Catherine Porter and Ana Castelain
bio: Catherine Porter and Ana Castelain are collaborators known for their work in Christian content and spiritual formation. Together they have contributed to resources designed to deepen faith and encourage spiritual growth among believers.

name: Dasl Yoon
bio: Dasl Yoon is a writer and content creator focused on Christian faith and cultural engagement. His work explores how believers can thoughtfully navigate contemporary issues through a biblical lens.

name: Milan Czerny
bio: Milan Czerny is a Jesuit priest and Vatican official known for his work on social justice, immigration, and indigenous rights within the Catholic Church. He has served as a consultor to various papal departments and is recognized for his advocacy on behalf of marginalized communities.

name: Paul Ritchie
bio: Paul Ritchie is pastor of Limerick Baptist Church in Ireland. Originally from Dublin, he is a Christian Focus author whose preaching and writing—including expositions through books such as Numbers—are shaped by his own experience of OCD and anxiety, giving his ministry a particular tenderness toward strugglers. His sermons and articles are regularly shared through The Aquila Report.

name: Daniel Bouchoc and Zach Hollifield
bio: Daniel Bouchoc and Zach Hollifield are Christian content creators and communicators dedicated to helping believers engage with Scripture and faith in meaningful ways. Together, they work to produce resources that encourage spiritual growth and deeper understanding of God's Word for contemporary audiences.

name: Scott Klusendorf
bio: Scott Klusendorf is a leading pro-life apologist and founder of The Case for Life, dedicated to equipping Christians with thoughtful arguments for the sanctity of human life. He has spent decades training students, church leaders, and everyday believers to engage respectfully in conversations about abortion, drawing on both philosophical reasoning and biblical conviction.
education: M.A. in Christian Apologetics, Biola University

books.title: The Case for Life: Equipping Christians to Engage the Culture
How to Use the Tools of Pro-Life Apologetics

name: Chris Buckley
bio: Chris Buckley is the chief China correspondent for The New York Times, reporting on China and Taiwan from Taipei. Raised in Sydney, he holds a doctorate in Chinese studies from the Australian National University and spent seven years as a senior Reuters correspondent in Beijing. He was a finalist for the 2020 Pulitzer Prize for reporting on Xinjiang and received the 2024 Shorenstein Journalism Award.

name: Ramon Antonio Vargas
bio: Ramon Antonio Vargas is a religion reporter and journalist who covers faith communities and Christian perspectives for major publications. His reporting focuses on how religious traditions engage with contemporary social and cultural issues.
affiliation: Religion journalist; contributions to major news outlets

name: Lily Kuo
bio: Lily Kuo is a journalist and reporter known for her international coverage and investigative work. While primarily known for secular journalism, her reporting often touches on themes of faith, culture, and human rights that resonate with Christian audiences seeking thoughtful, fact-based news analysis.

name: Sune Engel Rasmussen
bio: Sune Engel Rasmussen is a Danish-Icelandic journalist and author known for his investigative reporting on conflict, religion, and geopolitics, particularly in Afghanistan and the Middle East. His work explores the intersection of faith, politics, and human resilience in regions marked by religious complexity. Through his journalism and writing, Rasmussen brings nuanced Christian perspectives to understanding global conflict and cultural identity.
affiliation: The Guardian, The New York Times

books.title: The Faithful Spy: Dietrich Bonhoeffer and the Plot to Kill Hitler

name: Walter Shaw
bio: Walter Shaw is a pastor at Citylight Church in the Manayunk neighborhood of Philadelphia, an Acts 29 congregation. Trained at Westminster Theological Seminary, he serves through preaching, small-group leadership, and writing for his church on grace, grief, and the hope of Christ.

name: Samuel G. Parkison
bio: Samuel G. Parkison is a writer and editor known for his work in Christian apologetics and biblical theology. He has contributed to various Christian publications and platforms, helping readers understand and defend the Christian faith in contemporary contexts.

name: Brian Croft
bio: Brian Croft is a pastor and author dedicated to equipping church leaders and churches with biblical wisdom for ministry. Through his writing and speaking, Croft encourages believers to pursue authentic Christian community and Christ-centered pastoral ministry.

A Wheaton College graduate, she serves in premarital mentoring and marriage ministry at The Austin Stone Community Church in Austin, Texas, where she lives with her four young children. Her writing covers women's Bible study, generational issues, and family discipleship.

name: Erica L. Green

name: D.V. Rider

Through writing and teaching, Rider seeks to help readers deepen their understanding of Scripture and apply Christian principles to everyday challenges.

name: Dan Jarms
bio: Dan Jarms is a pastor and author who focuses on helping Christians develop a deeper understanding of Scripture and apply biblical principles to their daily lives. He is known for his clear, accessible teaching style that makes complex theological concepts relatable to modern audiences.

name: Rosaria Butterfield

She writes thoughtfully about faith, sexuality, hospitality, and the power of the gospel to change lives, speaking from personal experience and deep theological conviction.

bio: Cassie Achermann is a writer and content creator focused on helping Christians navigate faith, family, and modern life. Through her writing and online presence, she shares biblical insights and practical wisdom with a warm, relatable approach.

Our team of writers, editors, and contributors work together to bring you thoughtful, biblically-grounded resources designed to deepen your faith and understanding of Scripture.

name: Aie Balagtas See and Jes Aznar

name: Cath Clarke

name: Jared Malsin
bio: Jared Malsin is an international correspondent and journalist who has reported extensively from the Middle East and North Africa, covering stories of faith, conflict, and human resilience. His work has appeared in major publications and brings thoughtful Christian perspective to global events affecting believers in volatile regions.

name: Dr Lucien Tuinstra
bio: Dr Lucien Tuinstra is a thoughtful Christian thinker and writer who engages with contemporary theological and spiritual themes for modern believers. His work encourages readers to deepen their faith through careful reflection and biblical engagement.

name: Kyle Cravens

name: Edward Song
bio: Edward Song is a thoughtful voice in contemporary Christian writing and ministry. His work explores faith, discipleship, and the intersection of Christian conviction with modern life.

name: David S. Cloud
bio: David S. Cloud is a Christian author, researcher, and editor known for his detailed studies of Bible translations, historical Christian figures, and contemporary Christian issues. books.title: The History of the New King James Version
A Testimony of the Lord's Dealing

name: Joseph Minich
bio: Joseph Minich is a Christian writer and thinker who engages contemporary culture, theology, and philosophy from a reformed perspective. His work explores the intersection of faith, politics, and cultural formation for modern believers.

books.title: The Façade: A Diagnosis of American Christianity

name: Erica Roth
bio: Erica Roth is a writer and content creator focused on Christian living and faith topics. She contributes to various Christian publications and platforms, helping readers deepen their spiritual understanding and practice.

name: Dawn Sherill-Porter
bio: Dawn Sherill-Porter is a Christian author and speaker dedicated to equipping believers with practical faith-based guidance. Her writing focuses on spiritual growth, encouragement, and helping readers deepen their relationship with Christ.

name: Michael Graham
bio: Michael Graham is a respected voice in Christian media and commentary, known for his thoughtful analysis of faith, culture, and current events from a biblical perspective. He brings years of experience in Christian journalism and content creation to help readers understand how Scripture speaks to contemporary issues.

name: Rowena Mason Whitehall
bio: Rowena Mason Whitehall is an editor and content curator dedicated to amplifying Christian voices and perspectives. With a focus on editorial excellence, she works to make faith-based content accessible and meaningful to modern audiences.

name: Damian Paletta

books.title: The Wager: Reagan, Thatcher, and the First Great Clash of the Conservative Revolution

name: Brian Spegele
bio: Brian Spegele is a writer and content creator focused on Christian living and faith development. He contributes to various Christian publications and platforms, helping readers deepen their understanding of Scripture and apply biblical principles to daily life.

name: John Brown of Wamphray

Though he lived through significant religious and political upheaval, he remained devoted to Reformed theology and the advancement of biblical Christianity in his congregation.

name: Guy Waters
bio: Guy Waters is a Reformed theologian and pastor known for his scholarly yet accessible writing on biblical interpretation, systematic theology, and Christian living. name: Abraham Cho

name: Stephen Eide

books.title: The Beautiful Community: Unity, Diversity, and the Church at Its Best

name: George Robertson
bio: George Robertson is a Christian author and speaker known for his work in biblical teaching and spiritual formation. His writings encourage believers to deepen their faith and apply scriptural principles to everyday life.

name: Colin Redemer

A Protestant writer on ethics, technology, and classical education, he has contributed to First Things, Mere Orthodoxy, and Ad Fontes Journal and authored 'Made Like the Maker.'

name: Justine Coleman
bio: Justine Coleman is a journalist and political correspondent who brings thoughtful, fact-based reporting to contemporary issues. While not primarily known as a Christian author, her work often intersects with values-based coverage relevant to faith communities.

Through his site he offers Bible teaching alongside audio production, and his teaching content has aired on Christian radio outlets.

name: Andrew E. Kramer
bio: Andrew E. Kramer is a Christian author and theological writer dedicated to exploring biblical themes and their practical application in contemporary faith. His work engages evangelical audiences with thoughtful analysis of Scripture and Christian living.

name: Luke Broadwater
bio: Luke Broadwater is an investigative journalist who has covered politics, government accountability, and significant national events for major publications. While primarily known for his political reporting, his work often intersects with issues of ethics, integrity, and leadership that resonate with Christian audiences interested in cultural and civic matters.

name: Todd Johnson
bio: Todd Johnson is a respected voice in Christian content and apologetics, known for his thoughtful exploration of faith, culture, and biblical truth. He engages contemporary questions through a distinctly Christian worldview, helping believers think deeply about their convictions.

name: Jeremy Linneman
bio: Jeremy Linneman is a pastor and Christian writer committed to helping believers understand and live out their faith in practical ways. He brings biblical insight and pastoral experience to topics affecting modern Christian living and spiritual growth.

name: Jim McCarthy
bio: Jim (James G.) McCarthy is an evangelical author and evangelist who came to faith out of a Roman Catholic background and founded Good News for Catholics. He is best known for 'The Gospel According to Rome,' which compares Catholic tradition with Scripture, along with the video 'Catholicism: Crisis of Faith.' A former missionary to Ireland, he writes on the gospel and evangelism.

name: Paul Worcester

name: Thaddeus Williams

bio: Matthew Mpoke Bigg is a scholar of biblical theology and ancient Christianity, while Apoorva Mandavilli is a science journalist. name: Mark J. Henninger

name: Yan Zhuang
bio: Yan Zhuang is a writer and speaker who engages with contemporary issues through a Christian worldview. Her work explores faith, culture, and spirituality for modern audiences seeking thoughtful Christian perspective.

name: Temujin Doran and Katie Arnold
bio: Temujin Doran and Katie Arnold are voices in Christian content and commentary, engaging audiences on faith, culture, and contemporary issues from a biblical perspective. They contribute to Christian discourse through various media platforms and publications.
