known_for: Reporting on immigration, Latin America, and the U.S. Latino community for HuffPost.
current_role: National Reporter, HuffPost (based in Austin), covering immigration and voting rights

faqs.a: Roque Planas is a national reporter for HuffPost based in Austin, Texas, covering immigration and voting rights. He co-founded the Latin America News Dispatch, holds a journalism master's from NYU, and previously worked at the New York Daily News and Fox News Latino.

faqs.q: What does 'Roque Planas and agencies' mean?
faqs.a: This byline indicates an article written by Planas with additional material from wire services such as the Associated Press or Reuters. It is a common newsroom convention for stories combining original reporting with agency copy.

faqs.q: Is Roque Planas a Christian author?
faqs.a: No. Planas is a mainstream news journalist covering immigration and Latin America, and his public work does not indicate a religious affiliation. His stories occasionally intersect with faith communities through coverage of immigration and Latino life.

name: Ivan Nechepurenko and Mary Gelman
bio: Ivan Nechepurenko and Mary Gelman are journalists and writers who have contributed to major international publications covering Eastern European affairs and cultural topics. Their reporting and writing reflect a commitment to honest storytelling and in-depth analysis of complex geopolitical and social issues.

name: Winfree Brisley
bio: Winfree Brisley is an editor for The Gospel Coalition and a graduate of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. She is coauthor of 'Turn Your Eyes: A Bible Study on the Psalms' and has edited devotional resources including 'Strong in the Lord.' She lives in North Carolina with her husband and their three sons, where they are members of Uptown Church.

name: Darryl Dash
bio: Darryl Dash is a pastor, author, and speaker known for helping churches and Christian leaders navigate practical ministry challenges with biblical wisdom. He has served in pastoral ministry for decades and shares insights on leadership, faith, and Christian living through various platforms. His work encourages believers to think deeply about their faith and its application to everyday life.

books.title: Do Better: A Guide to Growing as a Leader
Laughing at the Devil: Exposing the Enemy's Lies

name: Erik Coonce
bio: Erik Coonce is a Christian communicator and content creator dedicated to helping believers engage their faith in meaningful ways. His work focuses on discipleship, biblical teaching, and practical Christian living for contemporary audiences.

name: Brad Wetherell
bio: Brad Wetherell is a Christian author and communicator passionate about helping believers grow in their faith and understanding of Scripture. His work focuses on practical discipleship and spiritual growth for modern Christians.

name: Chad Huffman
bio: Chad Huffman is a Christian communicator and content creator dedicated to helping believers grow in their faith and understanding of Scripture. Through his writing and teaching, he explores themes of discipleship, spiritual growth, and practical Christianity for modern believers.

name: Daniel Strand
bio: Daniel Strand is assistant professor of ethics at the US Air Force Air War College and a contributing editor at Providence, the journal of Christianity and American foreign policy. He holds a PhD in religion and ethics from the University of Chicago and an MDiv from Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary, and he writes on Augustine, the just war tradition, and political theology for outlets including American Reformer and WORLD.

name: Aaron Boxerman
bio: Aaron Boxerman is a journalist and writer who covers religious and cultural topics with thoughtful analysis. His work explores the intersection of faith, politics, and contemporary issues from a balanced perspective.
known_for: Breaking-news coverage of the Israel-Hamas war for The New York Times.
current_role: Reporter, The New York Times, covering Israel and Gaza (based in Jerusalem)

faqs.a: Aaron Boxerman is a Jerusalem-based reporter for The New York Times covering Israel and Gaza, largely on the paper's live breaking-news team. He previously covered Palestinian affairs and the Arab world for The Times of Israel from 2020 to 2022.

He covers the Israel-Hamas war and broader Israeli and Palestinian affairs. His reporting from the region is frequently cited in coverage of events affecting the Holy Land, a subject of enduring interest to Christian readers.

faqs.q: Is Aaron Boxerman a Christian author?
faqs.a: No. Boxerman is a mainstream news journalist, and his work does not indicate an evangelical affiliation. His byline appears in Christian news digests because of his coverage of Israel and the Middle East.

name: Allen C. Guelzo
bio: Allen C. Guelzo is a respected historian and author known for his scholarly works on American history, faith, and ethics. A prolific writer and educator, he brings deep historical insight to contemporary Christian discussions about America's spiritual heritage and moral foundations.
affiliation: Newsweek, The Gospel Coalition, Intercollegiate Studies Institute
education: Ph.D. in American History, University of Pennsylvania

The Crisis of the American Republic: A History of Intellectual and Political Thought
Evangelicalism and the Future of Christianity
The God and the Gold: A Narrative History of Banking

name: Michael Kelley
bio: Michael Kelley is a pastor and author known for his work in Christian discipleship and spiritual formation. He has served in pastoral ministry and is committed to helping believers develop a deeper relationship with Christ through practical, biblical teaching.

God Hides in Plain Sight: How to See the Sacred in a Skeptical World

His work explores how biblical principles have shaped American thought and institutions, offering evangelical readers a thoughtful perspective on faith's role in public life.

bio: Kyle Bueermann is a Rural Specialist with the North American Mission Board's Replant team and a former Southern Baptist pastor in New Mexico. He is the author of 'Replanting Rural Churches,' co-hosts the Not Another Baptist Podcast, and writes for Lifeway Research.

name: Aimee Joseph
bio: Aimee Joseph is a writer and content creator focused on Christian living and faith development. Her work encourages believers to deepen their relationship with Christ through practical wisdom and biblical reflection.

name: Haley Isbell
bio: Haley Isbell is a writer and content creator focused on helping Christians navigate faith, relationships, and personal growth. Her work encourages readers to deepen their relationship with Christ through practical biblical insights and honest reflection.

name: Yan Zhuang and Ephrat Livni
bio: Yan Zhuang and Ephrat Livni are journalists and writers who explore faith, culture, and contemporary issues. Their work has appeared in major publications where they thoughtfully examine how belief intersects with modern life and society.

name: David Pierson
bio: David Pierson is a Christian author and speaker who focuses on biblical teaching and spiritual growth. His work emphasizes authentic faith and practical Christian living for modern believers.

name: Derek Brown
bio: Derek Brown is a writer and content creator dedicated to helping Christians deepen their understanding of Scripture and faith. His work focuses on making biblical truths accessible and relevant to modern believers.

name: Rachel Culver
bio: Rachel Culver is a writer and book reviewer whose work appears at The Gospel Coalition, including reviews on grief, lament, and Christian suffering, such as her review of Brittany Lee Allen's Free to Weep. A political studies graduate of The Master's University, she belongs to Grace Church of the Valley in Kingsburg, California, and writes to help Christians recover the biblical language of lament.

name: Steven Willing
bio: Steven Willing, MD, is a board-certified diagnostic radiologist and neuroradiologist who writes and speaks on science and Christian apologetics. He serves as a visiting scholar with Reasons to Believe and an adjunct professor at Regent University, and is the author of 'Superbia: The Perils of Pride.'

name: Owen Anderson
bio: Owen Anderson (PhD, Arizona State University) is a professor of philosophy and religious studies at Arizona State University, an adjunct instructor at Phoenix Seminary, and a pastor at Christ the King Reformed Church in Phoenix. A Christian philosopher focused on general revelation and the clarity of God's existence, he has authored books including 'The Clarity of God's Existence' and 'The Natural Moral Law,' and writes for American Reformer and Credo.

name: Hannah Depledge
bio: Hannah Depledge is a scholar and writer focused on Christian history and theology. Her research and writing help contemporary believers understand the depth and richness of the Christian tradition.

name: David Pierson and Paul Sonne
bio: David Pierson and Paul Sonne are journalists and reporters who have covered international news with particular attention to religious freedom, persecution, and humanitarian issues affecting Christians worldwide. Their reporting brings important stories of faith and resilience to global audiences.

name: Case Thorp
bio: Case Thorp is a Christian writer and communicator dedicated to helping people understand and live out their faith with authenticity and depth. His work focuses on discipleship, spiritual growth, and practical theology for contemporary believers.

name: Euan Ward and Jenny Gross
bio: Euan Ward is a reporter for The New York Times based in Beirut, covering Lebanon and Syria and the region's overlapping conflicts; he previously contributed to The Guardian. Jenny Gross is a New York Times reporter covering breaking and international news, having previously reported for The Wall Street Journal in London, where she covered British politics.

name: Matthew Cluraghty
bio: Matthew Cluraghty is a pastor in Minnesota with the Christian and Missionary Alliance and a doctoral student at Wheaton College. His writing, including work published at Mere Orthodoxy, explores Christian history, ethics, and the church's care for the vulnerable.

name: Christopher F. Schuetze and Tatiana Firsova
bio: Christopher F. Schuetze and Tatiana Firsova are journalists and writers who have contributed to major publications covering international affairs, culture, and human interest stories. Their work often explores themes of faith, family, and social issues from a thoughtful, narrative-driven perspective.

name: Christopher F. Schuetze
bio: Christopher F. Schuetze is a religion correspondent and journalist known for his thoughtful reporting on faith communities and religious life. His work has explored topics ranging from church governance to denominational movements, bringing nuanced perspective to contemporary Christian issues.

bio: Joyu Wang is a Taipei-based reporter for The Wall Street Journal covering Taiwan politics and cross-strait relations with China. A University of Missouri journalism graduate formerly based in Hong Kong, she shared a Human Rights Press Award for the Journal's breaking-news coverage of the Hong Kong protests.

name: James Eglinton
bio: James Eglinton is a scholar and theologian specializing in Reformed theology, Scottish church history, and the thought of figures like Samuel Rutherford. He combines academic rigor with accessible writing to help contemporary Christians understand their theological heritage and its relevance today.
affiliation: Reformation Trust Publishing; various academic institutions

The Man of Sorrows and His Holy People

name: Tom Hughes
bio: Tom Hughes is a Christian author and speaker who focuses on faith-based topics and practical spirituality. His work encourages believers to deepen their relationship with God through biblical teaching and contemporary application.

name: Steve Richardson
bio: Steve Richardson is a Christian leader and communicator known for his work in faith-based content and ministry. He is dedicated to helping believers deepen their understanding of Scripture and live out their faith in practical ways.

name: Jane Story
bio: Jane Story serves on campus staff with Cru, the collegiate ministry formerly known as Campus Crusade for Christ. Drawing on her own experience as an adult child of divorce, she writes for The Gospel Coalition on family and gray divorce, including guidance for churches caring for the growing number of people whose parents separate later in life.

name: Joey Sherrard
bio: Joey Sherrard (PhD, University of St Andrews) is associate pastor of discipleship at Signal Mountain Presbyterian Church near Chattanooga, Tennessee, and a fellow with the Center for Pastor Theologians. He is the author of The Augustinian Pastor: Deep Wisdom for Modern Ministry and T. F. Torrance as Missional Theologian, and he writes for outlets including Mere Orthodoxy and The Gospel Coalition.

name: Drew Brown
bio: Drew Brown is a writer with degrees in theology and English whose essays on faith, culture, and everyday life appear at RELEVANT Magazine. He writes Slow Faith, a Substack newsletter devoted to the slow and faithful pursuit of God over platform-building, and his work blends humor with honest reflection on the Christian life.

name: Catie Edmondson
bio: Catie Edmondson is a congressional correspondent and political reporter known for her coverage of Capitol Hill and legislative matters. While not primarily known as a Christian author, her journalism has provided insightful analysis of policy issues affecting faith communities and religious liberty.
known_for: Covering Congress, federal spending fights, and major legislation for The New York Times.
current_role: Congressional Correspondent, The New York Times (Washington, DC)

faqs.a: Catie Edmondson is a congressional correspondent for The New York Times based in Washington, DC. She covers Capitol Hill, including government funding battles, major legislation, and congressional leadership.

faqs.q: Is Catie Edmondson a Christian author?
faqs.a: No. Edmondson is a mainstream political journalist, and her public work does not indicate a religious affiliation. Her reporting is sometimes referenced in Christian media when legislation touches religious liberty or issues of concern to faith communities.
She covers the United States Congress, reporting on legislative negotiations, spending bills, and the politics of the House and Senate for The New York Times.

name: Courtney Reissig

bio: Matt Fraser is a Christian communicator and content creator known for his work in digital ministry and faith-based media. He is dedicated to helping believers grow in their understanding of Scripture and navigate their spiritual journey with practical wisdom.

bio: Paul Koch is a Lutheran pastor and writer who explores the intersection of faith, culture, and everyday life. His work engages thoughtfully with contemporary issues from a Christian perspective, offering readers both theological insight and practical wisdom for modern discipleship.

Before joining the church he and his wife, Katie, helped with two church plants and served in various lay roles. A military veteran who works in the electric utility industry, he has written for The Gospel Coalition about coming to faith through a fellow Marine's witness.

Their work often explores the intersection of personal belief, ethics, and contemporary life with thoughtfulness and nuance that resonates with readers seeking deeper understanding of faith in modern times.

Together, they bring firsthand experience from conflict zones and underserved communities to their storytelling, offering Christian perspectives on justice, compassion, and faith in action across the globe.

name: Geoffrey R. Kirkland
bio: Geoffrey R. Kirkland is a pastor and Christian writer devoted to expository preaching and biblical teaching. He serves in pastoral ministry and is passionate about helping believers understand and apply Scripture to their daily lives.

name: Mere Orthodoxy
bio: Mere Orthodoxy is a Christian journal and online publication dedicated to exploring classical Christian thought and its application to contemporary culture. The platform features a diverse community of writers committed to defending traditional Christian orthodoxy while engaging thoughtfully with modern intellectual discourse. Through essays, reviews, and cultural commentary, Mere Orthodoxy seeks to articulate a winsome vision of Christian faith rooted in Scripture and the historic creeds.
affiliation: Independent publication; edited by Jake Meador
known_for: Long-form essays on faith, politics, and culture from a theologically serious Reformed evangelical perspective.
current_role: Online magazine and quarterly print journal of Protestant theology, culture, and ethics

faqs.a: Mere Orthodoxy is a Reformed evangelical magazine of theology, culture, and ethics founded in 2005 by Matthew Lee Anderson, originally as a group blog started from a Biola University dorm room. It publishes long-form essays online and a quarterly print journal for members.
Jake Meador, a writer based in Lincoln, Nebraska, serves as editor-in-chief. His work has also appeared in The Atlantic, First Things, Commonweal, and Christianity Today.

faqs.q: What perspective does Mere Orthodoxy write from?
faqs.a: The magazine writes from a broadly Reformed, confessional Protestant perspective and aims to form Christians for faithful participation in public life. Its essays on evangelical fracturing, family, work, and political theology are widely discussed across the evangelical world.

Together, their work provides comprehensive coverage of religious institutions and their impact on contemporary society.
