name: Alister McGrath
bio: Alister McGrath is a world-renowned theologian, scientist, and Christian apologist who has devoted his career to bridging faith and reason. With expertise in historical theology and the intersection of science and religion, he has written over 80 books exploring topics from the Reformation to atheism, helping countless Christians understand and defend their faith with intellectual rigor and pastoral sensitivity.
education: Doctor of Philosophy (DPhil), University of Oxford; Doctor of Medicine (MD), University of Aberdeen

books.title: The Intellectual Origins of the European Reformation

known_for: Bridging science and Christian faith as an Oxford theologian with a doctorate in molecular biophysics, and answering the New Atheism in books like The Dawkins Delusion.
current_role: Emeritus Andreas Idreos Professor of Science and Religion, University of Oxford; associate priest in Church of England parishes in the Cotswolds

faqs.a: McGrath is an Anglican and an ordained priest in the Church of England. Alongside his academic career he serves as an associate priest in a group of village parishes in the English Cotswolds.

Yes. McGrath was an atheist as a young man in Northern Ireland and converted to Christianity while studying at Oxford. He went on to earn Oxford doctorates in both molecular biophysics and theology, which shaped his lifelong focus on the relationship between science and faith.

faqs.q: What is Alister McGrath known for?
faqs.a: McGrath has written over 80 books, including the widely used textbook Christian Theology: An Introduction, a major biography of C.S. Lewis, and The Dawkins Delusion, a response to Richard Dawkins's The God Delusion. He held the Andreas Idreos Professorship of Science and Religion at Oxford until retiring in 2022.

McGrath retired from his Oxford chair in 2022 and is now Professor Emeritus of Science and Religion and an emeritus fellow of Harris Manchester College. He remains active as a writer and speaker; his recent book Why We Believe explores the rationality of belief in uncertain times.

name: Changwon Shu
bio: Changwon Shu is a Korean Reformed writer who studied at the Free Church College in Edinburgh. He contributes to Reformed evangelical publications including Banner of Truth, Evangelical Times, and Ligonier's Tabletalk magazine, often writing about the work of God in Korea, his native land.

name: Robert D. Cathcart
bio: Robert D. Cathcart is a respected biblical scholar and communicator known for his work in Old Testament studies and expository preaching. His contributions to Christian education and biblical interpretation have influenced generations of pastors and teachers seeking deeper understanding of Scripture.

name: Farnaz Fassihi
bio: Farnaz Fassihi is an award-winning international journalist and foreign correspondent known for her courageous reporting from the Middle East and conflict zones. With decades of experience covering faith communities, political upheaval, and human rights issues, she brings nuanced perspective to complex global stories that matter to Christians seeking to understand our world.

books.title: Waiting for an Ordinary Day: The Unraveling of Life in Iraq

name: W. Robert Godfrey
bio: W. Robert Godfrey is a Reformed theologian and church historian who has devoted his career to helping Christians understand Scripture and church tradition. As a prolific author and educator, he combines scholarly depth with accessible teaching to equip believers in their faith and understanding of God's Word.

books.title: Pleasing God: Discovering the Vision for Worship
An Unexpected Reformation: How the Sixteenth Century Changed the Course of Christianity
Reformation Sketches: Insights Into Luther, Calvin and the Reformation

name: Tom Sugimura
bio: Tom Sugimura is a pastor at New Life Church in Woodland Hills, California, a church-planting coach, and a professor of biblical counseling. A former engineer, he graduated from The Master's Seminary and earned a doctorate in biblical counseling from The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary. His books include Grace, Race, and the Church and The Church Behind Barbed Wire, and he hosts the Every Peoples Podcast.

name: Katie Deckert
bio: Katie Deckert is a pastor's wife and mother of three in northern Virginia, where she is a member of Emmanuel Baptist Church in Alexandria. Drawing on fifteen years alongside her husband in ministry, she writes to encourage pastors' wives with the truths of Scripture and honest reflection on the hidden costs and quiet graces of life in ministry, including for 9Marks.

name: Reid Patton
bio: Reid Patton is a content editor at Lifeway Christian Resources and cohost of a Bible study podcast. He develops small-group and discipleship studies for the church, and lives in the Nashville area with his family.

name: Rosemary Jensen
bio: Rosemary Jensen is a Bible teacher and author known for her accessible approach to Scripture study and Christian living. Her work emphasizes practical faith application and spiritual growth for modern believers.

name: Miranda Carls
bio: Miranda Carls is a Christian author, speaker, and leadership coach specializing in faith-and-work integration, leadership transitions, and emotional intelligence. She is the author of 'The Word at Work: Ten Biblical Principles for Christian Professionals' and has written for The Gospel Coalition and Biblical Leadership. She lives outside St. Louis, Missouri, with her husband and three sons.

name: Joel Morris
bio: Joel Morris is executive director at Union School of Theology in Wales, a Reformed theological college in the tradition of Martyn Lloyd-Jones. He writes on Christian living for Ligonier Ministries and Tabletalk magazine, including contributions to Ligonier's Fruit of the Spirit collection on joy and articles on generosity and the Christian life.

name: Darin White
bio: Darin White is the Margaret Gage Bush Professor of Business at Samford University in Birmingham, Alabama, where he directs the Sports Industry Program. He holds a PhD from the University of Alabama and has contributed to The Gospel Coalition, writing at the intersection of Christian faith, work, and culture.

name: Lesley Crews
bio: Lesley Crews is an editorial coordinator and writer at RELEVANT, the magazine covering faith, culture, and intentional living for younger Christians. Her articles for the publication range across relationships, culture, justice, and practical Christian living, including the biblical case for generosity toward the homeless.

name: Bruce Gilley
bio: Bruce Gilley is a political scientist and scholar known for his work on colonialism, governance, and international relations from a classical liberal perspective. His writing engages with historical and contemporary political questions, often challenging prevailing academic orthodoxies with rigorous analysis and contrarian perspectives.

books.title: The Right to Rule: How States Win Respect

name: Arlette Bashizi
bio: Arlette Bashizi is a Christian writer and speaker who brings African perspectives to contemporary faith discussions. Her work emphasizes reconciliation, spiritual growth, and the intersection of culture and Christian discipleship.

name: Dorothy Greco
bio: Dorothy Greco is a writer and speaker who addresses faith, parenting, and spiritual growth with honesty and biblical insight. She has contributed to various Christian publications and speaks at conferences on topics related to family, faith, and discipleship.

name: Andrew Davis
bio: Andrew Davis is a pastor and Bible teacher known for his expository preaching and commitment to helping Christians understand Scripture deeply. He has ministered in pastoral roles and is recognized for his work in discipleship and biblical exposition within evangelical churches.

name: David Huffstutler
bio: David Huffstutler is senior pastor of First Baptist Church in Troy, Michigan, after serving as lead pastor of First Baptist Church of Rockford, Illinois, from 2013 to 2025, where he was also a police chaplain. He holds a PhD in applied theology from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary and writes on Scripture, sanctification, and church leadership for G3 Ministries and Religious Affections Ministries.

name: Eric Demeter
bio: Eric Demeter is a Christian author and content creator focused on faith-based topics and spiritual growth. His work aims to help believers deepen their understanding of Scripture and live out their faith with greater intentionality.

name: John Starke
bio: John Starke is a writer and editor who has contributed thoughtful articles on Christian faith, culture, and theology to various evangelical publications. He is known for exploring how biblical truth intersects with contemporary life and culture in accessible, engaging ways.
known_for: Writing on prayer and the hidden spiritual life amid ambition and restlessness, including The Possibility of Prayer.
current_role: Lead Pastor, Apostles Church Uptown, New York City

faqs.a: John Starke is the lead pastor of Apostles Church Uptown in Manhattan, where he lives with his wife and four children. He previously served as an editor at The Gospel Coalition and has written for Christianity Today and Comment Magazine.

faqs.q: What is John Starke known for?
faqs.a: Starke is known for The Possibility of Prayer: Finding Stillness with God in a Restless World and The Secret Place of Thunder, books on contemplative prayer and resisting a culture of performance. He also co-edited the theological volume One God in Three Persons with Bruce Ware.

He pastors Apostles Church Uptown, an evangelical congregation in upper Manhattan, New York City. His ministry focuses on spiritual formation and prayer for Christians living in a demanding urban environment.

name: Scott Rae
bio: Scott Rae is a leading Christian ethicist and professor who has spent decades helping believers think carefully about faith and culture. He specializes in bioethics, business ethics, and Christian worldview development, offering practical biblical guidance on complex moral issues. Through his teaching, writing, and speaking, Rae equips Christians to make wise decisions grounded in Scripture.
affiliation: Talbot School of Theology at Biola University

books.title: Moral Choices: An Introduction to Ethics
Does God Help Those Who Help Themselves?
Body and Soul: Sports the Way God Intended

name: Rick Langer
bio: Rick Langer is a scholar and communicator dedicated to helping Christians understand and engage thoughtfully with contemporary culture and philosophy. With expertise in apologetics and worldview studies, he works to bridge the gap between academic rigor and accessible Christian teaching, equipping believers to think deeply about their faith.

name: Isabel Choat
bio: Isabel Choat is a scholar and writer focused on Christian history and theology. Her work explores the intersections of faith, culture, and historical understanding within Christian traditions.

name: Lydia Bugg
bio: Lydia Bugg is a Christian writer and content creator dedicated to helping believers deepen their faith and understanding of Scripture. Through her writing and speaking, she explores themes of discipleship, spiritual growth, and God's transformative work in everyday life.

name: Will Parker Anderson
bio: Will Parker Anderson is a senior editor at WaterBrook & Multnomah, the Christian imprint of Penguin Random House, and a pastor at Southlands Church in Santa Ana, California. He writes the Writers Circle newsletter and podcast to help Christian writers hone their craft, and his articles appear at The Gospel Coalition and Preaching Today.

name: Rich Wilkerson Jr.
bio: Rich Wilkerson Jr. is the lead pastor of VOUS Church in Miami, Florida, which he and his wife, DawnCheré, launched in 2015. The son of Trinity Church pastors Rich and Robyn Wilkerson, he is the author of Sandcastle Kings, Friend of Sinners, and Single & Secure, and he speaks widely on grace, relationships, and reaching the next generation.

name: Blake Glosson
bio: Blake Glosson (MDiv, Reformed Theological Seminary) is an assistant pastor at Chapelstreet Church in Geneva, Illinois, and previously served as director of young adults at New Covenant Bible Church. His writing on encouragement, suffering, and Christian relationships has been published by The Gospel Coalition and Crosswalk and republished by Tim Challies, Moody Radio, and The Aquila Report. He blogs at Fully Known, Fully Loved.

name: Max Kim and Chang W. Lee
bio: Max Kim is a Seoul-based journalist reporting for The New York Times, previously a Korea correspondent for the Los Angeles Times, whose feature writing has won SOPA and Sigma Delta Chi awards. Chang W. Lee is a veteran New York Times staff photojournalist who has covered wars, Olympics, and world events for the paper since 1994.

name: Jason Douglas
bio: Jason Douglas is Tokyo bureau chief for The Wall Street Journal, after covering Asian economies from the paper's Singapore bureau with a focus on China's economy and global trade. He previously reported on economics and public policy from London, covering Brexit and the pandemic, and began his career at newspapers in Northern Ireland before joining Dow Jones in 2007.

name: James White
bio: James R. White is director of Alpha and Omega Ministries, a Christian apologetics organization based in Phoenix, Arizona, and one of evangelicalism's most prolific public debaters, having engaged Roman Catholic, Muslim, Mormon, and skeptic interlocutors in well over a hundred moderated debates. He is the author of books including The King James Only Controversy, The Forgotten Trinity, and The God Who Justifies, and he hosts The Dividing Line webcast.

name: Shan Li
bio: Shan Li is a foreign correspondent for The Wall Street Journal in New Delhi, covering India and South Asia's politics and economy. She previously reported on Chinese tech giants from Beijing and covered the pandemic from both China and New York, joining the Journal from the Los Angeles Times. She has been named a Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan.

name: Lifeway Research
bio: Lifeway Research is the research arm of Lifeway Christian Resources, one of the largest Christian resource providers in the world and an entity of the Southern Baptist Convention. Based in Nashville, it conducts surveys and studies on church health, faith, and culture, and publishes data-driven insights and practical ministry articles to equip pastors and church leaders.

name: Rosaria Butterfield and Jared Moore
bio: Rosaria Butterfield is a former tenured professor of English at Syracuse University who, after her conversion to Christ, became one of evangelicalism's most influential voices on sexuality, hospitality, and identity; her books include The Secret Thoughts of an Unlikely Convert and The Gospel Comes with a House Key. Jared Moore (PhD, Southern Baptist Theological Seminary) is a Tennessee pastor and author of The Lust of the Flesh.

name: Dov Lieber
bio: Dov Lieber is a Wall Street Journal correspondent covering Israel and the Palestinian territories from Tel Aviv, where he has reported for the Journal since 2018 on politics, security, and regional conflict. He previously covered Palestinian affairs for The Times of Israel and holds a master's degree in Middle Eastern studies from Tel Aviv University.

name: Paul Putz
bio: Paul Emory Putz is a historian and director of the Faith & Sports Institute at Baylor University's Truett Seminary, where he helped create the seminary's MA in theology and sports studies. His book The Spirit of the Game: American Christianity and Big-Time Sports (Oxford, 2024) won the American Society of Church History's Brewer Prize, and he writes on sports and faith for Christianity Today and The Gospel Coalition.

name: Forrest Marion
bio: Forrest L. Marion is a military historian and retired US Air Force Reserve colonel who has served as a government historian since 1998, including at the Air Force Historical Research Agency. A Virginia Military Institute graduate with a PhD from the University of Tennessee, he is the author of Flight Risk and other military histories, and he writes on Presbyterian church matters for The Aquila Report as a longtime member of Eastwood Presbyterian Church in Montgomery, Alabama.

name: Julianne Schultz
bio: Julianne Schultz AM is professor emerita of media and culture at Griffith University in Australia and was founding editor of Griffith Review, which she published from 2003 to 2021. A fortnightly columnist for The Guardian, she is the author of The Idea of Australia: A Search for the Soul of the Nation and Reviving the Fourth Estate, and she was made a Member of the Order of Australia for services to journalism.

name: Gage Arnold
bio: Gage Arnold is a ministry leader and communications professional based in the Nashville area who serves on staff at First Presbyterian Church Nashville. His writing on faith, work, and economics has appeared at The Gospel Coalition, the Institute for Faith, Work & Economics, and Made to Flourish, alongside communications work for churches and faith-and-work organizations.

name: Guardian Staff
bio: Guardian staff is the collective byline used by The Guardian, the British news organization founded in Manchester in 1821 and owned by the Scott Trust, for articles produced by its newsroom rather than an individual reporter. The Guardian's global editions in the UK, US, and Australia cover world news, politics, and culture, including extensive reporting on religion and public life.

name: Jay Sklar
bio: Jay Sklar is a biblical scholar and author known for his work on Old Testament theology and biblical interpretation. He has contributed significantly to Christian education and theological understanding through his writing and teaching.

name: Mark Dance
bio: Mark Dance is a pastor, author, and leadership consultant who serves the local church through practical resources and training. He is passionate about helping church leaders navigate change, build healthy teams, and develop sustainable ministry practices that strengthen congregational life.

books.title: Tribal Church: Lead Small, Impact Big
The Advent Conspiracy: Reclaiming the True Meaning of Christmas

name: Ben Brophy
bio: Ben Brophy (MDiv, Midwestern Baptist Theological Seminary) is a bivocational pastor at Emmanuel Baptist Church in Alexandria, Virginia. He writes for The Gospel Coalition on eldership, productivity, and local-church leadership, including widely shared pieces on the partnership between staff pastors and lay elders. He and his wife, Marion, have three children.

name: Mary Mohler
bio: Mary Mohler is a writer and speaker known for her thoughtful contributions to Christian culture and family life. As the wife of seminary president R. Albert Mohler Jr., she brings a pastor's heart to conversations about faith, motherhood, and Christian living.
affiliation: The Briefing, Southern Baptist Theological Seminary

name: Damian Carrington
bio: Damian Carrington is the Environment Editor at The Guardian, where he covers critical environmental issues including climate change, biodiversity, and conservation. With a background in science journalism, he brings rigorous reporting and clarity to complex ecological topics that matter to Christians concerned with stewardship of God's creation.

name: Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan
bio: Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan are prominent political journalists known for their investigative reporting on U.S. politics and governance. While not primarily faith-focused writers, their work on political accountability and truthfulness aligns with Christian values of justice and integrity in public life.

books.title: Confidence Man: The Making of Donald Trump and the Breaking of America

name: Jonathan Malm
bio: Jonathan Malm is a creative strategist and author who helps churches and Christian organizations communicate their message more effectively. He has worked with numerous faith-based organizations to develop innovative strategies for reaching people in today's digital culture.

books.title: The Unwelcome Guests: How to Welcome People into God's Kingdom
Loud Families: Creating and Sustaining a Family Culture Filled with Laughter, Intentionality and Faith

name: Daniel Hames
bio: Daniel Hames is Vice President of Union (Union School of Theology) in the UK, where he lectures in systematic and historical theology, preaching, and spiritual formation. He has written with Michael Reeves, including 'God Shines Forth,' and contributes to outlets such as Desiring God. His work centers on a Trinitarian, Christ-centered vision of the Christian life.

name: Jonny Reid
bio: Jonny Reid is a Scottish pastor and author known for his thought-provoking content on faith, culture, and Christian living. His work resonates with readers seeking to integrate their faith with contemporary issues and personal discipleship.

name: Josh Herring
bio: Josh Herring is a Christian communicator and content creator dedicated to helping believers deepen their faith and understanding of Scripture. Through writing and teaching, he equips Christians to live out their convictions with biblical clarity and practical wisdom.

name: Richard Blackaby
bio: Richard Blackaby is a respected Christian author and speaker known for his work on spiritual leadership and God's guidance. Son of renowned pastor Henry Blackaby, Richard has devoted his ministry to helping believers understand how God directs their lives and calls them to purposeful service. His writings emphasize practical faith application and the importance of aligning one's work with God's will.
education: Master of Divinity, Canadian Baptist Seminary

books.title: Experiencing God: Knowing and Doing the Will of God
Spiritual Leadership: Moving People On to God's Agenda
The Seasons of God: How the Spirit Works in Human History
Called and Accountable: Discovering Your Place in God's Purpose
God's Invitation: A Challenge to the Greatest Adventure of Your Life

name: Kim Barker
bio: Kim Barker is a journalist and author known for her investigative reporting and personal narratives that explore faith, resilience, and human experience. Her work has appeared in major publications and reflects a thoughtful engagement with contemporary issues from a faith-informed perspective.

name: Michael Anthony Adams
bio: Michael Anthony Adams is a Christian author and thought leader whose work explores faith, culture, and discipleship for contemporary believers. His writings engage thoughtfully with how Christians can live out their convictions in an increasingly pluralistic world.

name: Oleksandra Mykolyshyn
bio: Oleksandra Mykolyshyn is a Ukrainian Christian author and content creator who shares faith-centered perspectives with audiences across Eastern Europe and beyond. Her writing reflects a commitment to exploring Christian themes through a contemporary cultural lens.

name: Sutton Raphael and Rebecca Suner
bio: Sutton Raphael and Rebecca Suner are video journalists at The New York Times. Raphael produces visual journalism for the paper's digital platforms, and Suner, who joined the Times in 2023 after serving as a senior producer at the digital media startup Brut, works on the social visuals team. Their collaborations include on-the-ground video reporting from Ukraine.

name: Ryan Denton
bio: Ryan Denton is a Reformed evangelist and director of Christ in the Wild Ministries, which he founded in 2016 after serving as a Southern Baptist pastor on the Navajo Reservation. An open-air preacher affiliated with Vanguard Presbyterian Church, he has studied at Puritan Reformed Theological Seminary and authored works on evangelism including 'A Certain Sound' and 'Even If None.'

name: Bill Elliff
bio: Bill Elliff is a pastor, author, and conference speaker known for his ministry in revival and spiritual leadership. He has served as senior pastor of the Summit Church in Arkansas and is deeply committed to equipping believers for authentic Christian living and biblical discipleship.

books.title: Prayed On: How to Pray for Your Pastor and Leaders

name: PJ Dunn
bio: PJ Dunn is founder and president of Table for One Ministries, launched in 2013 to disciple single adults, and serves in church revitalization with the Georgia Baptist Mission Board. An adjunct professor at New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary and a Lifeway author, he travels nationally speaking and coaching on singles ministry and young-adult discipleship, including how churches can help young adults engage AI with biblical wisdom.

name: Zak Mellgren
bio: Zak Mellgren is a Christian writer and former worship pastor who writes on books, faith, family, and film through his newsletter The SubZak. He holds an MA in biblical studies and often reflects on the local church and Christian living.

name: Ivan Mesa
bio: Ivan Mesa (PhD, The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary) is editorial director for The Gospel Coalition, where he oversees its book review section and annual book awards. He is the editor of several books, including 'Before You Lose Your Faith: Deconstructing Doubt in the Church,' 'Faithful Exiles,' and 'Scrolling Ourselves to Death.'

name: Marc Santora
bio: Marc Santora is a seasoned journalist and author who has covered major news stories for prominent publications including The New York Times. Drawing on his extensive reporting experience, he brings investigative insight and storytelling depth to his work, often exploring themes relevant to faith, culture, and human experience.

name: Thomas Brand
bio: Thomas Brand (PhD, Durham) is Ministry Director of the Evangelical Fellowship of Congregational Churches, a network of around a hundred UK churches, and has served on the leadership of Affinity, one of the largest networks of evangelical churches in Britain. He is the author of 'Intimately Forsaken: A Trinitarian Christology of the Cross.'

name: Carolyn Morris-Collier
bio: Carolyn Morris-Collier is a writer and editor who serves as editorial project manager for Christianity Today's Inkwell (formerly Ekstasis). An Oxford graduate, she writes the Substack The Green Door on religious trends, re-enchantment, and culture, and has contributed to outlets including Comment magazine.

name: Constant Méheut
bio: Constant Méheut was a French Christian artist and illustrator known for his devotional works and spiritual contributions to Christian literature. His artistic vision was shaped by a deep faith that influenced his illustrations and design work for religious publications.

name: Dawson Knaul
bio: Dawson Knaul is a writer contributing to American Reformer, a publication focused on Protestant social and political thought. His work engages questions of theology, ontology, and cultural renewal from a confessional Reformed perspective, including essays critiquing theological liberalism and defending historic Christian orthodoxy.

name: Jonathan Swan and David E. Sanger
bio: Jonathan Swan is a national political reporter known for his investigative journalism on Washington politics and policy, while David E. Sanger is a Pulitzer Prize-winning national security correspondent with deep expertise in foreign policy and cybersecurity. Together, they have collaborated on significant reporting projects examining government decisions and their consequences for Americans.

books.title: The Perfect Weapon: War, Sabotage, and Fear in the Cyber Age

name: Ashifa Kassam
bio: Ashifa Kassam is a European community affairs correspondent who reports on social, cultural, and community issues across Europe. Her journalism focuses on human interest stories and grassroots movements that reflect the lived experiences of European communities. Through her reporting, she brings attention to voices and perspectives often underrepresented in mainstream media coverage.

name: Kyle Burks
bio: Kyle Burks (MDiv, The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary) is a pastoral resident at Creekside Community Church in Gainesville, Florida. He writes for The Gospel Coalition and publishes on his Substack, 'Sweetheart, I'm Busy,' offering pastoral reflection on Christian living and discipleship.

name: James Marson
bio: James Marson is a journalist and author known for his investigative work on religious persecution and faith-based issues. His reporting has focused on the experiences of Christians facing persecution in various parts of the world, bringing attention to underreported stories of faith and resilience.

books.title: The Cost of Living Out Your Faith

name: Amelia Nierenberg and Matthew Mpoke Bigg
bio: Amelia Nierenberg and Matthew Mpoke Bigg are journalists and writers who have contributed to major publications covering faith, culture, and social issues. Their work explores the intersection of Christianity, contemporary society, and human stories with depth and nuance.
known_for: Co-bylined international breaking-news coverage for The New York Times.
current_role: Reporters, The New York Times (both based in London, covering international news)

faqs.q: Who are Amelia Nierenberg and Matthew Mpoke Bigg?
faqs.a: They are two New York Times journalists whose names appear together on co-bylined international stories. Amelia Nierenberg is a London-based reporter covering international news who previously wrote for the Food desk; Matthew Mpoke Bigg is a London-based reporter on the Times's live breaking-news team, writing mainly on the Middle East and Ukraine, after a career at Reuters.

No. Both are mainstream news journalists, and their public work does not indicate a religious affiliation. Their co-bylined coverage of world events, including the Middle East, is sometimes shared in Christian news digests.
Both cover international and breaking news from London for The New York Times, including the Middle East, Ukraine, and Europe.

name: R. Kent Hughes
bio: R. Kent Hughes is a respected evangelical pastor, author, and Bible teacher known for his expository preaching and thoughtful theological writing. He served as senior pastor of College Church in Wheaton, Illinois for over three decades, where he became known for his verse-by-verse biblical exposition and pastoral care. His numerous books on Scripture, worship, and Christian living have influenced countless believers seeking deeper engagement with God's Word.
affiliation: College Church in Wheaton, Illinois; Preaching the Word commentary series

books.title: Set Apart: Calling a Worldly Church to a Godly Life

name: Robert Hasler
bio: Robert Hasler is an assistant pastor at Christ Presbyterian Church (PCA) in Burke, Virginia, and a 2023 Cotton Mather Fellow with American Reformer. A graduate of Covenant Theological Seminary, he writes on Christian faith and public life and has been called to plant a PCA church in Abilene, Texas.

name: Joel Cho
bio: Joel Cho is a Christian author and speaker known for his work in spiritual growth and biblical teaching. He has contributed to various Christian publications and platforms dedicated to equipping believers in their faith journeys.

name: Dwayne McCrary
bio: Dwayne McCrary is a Christian author and speaker who focuses on faith-based topics and spiritual growth. He is dedicated to helping believers deepen their relationship with God through thoughtful writing and teaching.

name: Josh Dawsey
bio: Josh Dawsey is a political reporter and journalist known for his investigative work covering national politics and the Trump administration. While not primarily a Christian content creator, his reporting has been widely followed by evangelical audiences interested in political news and analysis from a major news perspective.

name: John Owen
bio: John Owen (1616–1683) was an English Congregationalist theologian and pastor whose works profoundly shaped Reformed theology and Christian spirituality. Known for his deep biblical scholarship and pastoral sensitivity, Owen served as Vice-Chancellor of Oxford University and ministered through both preaching and prolific theological writing. His treatises on sin, the Holy Spirit, and biblical interpretation remain influential among evangelicals seeking robust theological foundations.

books.title: Of Communion with God the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost
The Mortification of Sin in Believers
Of the Divine Original, Authority, Self-Evidencing Light and Power of the Scripture

name: Chrys Jones
bio: Chrys Jones is a pastor, writer, and Christian hip-hop artist and producer with Christcentric. He pastors Little Zion Baptist Church in Burgin, Kentucky, and previously served as a pastoral resident at Grace Church in Danville. A husband and father of four, he also runs The Undistracted Christian and writes for outlets like Desiring God.
affiliation: Little Zion Baptist Church, Burgin, KY; Christcentric

name: Karsten Harrison
bio: Karsten Harrison serves as pastor of student ministry and outreach at Emmanuel Baptist Church in Overland Park, Kansas, while studying biblical studies at Midwestern Baptist Theological Seminary. He is a staff writer for The Lion and has contributed to The Gospel Coalition, For The Church, and The Rebelution.
affiliation: Emmanuel Baptist Church, Overland Park, KS

name: Alex DiPrima
bio: Alex DiPrima is senior pastor of Emmanuel Church in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, which he helped plant in 2017. He holds a PhD in historical theology from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary with a focus on Charles Spurgeon, and he is the author of Spurgeon: A Life and Spurgeon and the Poor. His writing appears with 9Marks, the Spurgeon Center, Ligonier, and The Gospel Coalition.

name: Norimitsu Onishi and Hubert Hayaud
bio: Norimitsu Onishi is an accomplished journalist known for his reporting on African affairs and international development issues. Hubert Hayaud is a French researcher and writer focused on social and humanitarian topics. Together, their collaborative work explores complex global challenges through rigorous reporting and analysis.

name: Luis Ferré-Sadurní and Federico Rios
bio: Luis Ferré-Sadurní and Federico Rios are investigative journalists known for their in-depth reporting on complex social and environmental issues. While not primarily Christian content creators, their work often touches on themes of justice, stewardship, and human dignity that resonate with Christian values and concerns.

name: Tilly Dillehay
bio: Tilly Dillehay is an author, journalist, and podcast cohost who has written on beauty, envy, food, and the Christian home in books such as 'Seeing Green' and 'My Dear Hemlock.' A graduate of Lipscomb University, she contributes to The Gospel Coalition and Desiring God. She and her pastor husband raise their children in Tennessee.

name: T M. Suffield
bio: T M. Suffield is a British author and theologian who writes thoughtfully about faith, culture, and the Christian life. His work engages contemporary issues with theological depth and practical wisdom for modern believers.

books.title: Reclanting: What It Means to Abandon the Faith

name: Benjamin Vincent
bio: Benjamin Vincent is a biblical scholar and author dedicated to helping Christians understand Scripture more deeply. His work focuses on making biblical languages and theological concepts accessible to everyday believers.

name: Beth Claes
bio: Beth Claes is director of counseling at New Heights Church in Vancouver, Washington. She holds a doctorate in psychology and practiced as a psychologist for ten years before moving to a gospel-centered biblical counseling approach. A trainer for the Association of Biblical Counselors, she writes on counseling, trauma, and shame for The Gospel Coalition and at her blog, Wrestled Faith.

name: Brian Daniel
bio: Brian Daniel serves at Lifeway Christian Resources in Nashville, where he leads a team resourcing and training small-group and Bible-study leaders. He hosts the Group Answers Podcast and writes for Lifeway Research and Lifeway Voices, focusing on discipleship, group ministry, and equipping local churches.

name: Matthew Hall
bio: Matthew Hall is a theologian and author known for his work in Christian doctrine and biblical studies. He has contributed significantly to evangelical scholarship through his writing and teaching on topics central to Christian faith and practice.

name: Kristy Etheridge
bio: Kristy Etheridge is a features editor at Christianity Today. A Syracuse University graduate with a background in broadcast journalism, she began her career as a news producer and reporter at WECT-TV in Wilmington, North Carolina, and later reported in Charlotte before moving to Brooklyn in 2018. She is a multimedia journalist with a passion for telling stories about God and people.

name: Kate Lucky
bio: Kate Lucky is an editor and writer at Christianity Today, where she works on the features team as editorial director for features. She was previously managing editor of Commonweal, and her essays on faith and culture have also appeared in Plough and The Point.

name: Andrew Wilson
bio: Andrew Wilson is a British pastor and author known for his thoughtful biblical teaching and cultural commentary from a Reformed evangelical perspective. He serves as Teaching Pastor at King's Church London and is a regular contributor to leading Christian publications, helping Christians think carefully about faith, culture, and Scripture.

books.title: Unbreakable: What the Bible Teaches About Divorce and Remarriage
Incomparable: Jesus Christ in the Old Testament
Remaking the World: Vocation, Work, and the Glory of God
Spirit: God's Holy and Subversive Gift
Echoes of Exodus: Tracing Themes of Liberation, Deliverance, and Salvation Throughout the Bible

known_for: Combining Reformed theology with charismatic practice and writing Remaking the World, an account of how 1776 created the post-Christian West.
current_role: Teaching Pastor, King's Church London; columnist for Christianity Today

faqs.a: Andrew Wilson is an English pastor and author who serves as teaching pastor at King's Church London, part of the Newfrontiers family of charismatic evangelical churches. He holds degrees in history and theology from Cambridge and King's College London and writes a regular column for Christianity Today.

Yes. Wilson describes his ideal as 'eucharismatic' worship, combining historic liturgical and sacramental practice with charismatic gifts of the Spirit, a vision he laid out in Spirit and Sacrament. He is theologically Reformed while affirming the continuation of the gifts.

faqs.q: What is Andrew Wilson known for?
faqs.a: Wilson is known for Remaking the World: How 1776 Created the Post-Christian West, which won a Gospel Coalition book award, as well as books like God of All Things and Incomparable. He is also a prominent voice at the Think Theology blog and in British evangelicalism.

He is teaching pastor at King's Church London, a large charismatic evangelical church in southeast London. Earlier in his ministry he served at churches within the Newfrontiers movement, and he remains associated with that network.

name: Danson Ottawa
bio: Danson Ottawa (BTh, MDiv, Africa International University) is a Kenyan theologian and the national coordinator of the Africa Center for Apologetics Research (ACFAR), Kenya, equipping African believers in apologetics, discernment, and cult evangelism. He teaches theology and apologetics at Africa International University and is a regular contributor to The Gospel Coalition Africa and Langham's ASET Series.
affiliation: Africa Center for Apologetics Research (Kenya) / Africa International University

name: Preston Sprinkle
bio: Preston Sprinkle is an author and speaker known for addressing challenging biblical and cultural topics with grace and theological depth. His work focuses on helping Christians navigate difficult conversations around sexuality, violence, and social justice from a biblical perspective. Preston is dedicated to equipping believers to think critically about their faith and engage compassionately with a complex world.
affiliation: Theology in the Raw / The Center for Faith, Sexuality & Gender
education: M.A. in Theological Studies, Calvary Chapel Bible College

books.title: What Every Christian Should Know About the Qur'an
Fight: A Christian Case for Non-Violence
Living in a Gray World: A Christian Teen's Guide to Understanding Homosexuality
Embodied: Transexuality and the Christian Faith
Does the Bible Support Same-Sex Marriage?

tradition: Broadly evangelical; holds the historic Christian sexual ethic while emphasizing compassionate engagement
known_for: The Theology in the Raw podcast, the Exiles in Babylon conference, and books helping Christians engage sexuality and gender with both theological faithfulness and compassion.
current_role: President of Theology in the Raw; co-founder and president of The Center for Faith, Sexuality & Gender

faqs.a: Sprinkle is a broadly evangelical biblical scholar with a PhD from Aberdeen who resists tidy partisan labels. He holds a high view of Scripture, affirms the historic Christian sexual ethic, and is known for hosting charitable long-form conversations with people across theological and political divides on his Theology in the Raw podcast.

faqs.q: Is Preston Sprinkle affirming of same-sex marriage?
faqs.a: No. Sprinkle holds the historic view that marriage is between a man and a woman, argued in books like People to Be Loved and Does the Bible Support Same-Sex Marriage? 21 Conversations. At the same time, he emphasizes that LGBTQ people should be treated with dignity and genuinely welcomed in churches, and he critiques evangelical culture-war postures.

faqs.q: What is The Center for Faith, Sexuality & Gender?
faqs.a: It is an organization Sprinkle co-founded and leads that equips churches to engage questions of sexuality and gender with what it calls 'theological faithfulness and courageous love.' It produces courses, pastoral papers, and conferences from a historic-sexual-ethic perspective.

Exiles in Babylon is the annual conference Sprinkle launched in 2022 through Theology in the Raw. It deliberately platforms a range of viewpoints on contested topics — sexuality, race, politics, hell — modeling disagreement within a shared commitment to Scripture.

faqs.q: What else has Preston Sprinkle written about?
faqs.a: Beyond sexuality and gender, Sprinkle co-authored Erasing Hell with Francis Chan, wrote Fight on Christian nonviolence, and Exiles on Christian political identity. His consistent theme is that Christians are 'exiles' whose primary allegiance transcends partisan politics.

name: Joel Smit
bio: Joel E. Smit is senior pastor of Smyrna Presbyterian Church (PCA) in Smyrna, Georgia, and a visiting lecturer in pastoral theology at Reformed Theological Seminary in Atlanta. He contributes to publications including Tabletalk and the Gospel Reformation Network, and lives in the Atlanta area with his wife and their four children.

name: Kyla Gillespie
bio: Kyla Gillespie is an author, speaker, and founder of Renewed & Transformed ministries, which teaches on faith, sexuality, gender, and identity. A former professional women's hockey player from British Columbia, she tells the story of her gender transition and later detransition in her memoir 'TransFormed,' pointing readers to the sufficiency of God's Word.

name: Rebecca Pate
bio: Rebecca Pate is a Christian writer who served as Director of Marketing and Communications at Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary and has contributed articles to the seminary's Christ and Culture platform. Her writing engages faith, culture, and the Christian life from an evangelical, Baptist perspective.

name: David Garner
bio: David Garner is a Reformed theologian and professor known for his scholarly work in biblical theology and systematic doctrine. He has contributed significantly to evangelical theological discourse through his writing and teaching ministry.
education: Ph.D. in Systematic Theology, Westminster Theological Seminary

books.title: Did the Fall of Man Take Place in a Literal Space-Time Event?

known_for: Teaching systematic theology at Westminster since 2007 and writing Sons in the Son, a major study of the doctrine of adoption in Christ.
current_role: President of Westminster Theological Seminary (effective July 1, 2026); Charles Krahe Professor of Systematic Theology

faqs.a: David B. Garner is a Reformed theologian who became the fifth president of Westminster Theological Seminary in Glenside, Pennsylvania, effective July 1, 2026, succeeding Peter Lillback. He has taught systematic theology at Westminster since 2007 and previously served as its chief academic officer and vice president.

Yes. Garner is a confessional Reformed theologian in the Westminster tradition, committed to the Westminster Standards. His teaching and writing defend classic Reformed doctrine, including covenant theology and the doctrines of grace.

faqs.q: What is David Garner known for?
faqs.a: Garner is known for his book Sons in the Son: The Riches and Reach of Adoption in Christ, which develops the biblical doctrine of adoption, and for his global theological education work. He earned his PhD from Westminster and also served as a missionary educator in Eastern Europe.

name: Chris Osuh
bio: Chris Osuh is a community affairs correspondent dedicated to covering stories that matter to everyday people and communities. With a focus on bringing light to important social issues and human interest narratives, Chris works to amplify voices often unheard in mainstream media.

name: Yeganeh Torbati
bio: Yeganeh Torbati is a journalist and writer known for her reporting on religious freedom, faith communities, and social issues. Her work has appeared in major publications covering stories that intersect faith, culture, and current events.

name: Joshua Torrey
bio: Joshua Torrey is a Christian writer and curator focused on biblical theology and spiritual formation. He founded The Cripplegate, a popular Christian blog dedicated to equipping believers with sound doctrine and biblical thinking. Through his writing and content curation work, Torrey seeks to help Christians deepen their understanding of Scripture and live out their faith with integrity.

name: Don Carson
bio: D.A. Carson is a renowned biblical scholar and theologian who has shaped evangelical Christianity through decades of rigorous Scripture study and teaching. As co-founder of The Gospel Coalition and professor emeritus at Trinity Evangelical Divinity School, he has written extensively on New Testament theology, biblical interpretation, and Christian apologetics. His work emphasizes careful exegesis, doctrinal clarity, and the practical application of God's Word to contemporary faith.
affiliation: The Gospel Coalition, Trinity Evangelical Divinity School
education: Ph.D. in New Testament, University of Cambridge

books.title: The Difficult Doctrine of the Love of God
Scandalous: The Cross and Resurrection of Jesus

name: Kathleen Nielson
bio: Kathleen Nielson is a writer, speaker, and Bible teacher known for her work in Christian discipleship and women's ministry. She has served as Director of Gospel Life Women's Initiative at The Gospel Coalition and is passionate about equipping women to study and teach Scripture. Her work emphasizes the importance of women engaging deeply with God's Word and living out biblical truths in community.

books.title: Living Word, Living Church: Revitalizing Your Congregation Through Scripture
In Every Season: Finding God's Purpose in Our Trials
Proverbs: A Woman Who Fears the Lord
The Message of Ruth: Redeeming Losses

name: Amy Mantravadi
bio: Amy Mantravadi is a writer and speaker who explores faith, culture, and the Christian worldview. She engages thoughtfully with contemporary issues through a biblical lens, encouraging believers to think deeply about their convictions and live out their faith authentically in today's world.

name: Brian Smith
bio: Brian Smith is founder of The Christian Athlete and has served on staff with Athletes in Action since 2008. A Wake Forest University track and cross-country alumnus with a master's in theology and sports studies from Baylor University, he is the author of The Christian Athlete: Glorifying God in Sports and Away Game: A Christian Parent's Guide to Navigating Youth Sports, and he writes on sport and faith for The Gospel Coalition.

name: Everyday Theology Staff
bio: The Everyday Theology team is dedicated to exploring how Christian faith intersects with daily life, culture, and practice. Their collaborative approach brings together multiple perspectives to help readers think biblically about the ordinary moments and decisions they face.

name: Shawn Wright
bio: Shawn D. Wright is Professor of Church History at The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary and pastor of leadership development at Clifton Baptist Church in Louisville, Kentucky. He has written and edited books on Calvinism, ecclesiology, and the life and theology of Theodore Beza.

name: Cyril Chavis Jr.
bio: Cyril Chavis Jr. is a Reformed University Fellowship campus pastor serving at Howard University in Washington, DC, and a contributor to The Gospel Coalition. A graduate of the University of Virginia and Reformed Theological Seminary, he is the founder of Hidase Publishing and author of 'The Bible Explained,' a guide helping college students understand the essentials of the Christian faith.

name: Siobhán O'Grady
bio: Siobhán O'Grady is a journalist and foreign correspondent known for her reporting on international affairs and humanitarian issues. Her work often explores themes of faith, resilience, and human dignity in challenging global contexts.

name: Niharika Mandhana
bio: Niharika Mandhana is an Indian cricketer known for her exceptional talent and dedication to her sport. While primarily recognized for her athletic achievements, she represents the values of perseverance and excellence that resonate with faith-centered audiences seeking inspiration from contemporary role models.

name: Mark Landler
bio: Mark Landler is a seasoned foreign policy journalist and correspondent who has covered major global events and diplomatic developments for leading publications. His reporting often explores the intersection of international relations, politics, and ethics—topics relevant to Christians seeking to understand complex world affairs.

name: Vanessa Doughty
bio: Vanessa Doughty is a Christian writer and former schoolteacher who publishes the Substack Fields and Valleys, offering devotions and essays on godly contentment, identity, and everyday faithfulness. Her testimony includes being called out of New Age philosophy into faith in Christ.

name: J Oliver Conroy
bio: J. Oliver Conroy is a political culture reporter and features writer at Guardian US, covering the American right and life outside the liberal milieu. He previously spent six years as a Guardian US opinion editor, and his reported features, profiles, and reviews have also appeared in New York magazine, The New Criterion, and the Washington Examiner.

name: Ronald William DiGiacomo
bio: Ronald William DiGiacomo is a Reformed writer and ruling elder in the Presbyterian tradition who holds to the Westminster Standards. He blogs at Philosophical Theology on topics such as revelational epistemology, presuppositional apologetics, and Reformed metaphysics.

name: Kenneth Wingate
bio: Kenneth B. Wingate is an attorney in Columbia, South Carolina, and a Bible teacher at First Presbyterian Church (ARP). He is the author of books on biblical wisdom and perseverance, including 'A Father's Gift: Lessons from Proverbs,' 'Rich Grace in Poor Soil,' and 'Run with Endurance,' published with Banner of Truth.

name: Adam Loretto
bio: Adam J. Loretto is associate professor of English at Grove City College, where he directs the Writing Program and coordinates the Humanities core. He holds a PhD from the University of Pittsburgh and also serves as assistant director of the Center for Rural Ministry, writing on literacy, education, and faithful ministry.

name: Serhii Bosak
bio: Serhii Bosak is a Ukrainian Christian author and thought leader known for his work exploring faith, culture, and spiritual formation. He contributes to Christian discourse through writing and ministry in Eastern Europe and beyond.

name: Keith Bradsher
bio: Keith Bradsher is an award-winning international correspondent and economics reporter known for his investigative journalism on global trade, manufacturing, and economic policy. While not primarily a Christian content creator, his work examining economic justice issues and global inequality aligns with Christian values of stewardship and concern for workers worldwide.

books.title: High and Mighty: SUVs - The World's Most Dangerous Vehicles and How They Got That Way

name: Kevin Burrell
bio: Kevin Burrell is the co-lead pastor of StoneBridge Church Community in Charlotte, North Carolina, where his responsibilities include preaching and congregational care. He is the author of 'Considering Sparrows: What Birds Teach Us About Who We Are, Where We're Going, and the Joy of Following Jesus' and writes the devotional blog 'Ornitheology.'

name: Sue Roaf
bio: Sue Roaf is a respected Christian author and speaker known for her work exploring biblical themes and personal faith journeys. Her writings have encouraged countless readers to deepen their relationship with Christ and apply Scripture to everyday life.

name: Caleb Davis
bio: Caleb Davis is the founding and lead pastor of True Life Church in Arvada, Colorado. A regular contributor to The Gospel Coalition, 9Marks, and For The Church, he writes on the Christian life and cultural apologetics and is the author of the minibook 'When Faith Feels Dry.'

name: Sarah Hahn
bio: Sarah Hahn is a writer and speaker known for exploring themes of faith, motherhood, and spiritual growth. Her work encourages Christians to deepen their relationship with God through thoughtful reflection and biblical insight.

name: Tom Harper
bio: Tom Harper is a British author and religious commentator known for exploring the intersection of faith, history, and spirituality. His work draws on extensive research into Christian traditions and contemporary religious questions, offering thoughtful perspectives for modern believers seeking deeper understanding of their faith.

name: Walt Mueller
bio: Walt Mueller is a youth culture expert and founder of the Center for Parent/Youth Understanding, dedicated to helping Christian parents and leaders understand and effectively minister to today's adolescents. Through his writing, speaking, and research, he bridges the gap between generational perspectives and offers biblically grounded insights into the challenges facing young people.

books.title: Engaging the Soul of Youth Culture

name: Aie Balagtas See and Jason Gutierrez
bio: Aie Balagtas See is a Filipino freelance journalist who covers human rights, criminal justice, and the Philippine drug war, with reporting appearing in The New York Times and leading Philippine outlets. Jason Gutierrez is an award-winning Manila-based journalist and New York Times reporter who spent two decades as a correspondent for Agence France-Presse and served as news chief of BenarNews.

name: Marianne LeVine
bio: Marianne LeVine is a journalist and author known for her investigative reporting on religious movements and institutional accountability. Her work has appeared in major publications where she examines faith communities with both critical insight and respect for believers seeking truth.

name: Rachel Gilson
bio: Rachel Gilson is a writer and speaker who addresses faith, identity, and sexuality from a biblical perspective. Her work explores how Christian conviction intersects with cultural conversations, particularly around LGBTQ+ issues and discipleship. She is known for her thoughtful, compassionate approach to difficult theological topics.

books.title: Born Again This Way: Coming Out, Coming to Faith, and What Comes Next

name: Kevin Schaal
bio: Kevin Schaal has served as pastor of Northwest Valley Baptist Church in Glendale, Arizona, since founding it in 1987, and the church has since planted five congregations in Arizona and Mexico. A Bob Jones University graduate with an MDiv from Calvary Baptist Seminary and a DMin from International Baptist College, he has been president of the Foundations Baptist Fellowship International since 2017 and writes at Proclaim & Defend.

name: Tom Ascol
bio: Tom Ascol is a pastor, author, and advocate for Reformed theology and biblical fidelity in the local church. He is known for his work promoting Calvinism and expositional preaching within evangelical Christianity. Ascol has been influential in encouraging pastors to embrace a high view of Scripture and doctrinal precision in their ministry.

name: Jeri Choi
bio: Jeri Choi is community manager at 9Marks, the Washington, DC-based ministry devoted to building healthy churches, where she also contributes graphic design. A University of Maryland, Baltimore County graduate with an MA in Christian education, she is married to James, pastor of New Covenant Baptist Church, and they live in Maryland with their three children.

name: Jeremy Bell
bio: Jeremy Bell is a writer and content creator focused on faith, culture, and Christian living. His work explores how believers can engage thoughtfully with contemporary issues while maintaining biblical conviction.

name: Benjamin L. Mabry
bio: Benjamin L. Mabry, PhD, is an assistant professor of political science at Lincoln Memorial University and a regular contributor to American Reformer, writing on Christian social and political thought. His work also appears in First Things and The American Mind, examining how belief systems shape political action.

name: Scott McConnell
bio: Scott McConnell is a respected voice in Christian media and leadership development. He has contributed significantly to conversations around faith, culture, and discipleship within evangelical communities.

name: Zane Irwin and Shirin Hakim
bio: Zane Irwin and Shirin Hakim are content creators and communicators who engage with contemporary Christian topics and cultural conversations. Their work aims to bridge faith perspectives with modern life and relevant social discourse for thoughtful believers.

name: Hannah Beech and Daniel Berehulak
bio: Hannah Beech is an award-winning international correspondent and journalist who has covered some of the world's most critical stories, bringing important global narratives to light. Daniel Berehulak is an acclaimed photojournalist known for his powerful visual storytelling across conflict zones and humanitarian crises. Together, they represent a commitment to truth-telling and bearing witness to human experiences across the globe.

name: Laetitia Vançon
bio: Laetitia Vançon is a French Christian author and speaker known for her work in Christian discipleship and spiritual formation. She writes and ministers primarily in French-speaking contexts, offering biblical insights for contemporary believers seeking deeper faith and practical Christian living.

name: Grace Thomas
bio: Grace Thomas is a writer who serves alongside her husband at Hillview Bible Chapel in Santa Clara, California. Born and raised in the Philippines as a missionary kid and a former elementary teacher, she now writes on motherhood and applying the gospel to everyday life. Her work has appeared at The Gospel Coalition, Risen Motherhood, and Revive Our Hearts.

name: Amy Gannett
bio: Amy Gannett (MDiv, Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary) is a writer, Bible teacher, and founder of Tiny Theologians, which creates discipleship tools that teach children ages 4 to 12 the basics of the Christian faith. She is the author of Fix Your Eyes and several exegetical Bible studies, and her teaching has been featured by The Gospel Coalition, Lifeway Women, and Risen Motherhood.

name: John Currie
bio: John Currie is a respected voice in Christian ministry and leadership. With a passion for equipping believers to live out their faith authentically, Currie has contributed to numerous publications and speaking engagements within evangelical communities.

name: Davy Ellison
bio: Davy Ellison is Director of Training at the Irish Baptist College in Northern Ireland, where he teaches Biblical Hebrew and Old Testament, and serves as an elder at Antrim Baptist Church. He holds BD, MTh, and PhD degrees and is the author of several books; his writing appears at The Gospel Coalition, For The Church, and 9Marks.

name: CaReese Rials
bio: CaReese Rials is a program specialist and freelance writer from Chicago, Illinois. Her writing on simplicity, faith, and intentional living has appeared in RELEVANT and Lookout Magazine, including RELEVANT's guide to living with less, which explores why many Christians are rejecting the 'gospel of more' in favor of simpler, more generous lives.

name: Alistair MacDonald
bio: Alistair MacDonald is a Scottish minister and author known for his thoughtful approach to Christian faith and pastoral ministry. His writings reflect a deep commitment to biblical theology and the practical application of Scripture in contemporary church life.

name: Erica Barthalow
bio: Erica Barthalow is an author, blogger, and writing coach who helps people wrestle well with faith when it is difficult. A former missionary to India and a pastor's wife, she writes on doubt and prayer and is the author of 'Holy Doubt' and 'Praying is (not) Hard.' She and her family live in central Iowa.

name: R. Andrew Compton
bio: R. Andrew Compton is a pastor and Christian author devoted to expository preaching and biblical teaching. He writes thoughtfully about Scripture and pastoral ministry for a Protestant evangelical audience. Compton is known for his commitment to helping churches understand and apply God's Word.

name: Justin Dillehay
bio: Justin Dillehay is a pastor and Christian communicator dedicated to helping believers grow in their faith and understanding of Scripture. He is known for his engaging teaching style that makes biblical truths accessible and applicable to everyday Christian life.

name: Joshua Parcha
bio: Joshua Parcha is a writer and associate professor of communication at Penn State Hazleton, where his academic work focuses on business and organizational communication. He also writes for evangelical outlets, contributing articles on the Christian life and cultural engagement to American Reformer, For The Church, and Baptist Press.

name: Jill E. McCormick
bio: Jill E. McCormick is a Christian writer, speaker, and church communications director who connects women to Jesus through 'common-sense grace.' She hosts the Grace In Real Life podcast and writes at jillemccormick.com, with work featured in RELEVANT and For Every Mom, and speaks at women's retreats and mom's groups.

name: Nazaneen Ghaffar
bio: Nazaneen Ghaffar is a journalist and media professional known for her work in broadcast news and digital storytelling. While her primary career has focused on journalism and communications, she brings a thoughtful perspective to contemporary cultural conversations.

name: Jon Coombs
bio: Jon Coombs is lead pastor of Mooroolbark Baptist Church in Melbourne, Australia, and has served in ministry for two decades across churches, schools, and mission agencies, including years as a youth and associate pastor. He holds an MDiv from the Melbourne School of Theology and writes regularly on discipleship, pastoral care, and everyday faith at joncoombs.com, The Gospel Coalition Australia, and Rooted Ministry.

name: Simon van Bruchem
bio: Simon van Bruchem is a Christian author and speaker known for his contributions to faith-based content and theological reflection. His work engages contemporary Christian audiences with thoughtful perspectives on spiritual growth and biblical understanding.

name: Jacob Percy
bio: Jacob Percy (PhD, The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary) serves as Vice President of Communications at Southern Seminary and Boyce College, where he leads institutional messaging and content strategy. Trained in systematic theology, he contributes articles for Baptist Press and Southern Equip.

name: Jessica Murray
bio: Jessica Murray is a social affairs correspondent who reports on issues affecting communities and society. Her work examines social trends, policy impacts, and human interest stories that shape our world.

name: Ryan Dubé
bio: Ryan Dubé is a Wall Street Journal reporter covering Latin America, based in Lima, Peru. Originally from Alberta, Canada, he first came to Peru as an exchange student, later returning after completing a degree in Latin American studies and anthropology. He covers economics, business, and politics across the region, with earlier work appearing in The Globe and Mail and BNamericas.

name: Lane Tipton
bio: Lane Tipton is a Reformed theologian and professor known for his work in systematic theology and biblical exegesis. He has contributed significantly to evangelical and Reformed discussions on doctrine, particularly regarding Christology, the covenant, and biblical hermeneutics. His teaching and writing aim to help Christians understand and live out biblical truth with theological depth.

name: Dan Olinger
bio: Dan Olinger is a writer and editor known for his work in Christian publishing and content creation. He has contributed to various evangelical publications and is recognized for his thoughtful approach to contemporary Christian issues.

name: Josh Irby
bio: Josh Irby is a pastor and Christian writer known for his thoughtful exploration of Scripture and practical Christian living. He engages readers with biblical insights and contemporary applications designed to deepen faith and discipleship.

name: Adam Goldman
bio: Adam Goldman is a journalist and reporter known for his investigative work covering national security, law enforcement, and intelligence matters. While not primarily known as a Christian author, his reporting has touched on issues of faith, ethics, and institutional accountability that resonate with thoughtful Christian readers.

name: Dustin Volz and Michael Schwirtz
bio: Dustin Volz is a cybersecurity and national security reporter, while Michael Schwirtz is an investigative journalist. Together and separately, they have covered complex geopolitical and security issues with rigorous reporting.

name: Scott W. Kay
bio: Scott W. Kay is a writer and Christian thinker who explores themes of faith, culture, and Christian worldview. His work engages contemporary issues through a theological lens, offering thoughtful perspective for believers navigating modern culture.

name: Simona Gorton
bio: Simona Gorton is a Christian author who formerly served as International Operations Manager of 9Marks. She has written youth and adult biographies of Elaine Townsend as well as 'Mothering Against Futility: Balancing Meaning and Mundanity in the Fear of the Lord.' She lives with her husband and three children in Pennsylvania.

name: Kadin Christian
bio: Kadin Christian is a content creator and Christian communicator dedicated to helping believers engage with faith in meaningful ways. Through writing and digital content, he explores topics relevant to modern Christian living and spiritual growth.

name: Stephen Mattson
bio: Stephen Mattson is a writer and journalist who explores the intersection of faith, politics, and social justice from an evangelical perspective. His work challenges Christians to engage thoughtfully with contemporary issues while remaining rooted in biblical values and compassion.

books.title: The Millennial Mosaic: Restoring Hope and Purpose to a Generation

name: Sadie Maples
bio: Sadie Maples is the 2026 Gene Habecker Fellow at Christianity Today, where she writes on Christian living, spiritual formation, and contemporary culture. Her essays include reflections on why mindfulness alone cannot satisfy, the church's calling amid America's 250th anniversary, and how Christ's message bridges the country's deepest social divides.

name: Arthur Gonçalves
bio: Arthur Gonçalves is founding pastor of Restoration Church of Sanford in Sanford, Florida, planted in 2022. He serves as regional chapter leader for The Gospel Coalition Orlando and founded Shepherd's Care Ministry, and he writes for The Gospel Coalition on pastoral friendship, local church networks, and gospel partnership.

name: Peter Rosenberger
bio: Peter Rosenberger is a Christian author, radio host, and caregiver advocate who has devoted his ministry to supporting those navigating the complexities of chronic illness and caregiving. Through his writing, broadcasting, and speaking engagements, he encourages believers to find hope and purpose amid life's most difficult circumstances.

books.title: A Place Called Home: Finding Hope When Chronic Illness Strikes

name: Erin Ford
bio: Erin Ford is a speaker and author passionate about helping women navigate faith, relationships, and personal growth from a biblical perspective. Through her writing and speaking engagements, she encourages believers to deepen their walk with Christ and find authentic community.

name: Cal Crucis
bio: Cal Crucis is a Reformed, Anglican-minded Christian writer whose essays on theology, church history, and Christian political thought appear at American Reformer, the Theopolis Institute, and The North American Anglican. Writing under a pen name, he draws on patristics, philosophy, and early modern British history to explore faithful Christian politics.

name: Luis Ferré-Sadurní and Leo Sands
bio: Luis Ferré-Sadurní and Leo Sands are journalists and writers who have contributed reporting and analysis to major publications. Their work often explores social, political, and cultural issues with careful research and journalistic integrity.

name: Frances Robles
bio: Frances Robles is a journalist and author known for her investigative reporting on social justice issues and human interest stories. Her work, often grounded in compassion and truth-telling, has appeared in major publications and reflects a commitment to amplifying marginalized voices.

name: Murungi Igweta
bio: Murungi Igweta is the pastor of Trinity Baptist Church in the Donholm area of Nairobi, Kenya, where he has ministered since 2010. A Reformed Baptist trained through Reformed Baptist Seminary, he writes and teaches on prayer, the church, and the Christian life, contributing to Tabletalk magazine and the Reformed Baptist Network.

name: Kirsten Black
bio: Kirsten Black serves as director of women's support for Acts 29, the church-planting network. In 2009 she and her husband, Vince, moved to Fort Collins, Colorado, to plant The Town Church. She holds a master's degree in counseling from Covenant Theological Seminary and writes for The Gospel Coalition on women's ministry and the Christian life.

name: Matt Recker
bio: Matt Recker is a Bible teacher and content creator focused on helping Christians understand Scripture with depth and clarity. Through his teaching ministry, he equips believers to study God's Word more effectively and apply biblical truths to their daily lives.

name: James Anderson
bio: James Anderson is a Reformed theologian and author known for his thoughtful engagement with Christian doctrine and apologetics. His work explores the intersection of biblical theology, philosophy, and contemporary faith questions for evangelical audiences.

name: Kathleen Allen
bio: Kathleen Allen is a Christian author and speaker dedicated to helping believers discover deeper faith and spiritual growth. Her work focuses on biblical wisdom and practical Christian living for modern audiences.

name: Emma Bubola
bio: Emma Bubola is a journalist and writer who has contributed to major publications covering faith, culture, and human interest stories. Her reporting often explores the intersection of spirituality, community, and contemporary life with thoughtful, narrative-driven journalism.

name: Isayen Herrera and Tibisay Romero
bio: Isayen Herrera and Tibisay Romero are Christian content creators and writers dedicated to sharing faith-based insights with Spanish-speaking and bilingual audiences. Through their collaborative work, they seek to inspire and encourage believers in their spiritual journeys.

name: Jacob Leeming
bio: Jacob Leeming is a writer and theology student who studied at Master's College and Seminary in Peterborough, Ontario. He contributes to The Gospel Coalition Canada, writing on theology and the Christian life for a Canadian evangelical readership.

name: Michael Grayston
bio: Michael Grayston (EdD) is the Discipleship and Groups Pastor at LifeFamily, with prior service as a location pastor at Next Level Church and as Next Steps and Multisite Pastor at Centerpointe Church. He writes on spiritual formation and small-group discipleship, drawing on more than a decade in healthcare leadership before entering full-time ministry.

name: Zach Carter
bio: Zach Carter is the lead pastor of Redeemer Church in Huntsville, Alabama, and serves as director of communication and training for the Great Commission Collective. A convert from Mormonism, he is the editor of 'Cloud of Witnesses: A Treasury of Prayers and Petitions Through the Ages' and writes for The Gospel Coalition on church history and biblical theology.

name: George Grant
bio: George Grant is a prolific Christian author, educator, and cultural commentator known for his thoughtful exploration of faith, history, and public policy. His work bridges classical Christian thought with contemporary social issues, offering readers a distinctly Reformed perspective on culture and stewardship.
education: Studied at Hillsdale College and Reformed Theological Seminary

books.title: The Micah Mandate: Balancing the Christian Life
Carry a Big Stick: The Uncommon Heroism of Theodore Roosevelt
The Blood of the Moon: The Dedication of the Thomas Jefferson Memorial
Sorrow and Blood: Suffering in the Christian Life
The Patriot's Handbook: A Cyclopedia of American Quotations

name: Zac Workun
bio: Zac Workun is a thoughtful voice in Christian media and content creation, known for his work exploring faith, culture, and discipleship. His writing and speaking engage contemporary audiences with biblical insight and practical wisdom.

name: Ben White
bio: Ben White is a writer and speaker known for his work in Christian apologetics and cultural commentary. He has contributed to various Christian publications and platforms, engaging thoughtfully with contemporary issues from a Christian worldview perspective.

name: Fonie Mitsopoulou
bio: Fonie Mitsopoulou is a Christian author and speaker who writes on faith, spirituality, and personal transformation. Her work encourages believers to deepen their relationship with God through practical wisdom and biblical insight.

name: Dalya Alberge
bio: Dalya Alberge is a distinguished arts and cultural correspondent known for her insightful reporting on faith, heritage, and the arts. Her work bridges Christian perspectives with cultural commentary, exploring how faith intersects with society, tradition, and creative expression.

name: Tibisay Romero
bio: Tibisay Romero is a Venezuelan journalist and broadcaster from Carabobo state who has covered her country's political and economic turmoil for years, reporting for The New York Times, Reuters, and other international outlets. Her recent work includes firsthand accounts of Venezuelan migrants detained in Salvadoran prisons.

name: Luis Ferré-Sadurní and Genevieve Glatsky
bio: Luis Ferré-Sadurní and Genevieve Glatsky are journalists who have reported on significant social and political issues affecting communities across the United States. Their investigative work often examines systemic challenges and human stories that reflect broader concerns about justice and community welfare.

name: Corinne Carver
bio: Corinne Carver is a writer and cross-cultural worker originally from Portland, Oregon, who has served in ministry in the Dominican Republic. She writes on faith, ministry, and life overseas for Velvet Ashes, a community for Christian women serving in missions around the world.

name: Bruce McKanna
bio: Bruce McKanna is senior pastor of the Evangelical Free Church of Mt. Morris, Illinois. He holds an MDiv from Trinity Evangelical Divinity School, and his writing on Scripture, citizenship, and the Christian life appears at The Gospel Coalition and the EFCA blog, where he also contributes book reviews.
